The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) only granted a concession regarding it out of necessity during campaigns and in the absence of women, when there was a severe need for a woman. So whoever grants a concession regarding it while at home, with women abundant and ordinary marriage possible, has transgressed, and Allah does not love transgressors.

If it is said: what will you do with what Muslim transmitted in his Sahih from the hadith of Jabir and Salamah ibn al-Akwa', who both said: "The herald of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us and said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has permitted you to enjoy [mut'ah] (meaning: the mut'ah of women)."

It is said: this was at the time of the Conquest, before the prohibition. Then he prohibited it after that, as evidenced by what Muslim transmitted in his Sahih from Salamah ibn al-Akwa', who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) granted us a concession regarding mut'ah for three days in the year of Awtas, then he forbade it."

(The year of Awtas) and (the year of the Conquest) are one and the same, because the expedition of Awtas is connected to the Conquest of Mecca.

If it is said: what will you do with what Muslim transmitted in his Sahih from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "We used to enjoy a handful of dates and flour for days during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr, until 'Umar forbade it, concerning the case of 'Amr ibn Hurayth," and with what is established from 'Umar that he said: "There were two mut'ahs during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I forbid them: the mut'ah of women and the mut'ah of Hajj"? (p-1192)

It is said: people are of two groups on this matter.

One group says: 'Umar is the one who prohibited it and forbade it. The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded following what the Rightly-Guided Caliphs had established. This group did not regard the hadith of Sabrah ibn Ma'bad concerning the prohibition of mut'ah in the year of the Conquest as authentic, because it comes through 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Rabi' ibn Sabrah, from his father, from his grandfather. Ibn Ma'in has spoken about it. Al-Bukhari did not choose to include its hadith in his Sahih despite the great need for it and its being a foundational principle of Islam. Had it been authentic in his view, he would not have refrained from including it or from citing it. They said: had the hadith of Sabrah been authentic, it would not have been unknown to Ibn Mas'ud, so that he would narrate that they did it and argue from the verse.

They also said: had it been authentic, 'Umar would not have said: "It was during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and I forbid it and punish for it," but rather he would have said: "He (ﷺ) prohibited it and forbade it."

They said: had it been authentic, it would not have been practised during the time of al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr), which was truly the era of the caliphate of prophethood.

The second group: they considered the hadith of Sabrah to be authentic, and even if it were not authentic, the hadith of Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) is authentic: "that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the mut'ah of women." (p-1193)

Therefore, the hadith of Jabir must be understood as meaning that the one who reported its practice had not received word of the prohibition, and it had not become widely known until the time of 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him). When people engaged in it during his time, it became apparent and widely known. By this the hadiths concerning it are reconciled. And Allah is the Granter of success. [End of quotation.]

This, and those who took the verse as explaining the ruling on marriage said: what is meant by His saying, ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree upon﴾ etc., is that if the dower has been fixed at a specific amount, there is no harm in her reducing some of the dower for him, or releasing him from it entirely, by mutual consent, as has already been mentioned. This is like His saying: ﴿And if they give you willingly a part of it, then consume it with satisfaction and pleasure﴾ [al-Nisa': 4] [al-Nisa': 4], and His saying: ﴿Unless they forgo, or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgoes﴾ [al-Baqarah: 237] [al-Baqarah: 237, part of verse 237].

Al-Tabari transmitted from al-Hadrami that men used to lend the dower, then perhaps one of them would fall into hardship, so Allah said: ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree upon after the obligation﴾ etc.

That is: if she gives you a part of it, it is lawful for you.

As for those who took the verse as explaining mut'ah, they said: what is meant by the negation of blame is that when the term of the mut'ah has ended, the man has no claim whatsoever over the woman. If he says to her: "Increase the days and I will increase the payment," the woman has the choice: if she wishes she does it, and if she wishes she does not. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree upon after the obligation﴾, i.e., after the amount previously mentioned of the payment and the term. This was related by al-Razi.

Al-Suddi said: if he wishes, he may satisfy her after the initial obligation, meaning the payment he gave her for his enjoyment of her before the end of the term between them. He says: "I will enjoy you again for such and such," and if he wishes he may add to it before she completes her waiting period (istibra') on the day the term ends. This is His saying: ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree upon after the obligation﴾.

Al-Suddi said: once the term has ended, there is no claim upon her; she is free from him, and she must observe the waiting period for what is in her womb. There is no inheritance between them, so neither inherits from the other.

(p-1194) Al-Tabari said: the more correct of the two interpretations is the first, because the proof of Allah's prohibition of mut'ah on the tongue of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is established. [End of quotation.]

Al-Mahayimi said: Then He (exalted) pointed to the marriage of what is permitted out of necessity, such as marriage by mut'ah. But this is a continuing necessity which does not end with the abundance of Muslims. So He said:

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:
﴿And whoever among you cannot afford sufficient means to marry free, believing women, then let him marry from what your right hands possess of your believing young women. And Allah knows best your faith; you are of one another. So marry them with the permission of their people and give them their bridal gifts according to what is reasonable, as chaste women, not fornicators nor those who take secret lovers. And when they become chaste through marriage, if they commit immorality, they shall receive half the punishment for free women. That is for whoever among you fears sin, but to be patient is better for you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [25]

﴿And whoever among you cannot afford﴾ i.e., is unable, ﴿among you﴾, O free men, unlike slaves, ﴿sufficient means﴾, i.e., wealth by which he is able ﴿to marry free women﴾, i.e., chaste free women, unlike prostitutes, for they are not regarded, ﴿believing﴾, since disbelievers are not regarded. ﴿then let him marry from what your right hands possess﴾, i.e., he may marry some of what the right hands of your brothers possess, ﴿of your young women﴾, i.e., your female slaves in bondage, ﴿believing﴾, not from the People of the Book; for he cannot bear the shame of disbelief together with the shame of slavery. It is derived from the context of this verse that Allah, Exalted, stipulated three conditions for marrying slave women: two of them concern the one who marries, and the third concerns the woman who is married.

As for the two concerning the one who marries: the first is that he is unable to afford the bridal gift required for marrying a free believing woman, and this is the meaning of His words: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford sufficient means to marry free, believing women﴾ (p-1195). Thus, the inability to afford sufficient means is an expression for lacking what one would marry a free woman with. If it is said: a man who is able to marry a slave woman is able to marry a poor free woman, so whence this disparity? We say: it was customary that the bridal gifts and maintenance of slave women be lighter, since they were occupied with serving their masters, and on this assumption the disparity becomes apparent.

As for the second condition, it is the one mentioned at the end of the verse, His words: ﴿That is for whoever among you fears sin﴾, i.e., fornication, by reason of his severe unmarried state.

As for the third condition, which is considered regarding the woman being married: that the slave woman be a believer, not a disbeliever. For if the slave woman is a disbeliever, she is deficient in two respects: slavery and disbelief. And there is no doubt that the child follows the mother in freedom and slavery; in that case the child would be born a slave under the ownership of a disbeliever, so there would be a deficiency of slavery and a deficiency of being owned by a disbeliever. What we have mentioned is what corresponds to the meaning of the verse, and whatever else is said involves an artificiality that the wording of the verse does not support.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you say: why is marrying a slave woman inferior to marrying a free woman? I say: because of what it entails of the child following the mother in slavery, of the master's right being established over her and in her service, and because she is debased, degraded, going out and coming in; all of that is a deficiency that reflects upon the one who marries, and a humiliation, while honor is one of the attributes of the believers. More will come on this at His words: ﴿But to be patient is better for you﴾.

His words: ﴿And Allah knows best your faith﴾ are an indication that it is not required to scrutinize their inner states; rather, the outward appearance of their faith suffices. That is: suffice yourselves with the outward appearance of faith, for He, Exalted, is the Knower of hidden things and of the differences among you in faith, so many a slave woman may surpass a free woman in it.

His words: ﴿you are of one another﴾ are another parenthetical remark, brought to put them at ease about marrying slave women at that time, i.e., you and your slaves are kindred: your lineage traces back to Adam, and your religion is Islam.

﴿So marry them with the permission of their people﴾, i.e., their masters, not independently; this is because their usufruct belongs to them, and it is not permissible for anyone else to benefit from any of it except with the permission of its owner.

﴿And give them﴾, i.e., bestow upon them, ﴿their bridal gifts﴾, i.e., their dowries, ﴿according to what is reasonable﴾, i.e., without delay, harm, or compelling them to demand it.

Imam Malik took this as evidence that they have the better right to their dowries, and that the master has no right to it.

(p-1196) The majority held that the dowry belongs to the master, and that He attributed it to them only because payment to them is payment to their master, since they are his property.

﴿As chaste women﴾ is a circumstantial clause of the object of ﴿So marry them﴾, i.e., while they are chaste from fornication. ﴿Not fornicators﴾ is an emphasizing circumstantial clause, i.e., not committing fornication with every man who calls them. ﴿Nor those who take secret lovers﴾, i.e., boyfriends with whom they are specially involved in fornication.

Abu Zayd said: al-akhdan are companions in immorality, and the singular is khidn and khudayn.

Al-Raghib said: most of this usage concerns one who keeps company out of carnal desire.

Among the subtleties of His words ﴿as chaste women﴾ etc. occurring right after His words ﴿and give them their bridal gifts﴾ is the implication that if they were one of these two (fornicators or those with secret lovers), you would have the right to contest the payment of their dowries, so that they would ransom their souls.

﴿And when they become chaste﴾, i.e., by marriage. It was also read in the active voice, i.e., when they guard their chastity or their husbands. ﴿If they commit immorality﴾, i.e., they do an immorality, which is fornication, ﴿they shall receive﴾, i.e., there is established against them by the Law, ﴿half the punishment for free women﴾, i.e., for free women, ﴿of the punishment﴾, i.e., of the prescribed penalty, which is one hundred lashes, so half of it is fifty lashes, not stoning.

Al-Mahayimi said: because they are among those who are debased, so excessive severity in deterrence is of no benefit to them.

* *

Note:
Ibn Kathir said: The position of the majority is that if a slave woman commits fornication, she receives fifty lashes, whether she is Muslim or non-Muslim, married or a virgin. Yet the implication of the verse requires that there is no prescribed penalty for a slave woman who commits fornication who is not chaste, and their answers to this differ.

As for the majority, they said: there is no doubt that the explicit text takes precedence over the implicit, and general hadiths have come concerning the enforcement of the prescribed penalty upon slave women, so we give them precedence over the implication of the verse.

Among these is what Muslim related in his Sahih, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he gave a sermon and said: O people! Enforce the prescribed penalty upon your slaves, whether they are chaste or not, for a slave woman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ committed fornication, and he commanded me to lash her; but she had recently given birth, so I feared that if I lashed her I would kill her (p-1197). I mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: You did well; leave her until she recovers.

In the narration of Abdullah ibn Ahmad from someone other than his father: "When she recovers from her postpartum bleeding, lash her fifty times."

From Abu Hurayrah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "If the slave woman of one of you commits fornication and her fornication is clear, let him inflict the prescribed penalty on her and not reproach her. Then if she commits it a second time, let him inflict the prescribed penalty on her and not reproach her. Then if she commits it a third time and her fornication is clear, let him sell her even for a rope of hair."

In Muslim's version: "If she commits it three times, then let him sell her in the fourth."

Malik related from Abdullah ibn Ayyash al-Makhzumi, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab commanded me, along with a group of young men from Quraysh, and we lashed some of the slave girls of the governorship fifty lashes each for fornication.

The second answer: the answer of those who held that if a slave woman commits fornication and is not chaste, there is no prescribed penalty upon her, and she is only disciplined by beating. This is related from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, and Tawus, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam, and Dawud ibn Ali al-Zahiri (in one report from him) also held it, and their basis is the implication of the verse, which is one of the implications of a condition; it is authoritative according to most of them, so it takes precedence over the general in their view.

And the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and Zayd ibn Khalid: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about a slave woman who commits fornication and is not chaste. He said: If she commits fornication, lash her; then if she commits it again, lash her; then if she commits it again, sell her even for a braid of hair." Ibn Shihab said: "I do not know whether it was after the third or the fourth." Both of them are narrated in the two Sahihs.

In Muslim's version, Ibn Shihab said: "The dafir is the rope." They said: no number is specified in it as is specified for the chaste woman, and as the Qur'an specified it as half of what is upon free women. So it is necessary to reconcile the verse and the hadith in this manner, and Allah knows best.

Even clearer than that is what Sa'id ibn Mansur related from Ibn Abbas, traced to the Prophet: "There is no prescribed penalty upon a slave woman until she is made chaste, meaning married. When she is made chaste by marriage, then upon her is half of what is upon free women."

Ibn Khuzaymah related it also traced to the Prophet and said: its tracing to the Prophet is an error; it is only the statement of Ibn Abbas. Al-Bayhaqi related it likewise and said the same as Ibn Khuzaymah.

They said: the hadith of Ali and Umar are cases of specific incidents, and the hadith of Abu Hurayrah has several answers:

First: that it is to be understood as referring to a married slave woman, in order to reconcile it with this hadith.

Second: that the word "prescribed penalty" in his words "let him inflict the prescribed penalty upon her" was inserted by some narrators, as evidenced by:

The third answer: that this is from the hadith of two Companions, and that is from the narration of Abu Hurayrah alone, and what comes from two is more deserving of precedence than what comes from one.

Also, al-Nasa'i related it with a chain meeting Muslim's conditions, from the hadith of Abbad ibn Tamim from his paternal uncle, who had witnessed Badr: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: If the slave woman commits fornication, lash her; then if she commits it again, lash her; then if she commits it again, lash her; then if she commits it again, sell her even for a braid of hair."

The fourth: it is not unlikely that some narrator applied the word "prescribed penalty" in the hadith to "lashing", because since it was lashing he believed it to be a prescribed penalty; or he applied the word "prescribed penalty" to discipline, just as "prescribed penalty" was applied to striking one who committed fornication among the sick with a palm-spathe containing one hundred shoots, and to lashing one who committed fornication with his wife's slave girl one hundred times when she permitted him to do so. That is only discretionary punishment and discipline according to those who hold it, such as Ahmad and others among the early scholars. The true prescribed penalty is the lashing of a virgin one hundred times and the stoning of a married person. End of quote.

He has a comprehensive continuation.

Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in Zad al-Ma'ad: As for the slave woman who commits fornication and is not chaste, she is subject to the prescribed penalty. As for His words, Exalted, concerning slave women: ﴿And when they become chaste, if they commit immorality, they shall receive half the punishment for free women﴾, it is explicit that her prescribed penalty after marriage is half the prescribed penalty for a free woman in lashes. As for before marriage, she is ordered to be lashed; and regarding this prescribed penalty there are two views:

(p-1199) One of them: that it is the prescribed penalty, but the situation differs before marriage and after it, for the master may enforce it before marriage, whereas after marriage only the Imam enforces it.

The second view: that her lashing before becoming chaste is discretionary punishment, not a prescribed penalty. This does not invalidate what Muslim related in his Sahih from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, traced to the Prophet: "If the slave woman of one of you commits fornication, let him lash her and not reproach her three times. If she returns in the fourth, let him lash her and sell her even for a braid of hair." In another wording: "Let him strike her with the Book of Allah."

Also in his Sahih, from the hadith of Ali, may Allah ennoble his face, that he said: "O people! Enforce the prescribed penalty upon your slaves, whether they are chaste or not, for a slave woman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ committed fornication, and he commanded me to lash her..." the hadith.

The word "prescribed penalty" in the speech of the Lawgiver includes discretionary punishment, as in his saying ﷺ: "No one shall be struck more than ten lashes except for one of the prescribed penalties of Allah, Exalted."

Discretionary punishment exceeding ten lashes in kind and quantity has been established in numerous instances, and its abrogation has not been established, and the Ummah has not agreed against it.

In any case, her state after becoming chaste must differ from her state before it, otherwise the restriction would have no benefit.

Either it is said that before becoming chaste there is no prescribed penalty upon her, but the authentic Sunnah nullifies this; or it is said that her prescribed penalty before becoming chaste is that of a free woman and after it is half of that, which is clearly false and contrary to the principles and foundations of the Law; or it is said that her prescribed penalty before becoming chaste is discretionary punishment and after it a prescribed penalty, and this is stronger; or it is said that the difference between the two states (p-1200) lies in the enforcement of the prescribed penalty, not its amount, and that in one state it belongs to the master and in the other to the Imam, and this is the closest of what is said.

It may be said: the explicit mention of halving (the punishment) after ihsan (chastity/marriage status) is so that no one would imagine that with ihsan the halving disappears and her punishment becomes that of a free woman, just as the flogging for an unmarried (virgin) woman is removed by ihsan and it transfers to stoning. Thus it remains halved in its most complete state, which is ihsan, as an alert that if it is retained for her in that state, then before ihsan it is all the more fitting and proper. And Allah knows best.

﴿That﴾, i.e., the permission to marry female slaves, is ﴿for him who fears falling into sin﴾, i.e., the hardship of guarding oneself against fornication, ﴿among you﴾, O free men, ﴿but that you endure patiently﴾ the bearing of that hardship, abstaining from marrying them, ﴿is better for you﴾ than marrying them. Even though the concession was mentioned, this is because marrying them exposes the child to slavery. ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Whichever free man marries a slave woman has enslaved half of himself." Also, the right of the master over her is stronger, so she is not exclusively available to the husband as free women are. Also, the master can make use of her however he wishes, whether traveling or at home, and sell her to both the present and the absent. In this there is an unmatched disruption of the husband's situation and that of his children. Also, she is degraded, belittled, frequently going out and coming in, and all of this is humiliation and abasement that spreads to the one who marries her, whereas honor is what befits the believers. Also, her dowry belongs to her master, so she cannot enjoy it or give it to the husband, and thus the affairs of the household are not put in order. So Abu al-Su'ud has written. And it has been said:

"When a man's household has no free woman to manage it, the interests of his home are lost."

In al-Iklil it is said: the verse indicates the disliking (karahah) of marrying a slave woman when the conditions are met, by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But that you be patient is better for you; and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

(p-1201) The interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

﴿Allah desires to make clear to you and to guide you to the ways of those before you, and to turn to you in forgiveness. And Allah is Knowing, Wise.﴾ [26]

﴿Allah desires﴾ means: in forbidding what He has forbidden of women, and permitting what He has permitted of them, under the stated conditions. ﴿to make clear to you﴾ means: His laws. ﴿and to guide you to the ways of those before you﴾ means: to direct you to the practices of those who came before you among the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) in forbidding what He forbade, so that you may follow them in adhering to the laws He loves and approves.

The verse indicates that everything He has shown to be forbidden to us of women in the preceding verses was likewise the ruling in the earlier religious community (millah).

I have read in the Book of the Priests, Leviticus (Sifr al-Ahbar al-Lawiyyin), of the Torah (al-Tawrah), in (Chapter Eighteen), what confirms this, apart from what God, exalted is He, has lifted from us of that which entails hardship.

﴿and to turn to you in forgiveness﴾ means: He will overlook what you did in the time of ignorance (jahiliyyah), or He will bring you back from the disobedience you were engaged in to obedience to Him. ﴿And Allah is Knowing﴾ means: regarding what He has legislated for you of rulings. ﴿Wise﴾ means: in all His decrees He observes wisdom.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

﴿And Allah desires to accept your repentance, while those who follow desires want you to deviate with a great deviation﴾ [27]

﴿And Allah desires to accept your repentance﴾ i.e., from sins (al-ma'athim) and what is forbidden (al-mahaarim); that is, He brings you out of everything He dislikes to what He loves and is pleased with. In this is an explanation of the perfect benefit of what Allah Exalted desires, and the perfect harm of what the wicked (al-fajara) desire, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And those who follow desires desire﴾, i.e., what the Law has forbidden, and they are the fornicators (al-zunat), ﴿that you deviate﴾ from the truth through disobedience, ﴿with a great deviation﴾, meaning by your committing what Allah has forbidden to you.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 4, verse 28:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Allah desires to lighten [the burden] for you, and man was created weak﴾ [28]

﴿Allah desires to lighten [the burden] for you﴾ That is: in His laws, His commands, His prohibitions, and what He decrees for you. For this reason He permitted marrying slave women under its conditions. A parallel to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185] [al-Baqarah: part of verse 185], and His saying: ﴿And He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty﴾ [al-Hajj: 78] [al-Hajj: 78].

﴿And man was created weak﴾ That is: unable to repel the impulses of his desires. Thus lightening [the burden] is fitting for him, because of the weakness of his resolve and determination and his weakness in himself. So the sentence is a parenthetical concluding statement (i'tiraD tadhyili), brought to affirm what precedes it of lightening in the rulings of the Sharia.

In al-Iklil, Tawus said: "weak" means: in the matter of women, he cannot be patient regarding them. WakI' said: his intellect departs from him in their presence. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated both. In this there is a basis for what the physicians mention regarding the benefits of intercourse and the harms of abstaining from it.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 4, verse 29:

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿O you who have believed, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly, except in the case of trade by mutual consent. And do not kill yourselves. Indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you.﴾ [29]

﴿O you who have believed, do not consume your wealth among yourselves﴾, meaning: let none of you consume the wealth of another, ﴿unjustly﴾, meaning: what the Shari'ah has not permitted, such as usury (riba), gambling (qimar), bribery (rishwah), usurpation (ghasb), theft (sariqah), betrayal of trust (khiyanah), and what is similar to these of the various kinds of stratagems (hiyal). (p-1203)

﴿except that it be trade﴾, meaning: a pure exchange, such as sale (bay'), ﴿by mutual consent from among you﴾, regarding the concession (muhabah) on the part of the one who takes and the one from whom it is taken. It is recited as "tijaratun" (تِجارَةٌ) in the nominative, on the basis that "kana" (كانَ) is complete (tammah), and in the accusative, on the basis that it is incomplete (naqisah). The implied meaning is: "except that the transaction, or the trade, or the wealth be trade."

Al-Suyuti said in "al-Iklil": The verse contains the prohibition of consuming wrongful wealth without a lawful basis, and the permissibility of trade and profit therein, and that its condition is mutual consent. From here al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, derived the requirement of offer and acceptance (ijab wa qabul) verbally, because mutual consent is an inward matter, so there must be evidence for it. Whoever does not stipulate these two may also cite it when consent is present, end of quote.

That is, because statements indicate mutual consent, so too actions indicate it in some situations with certainty, and therefore the sale by exchange of goods without words (bay' al-mu'atah) is valid in every case.

In "al-Rawdah al-Nadiyyah": The true nature of mutual consent is known only to God, the Exalted, and what is meant here is its sign, such as offer and acceptance, and such as the exchange of goods (ta'ati) according to the one who holds this view. This is the position of the people of knowledge, because no text has come that indicates what some of them have required, namely specific wordings, and that a sale is not permissible without them. Nor does what has been reported in some narrations, such as "I have sold to you and you have bought from me," benefit them, for we do not deny that a sale is valid by that, but the dispute is over whether it is valid only by it, and nothing has come concerning that. God the Exalted has said: ﴿trade by mutual consent﴾, which indicates that mere mutual consent is the criterion, and it must be indicated by a word, a gesture, or writing, by whatever wording occurs, in whatever form it is, and by whatever gesture conveys it, end of quote.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not kill yourselves. Indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you﴾, it has two possible meanings:

The first: the meaning is "do not kill those of your own kind from among the believers, for they are all like a single soul." The expression of them as "souls" is for emphasis in forbidding the killing of them, by depicting it in the form of something that a rational person would hardly do.

The second: the prohibition of a person killing himself. This verse was used as evidence by Amr ibn al-As regarding the question of tayammum (dry ablution) because of cold, and the Prophet (ﷺ) approved of his argument, as related by Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud. The wording of Ahmad is:

From Amr ibn al-As, that he said: "When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent him in the year of Dhat al-Salasil, he said: I had a wet dream on a night of extreme cold, and I feared that if I bathed I would perish, so I performed tayammum, then led my companions in the dawn prayer. He said: When we came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), I mentioned that to him, and he said: O Amr, you led your companions in prayer while you were in a state of major impurity (junub)? I said: Yes, O Messenger of God, I had a wet dream on a night of extreme cold, and I feared that if I bathed I would perish, and I remembered the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And do not kill yourselves. Indeed, Allah is ever Merciful to you﴾. So I performed tayammum and then prayed. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) laughed and said nothing." Abu Dawud also related it in this manner.

Ibn Kathir said: This, that is, the second meaning, God knows best, is more fitting to the truth. Reports have abounded concerning the prohibition of a person killing himself and the threat of punishment for it.

Al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and the authors of the Sunan and others related from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever throws himself from a mountain and kills himself, he will be in the fire of Hell, throwing himself therein, abiding eternally therein forever. Whoever drinks poison and kills himself, his poison will be in his hand, sipping it in the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein forever. Whoever kills himself with an iron implement, his iron will be in his hand, stabbing himself in his belly in the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein forever."

(p-1205) Al-Shaykhan also related from him, may God be pleased with him, who said: "We witnessed Khaybar, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to a man among those with him who claimed to be Muslim: This is one of the people of the Fire. When the fighting began, the man fought the most fiercely, until he was heavily wounded. Some of the people nearly doubted, but the man felt the pain of his wound, so he reached with his hand to his quiver, drew arrows from it, and slashed his own throat with them. Some men among the Muslims rushed forward and said: O Messenger of God, God has verified your saying, so-and-so has slashed his throat and killed himself. He said: Rise, O so-and-so, and proclaim that none enters Paradise except a believer, and that God supports this religion even through a wicked man." This is the wording of al-Bukhari.

Abu Dawud related from Jabir ibn Samurah, may God be pleased with both of them, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was informed of a man who had killed himself, so he said: I will not pray over him."

In the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Jundub ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Among those who were before you there was a man who had a wound, so he became distressed, took a knife and cut his hand with it. The blood did not stop until he died. God, Mighty and Majestic, said: My servant has hastened to take his own life; I have forbidden Paradise to him."

For this reason, God, the Exalted, said:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 4, verse 30:

(p-1206) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And whoever does that in transgression and injustice, We will drive him into a Fire, and that is ever easy for Allah.﴾ [30]

﴿And whoever does that﴾, i.e., the killing, ﴿in transgression and injustice﴾, i.e., overstepping in it, being unjust in engaging in it, that is, knowing its prohibition and audaciously violating it. ﴿We will drive him into a Fire﴾, i.e., We will cause him to enter ﴿a Fire﴾, i.e., an awesome one of severe punishment. ﴿And that is ever easy for Allah﴾, i.e., his being driven into the Fire is ﴿easy for Him﴾, with no difficulty in it and no one to turn Him away from it, because He, exalted is He, is not overcome by anything.

Al-Nasafi said: This threat applies to the one who deems it lawful, regarding eternal abiding (in the Fire), and to others, to show that he deserves to enter the Fire, alongside Allah's promise of forgiving him. Ended.

**The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:**

﴿If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will remove your bad deeds from you and admit you to an honorable entrance﴾ [31]

﴿If you avoid﴾, i.e., you leave aside, ﴿the major sins you are forbidden﴾, i.e., the major sins (kaba'ir, "major sins") which the Law has forbidden you, whether those mentioned here or those not mentioned. ﴿We will remove your bad deeds﴾, i.e., the minor sins (sagha'ir, "minor sins") of your wrongdoings, and We will erase them from you, and We will admit you to Paradise, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And We will admit you﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿to an honorable entrance﴾, i.e., a good one, which is Paradise. The word (mudkhalan) has been read with a ḍammah on the mīm, as a noun of place or a mīmī verbal noun, meaning: an entering together with honor. And with a fatḥah on the mīm, which also may be a noun of place or a verbal noun. In the verse there is evidence that minor sins are expiated by avoiding major sins, and a refutation of those who say that all sins are major sins and that there is no minor sin.

The Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in *al-Jawab al-Kafi*: The Qur'an, the Sunnah, the consensus (ijma', "scholarly consensus") of the Companions (p-1207) and the Successors (tabi'un, "the generation after the Companions") after them, and the imams, all indicate that among sins there are major and minor ones. Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will remove your bad deeds from you﴾ [al-Nisa’: 31], and He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Those who avoid major sins and indecencies, except for minor lapses﴾ [al-Najm: 32].

In the Sahih, from him ﷺ, he said: "The five daily prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiations for what is between them, if major sins are avoided."

These expiating deeds have three degrees:

The first: that they fall short of expiating minor sins, due to their weakness and the weakness of sincerity in them and the observance of their rights. This is like a weak medicine which falls short of resisting the disease in quantity and quality.

The second: that they resist minor sins but do not reach the expiation of any major sins.

The third: that they are strong enough to expiate minor sins, and there remains in them a strength by which some major sins are expiated. So reflect on this, for it removes from you many difficulties.

In the Sahih, from him ﷺ, he said: "Shall I inform you of the greatest of the major sins?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Associating partners with Allah, and disobedience to parents." He was reclining and he sat up and said: "Beware, and false speech," three times.

(p-1208) In the Sahih, from him ﷺ: "Avoid the seven destructive sins."

They said: "What are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah, sorcery, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, consuming usury, consuming the property of an orphan, fleeing on the day of battle, and slandering chaste, unwary, believing women."

In the Sahih, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Which sin is greatest in the sight of Allah? He said: That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you. I said: Then which? He said: Then that you kill your child for fear that it will eat with you. I said: Then which? He said: That you commit adultery with the wife of your neighbor."

He said: This verse was revealed confirming his ﷺ words: ﴿And those who do not call upon another god with Allah, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, nor commit adultery﴾ [al-Furqan: 68], to the end of the verse. Then he (al-Qasimi) went on to cite the disagreement regarding their enumeration. End of quote.

In my view, the correct position is to stop at the enumeration as established by the authentic hadiths, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the one who explains the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and is trusted with its interpretation. The reference for explaining the Book of Allah, Exalted is He, is the authentic Sunnah. Likewise, the reference for defining the major sin is enumeration rather than fixing it with a definition, as a group of jurists undertook, and the debate among them over those definitions went on at length. Some of those definitions are not comprehensive, and some are not exclusive. All of that is unnecessary once the sound reports have come concerning this matter.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir has cited here a considerable number of them, along with transmissions from the Companions, the early generations and the Successors, so consult him, for it is valuable.

Then Exalted is He forbade envy, and forbade wishing for what Allah has favored some people with over others, in wealth and the like, which is an area of competition, by His words:

(p-١٢٠٩) On the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others. For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned. And ask Allah of His bounty. Indeed, Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾ [32]

﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others. For men is a share of what they have earned﴾: i.e., what they have attained and acquired. ﴿And for women is a share of what they have earned﴾: i.e., what they have attained and acquired. That is, for each group there is a share of what it has earned of the bounties of this world, whether by restriction or expansion. So one should be content with what Allah has apportioned to him.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Mujahid that "Umm Salamah said: 'O Messenger of Allah, men go out to fight and women do not go out to fight, and we only have half of the inheritance.' So Allah, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And do not wish for...﴾, the verse." Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it and said: "It is gharib (unusual)."

Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak and added: "Then Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, I will not lose the work of any worker among you, whether male or female﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:195], the verse." If this is authentic, then the meaning is that each person has a measure of reward that he deserves by the generosity and kindness of Allah. So do not wish for the opposite of that. There is no barrier to the verse encompassing matters relating to the conditions of this world and the Hereafter, since the wording permits this and there is no contradiction. And Allah knows best.

﴿And ask Allah of His bounty﴾: i.e., from the treasuries of His blessings, which never run out. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ask Allah of His bounty, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves to be asked. And the best of worship is waiting for relief."

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing﴾. For this reason He has placed people in ranks, raising some of them above others in degrees, according to the levels of their capacities, which overflow upon them in accordance with a will founded upon noble wisdom. This was said by Abu al-Su'ud.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And for every one We have appointed heirs (mawali) to what the parents and close relatives leave, and to those whom your oaths have bound [in alliance], give them their share. Indeed, Allah is ever Witness over all things.﴾ [4:33]

﴿And for every one We have appointed heirs to what the parents and close relatives leave⟩ That is: for every [portion] of the wealth left by the parents and close relatives, We have appointed heirs and agnatic kinsmen (asabah) who take charge of it and safeguard it, and they inherit it to the exclusion of the rest of people.

As is established in the two Sahih collections (al-Sahihayn), on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give the prescribed shares to their rightful owners, and whatever remains belongs to the nearest male relative." That is: divide the inheritance among the sharers (ashab al-fara'id) whom Allah mentioned in the two verses of inheritance, and whatever remains after that, give it to the agnatic kinsmen. Thus "mimma" (from what) is explanatory of "likulli" (for every one).

Ibn Jarir said: The Arabs call a paternal cousin a mawla, as al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas said:

Gently, sons of our paternal uncle, gently, our mawali;
let not appear among us what has been buried.

(p. 1211) In the "al-Qamus" and its commentary "Taj al-Arus": al-mawla is the close relative, like a paternal cousin and the like.

Ibn al-A'rabi said: A paternal cousin is a mawla, and a sister's son is a mawla. And the poet's saying:

They are our mawla, even if they act unjustly toward us,
and we are indeed visitors at their meeting.

Abu Ubayda said: he means the mawali, that is, paternal cousins. Al-Lahbi, addressing the Banu Umayya, said:

Gently, sons of our paternal uncle, gently, our mawali;
walk slowly as you used to walk.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and those whom your oaths have bound⟩, it is a subject (mubtada') that is given the sense of a conditional, so its predicate comes with the fa' (then), which is His saying: ﴿so give them their share⟩. It is recited as ("'aqadat") with an alif, and the object is omitted, meaning: "aqadat-hum" (whom they bound). It is also recited without the alif, and the object and the returning pronoun are both omitted; its estimation is: "'aqadat halifahum aymanukum" (your oaths bound their alliance). The 'aqd (binding) means tying, fastening, confirming and strengthening, and from it comes: "'aqada al-'ahd, ya'qiduhu," meaning he tied it firmly.

Al-aymān is the plural of yamin, either in the sense of the right hand, because they placed their hands in covenants, or in the sense of an oath, and this is the more apparent, because 'aqd is the opposite of naqd (breaking), and it has come linked with oath-swearing in His saying: ﴿And do not break oaths after their confirmation﴾ [16:91], and in His saying: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintended in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what you have bound with [deliberate] oaths﴾ [5:89].

(p. 1212) This verse carries many meanings and aspects, both of the early (salaf) and later (khalaf) scholars. The most apparent of them to the early exegetes, may Allah be pleased with them, is that what is meant by the relative pronoun is the allies (al-hulafa'), and this is what is transmitted from Ibn Abbas in al-Bukhari, as will come.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was transmitted from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Ata', al-Hasan, Ibn al-Musayyib, Abu Salih, Sulayman ibn Yasar, al-Sha'bi, Ikrimah, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan, that they said: they are the allies. End of quotation.

It may be added: Ali ibn Abi Talhah as well.

The allies used to inherit a sixth (sudus) from their allies.

Al-Tabari related through the chain of Qatadah: A man would make a covenant with another man in the pre-Islamic period, and he would say: "My blood is your blood, you inherit me and I inherit you, you seek vengeance for me and I seek it for you." When Islam came, some of them remained, so they were commanded to give them their share of the inheritance, which is a sixth; then that was abrogated (nusikha) by inheritance through kinship, and He said: ﴿And the blood relatives are more entitled to one another﴾ [33:6].

For this reason Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "so give them their share of the inheritance." He said: Abu Bakr made a covenant with a mawla and inherited from him.

Al-Zamakhshari said: What is meant by ("those whom your oaths have bound") is the mawali of alliance (mawali al-muwalah). A man would make a covenant with another man and say: "My blood is your blood, my ruin is your ruin, my vengeance is your vengeance, my war is your war, my peace is your peace, you inherit me and I inherit you, you seek vengeance for me and I seek it for you, you pay the blood-money (ya'qilu) for me and I pay it for you." So the ally receives a sixth of the ally's inheritance. End of quotation.

(p. 1213) On this basis, the meaning of the verse is: "and those with whom you made a covenant of allegiance and alliance, and you swore mutual oaths, you and they, for support and inheritance, before the revelation of this verse, so give them their share of the inheritance, fulfilling the contracts and covenants, since you promised them that in binding oaths."

Ibn Abi Hatim related: Before Islam, a man would make a covenant with a man and say: "You inherit me and I inherit you." The tribes used to form alliances with one another, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every alliance in the pre-Islamic period, or covenant that Islam found, Islam increases it only in firmness; there is no covenant and no alliance in Islam."

Imam Ahmad, Muslim and al-Nasa'i related, on the authority of Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no alliance in Islam, and whatever alliance existed in the pre-Islamic period, Islam has increased it only in firmness."

Imam Ahmad related on the authority of Qays ibn Asim that he asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the alliance. He said: "Whatever alliance existed in the pre-Islamic period, hold fast to it, but there is no alliance in Islam."

He also related it through Amr (p. 1214) ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered Makkah in the year of the Conquest, he stood up to deliver a sermon to the people, and said: 'O people, whatever alliance existed in the pre-Islamic period, Islam has increased it only in firmness, and there is no alliance in Islam.'"

Ibn al-Athir said: Alliance (hilf), in its origin, is a binding and a mutual pact upon mutual support, aid and agreement. So whatever of it existed in the pre-Islamic period concerning strife, fighting and raids, that is what the prohibition in Islam refers to, in his (ﷺ) saying: "There is no alliance in Islam." And whatever of it existed in the pre-Islamic period concerning the support of the oppressed and the maintenance of kinship ties, like the alliance of the Perfumed Ones (Hilf al-Mutayyibin), and what went in its course, that is what he (ﷺ) referred to in his saying: "Whatever alliance existed in the pre-Islamic period, Islam has increased it only in firmness." He means by binding oneself to goodness and support of the truth, and by this the two hadiths are reconciled, and this is the alliance that Islam requires, while what is forbidden is what contradicts the ruling of Islam. End of quotation.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: This, that is, inheritance by alliance, was at the beginning of Islam, then it was abrogated after that, and they were commanded to fulfil their obligations to those with whom they had made covenants, and not to create any new covenant after this verse.

Ibn Abi Hatim related on the authority of Ibn Abbas concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those whom your oaths have bound, so give them their share﴾: "A man before Islam would make a covenant with a man and say: 'You inherit me and I inherit you.' The tribes used to form alliances, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Every alliance in the pre-Islamic period, or covenant that Islam found, Islam increases it only in firmness, and there is no covenant and no alliance in Islam.' So this verse abrogated it: ﴿And blood relatives are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah﴾ [8:75]."

Abu Dawud related on the authority of Ibn Abbas concerning this verse: A man would make an alliance with a man, and there was no kinship between them, and one of them would inherit from the other. So that was abrogated in al-Anfal, when He said: ﴿And blood relatives are more entitled to one another﴾ [8:75], and so on.

(p. 1215) Ibn Jarir related, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A man would make a covenant with a man, so whichever of them died, the other would inherit from him. Then Allah, exalted is He, sent down: ﴿And blood relatives are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah than the believers and the emigrants, except that you do kindness to your allies﴾ [33:6]. He says: "except that you bequeath to their allies who made a covenant a bequest, and it is permissible for them out of the one-third of the deceased's property; that is the kindness."

Thus several of the early scholars stated explicitly that this verse was abrogated by His saying: ﴿And blood relatives [are more entitled]﴾ [8:75], and so on.

I say: According to what has been mentioned, the verse is muhkam (definitive, not abrogated) at the beginning of Islam, and abrogated after it.

There is another aspect to it, which is that it abrogates the inheritance of the ally through another interpretation, which is what al-Bukhari related on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: ﴿For every one We have appointed heirs (mawali)⟩ as heirs, ﴿and those whom your oaths have bound⟩: When the emigrants came to Madinah, the emigrant would inherit from the Ansari to the exclusion of his blood relatives, because of the brotherhood which the Prophet (ﷺ) established between them. But when He revealed: ﴿For every one We have appointed heirs⟩, it was abrogated. Then He said: ﴿and those whom your oaths have bound﴾, of support, assistance and counsel, and the inheritance has gone, but a bequest is made to him.

Some scholars understood from this report that this verse abrogated alliance in the future, and the ruling of past alliance as well, and that there is no inheritance by it. The correct view is what we have already presented, namely the establishment of inheritance by a previous alliance before the revelation of the verse at the beginning of Islam, as related by several of the early scholars, and as Ibn Abbas said: "The emigrant used to inherit from the Ansari to the exclusion of his blood relatives until that was abrogated."

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, in "Fath al-Bari," attempted to reconcile the earlier reports with the report of al-Bukhari, by supposing that the abrogation occurred twice:

The first: when the ally inherited alone, to the exclusion of the agnatic kinsmen. Then ﴿For every one We have appointed⟩ was revealed, so they all inherited together. Then the verse of al-Ahzab abrogated that, and inheritance was restricted to the agnatic kinsmen, while the ally retained support, assistance and similar things. And Allah knows best.

(p. 1216) Furthermore, there are other reports about the occasion of revelation:

Among them: what Abu Dawud and Ibn Abi Hatim related on the authority of Dawud ibn al-Husayn, who said: "I used to recite to Umm Sa'd bint al-Rabi', who was an orphan in the care of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him. I recited: ('wa-alladhina 'aqadat aymanukum') [with an alif], and she said: 'Do not recite it like that, but: ﴿and those whom your oaths have bound⟩. It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and his son Abd al-Rahman, may Allah be pleased with them both, when he refused Islam, and Abu Bakr swore that he would not give him an inheritance. But when he embraced Islam, Allah commanded him to give him his share.'"

Among them: what Ibn Jarir related from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyib, who said: This verse was revealed concerning those who adopted men who were not their sons and made them heirs. So Allah revealed concerning them, and gave them a share in the bequest, and returned the inheritance to the mawali in the case of kinsmen and agnates, and Allah refused that those they claimed and adopted should be heirs, but He gave them a share in the bequest.

Know that these early aspects reported concerning the occasion of revelation are all such that the verse is true of them, encompasses them, and its ruling applies to them, and there is no contradiction among them, because of what we have already stated in the introduction to the tafsir, so refer back to it and do not overlook it.

Now, Abu Ali al-Jubba'i has another interpretation of the verse. He said: The estimate of the verse is: "and for every one, of what the parents and close relatives leave, and those whom your oaths have bound, there are mawali, heirs ﴿so give them their share⟩, that is: give the mawali and heirs their share." So His saying: ("and those whom your oaths have bound") is coordinated with His saying: ﴿the parents and close relatives﴾, and the meaning is: what those whom your oaths have bound leave, has an heir who is most entitled to it. Allah, exalted is He, named the heir a mawla. The meaning is: do not give the property to the ally, but to the mawla and the heir.

(p. 1217) Abu Muslim al-Isfahani said: What is meant by ("those whom your oaths have bound") is the husband and wife, and marriage is called an 'aqd (binding contract). Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿and do not resolve upon the tie of marriage﴾ [2:235]. So He mentioned the parents and close relatives, and mentioned with them the husband and wife. A parallel to this is the verse of inheritance, in that when He explained the inheritance of the child and the parents, He mentioned with them the inheritance of the husband and wife.

I say: This interpretation mentioned, and what came before it, is the method of one who does not stop with the transmitted reports of the early scholars in tafsir, and sees himself as competing with them in ijtihad (independent reasoning) on this matter, on the basis that whatever has not been established by mass transmission (tawatur) concerning the meaning of the verse, whether by report or consensus (ijma'), there is no proof in what is transmitted from it by individual narrators (ahad), whether traced to the Prophet or stopping at a companion, even if it is authentic. This method is the path of a group who fell short in knowledge of the revealed texts (ilm al-sam') and neglected inquiry into it, so from this arose deficiency in the religion and addition to it by mere opinion.

Our position is that there is no escape from returning to the tafsir of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), because of the praise for them that is established in the Book and the Sunnah, and because the Qur'an was revealed in their language, so error is further removed from them than from others. This is especially so for the tafsir of the scholar of the Ummah (ḥibr al-ummah, one of the most learned of the Ummah) and its sea (baḥruhā), ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father). Thus, whenever the chain of narration to him is sound, his tafsir is among the most authentic tafsirs, taking precedence over many of the great imams, for several reasons:

Among them: it is established from him (may Allah be pleased with him) that he would not permit interpreting the Qur'an by personal opinion (taʾwil bi-l-ra'y). It is related from him that he said: "Whoever speaks about the Qur'an according to his opinion, let him take his seat in the Fire." In another narration: "without knowledge." Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-ʿIlm, al-Nasa'i, and al-Tirmidhi.

So when he (may Allah be pleased with him) affirms a matter definitively, it serves as evidence that it is traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ), as we mentioned in the introduction.

(p-1218) "Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things" — among the things of which giving and withholding are a part — "Witness" (shahidan), i.e., Knowing. In it is both promise and warning.

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women, because Allah has made some of them excel over others, and because they spend from their wealth. So righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding in the husband's absence what Allah has commanded them to guard. As for those women from whom you fear disobedience (nushuz), admonish them, abandon them in the beds, and strike them. But if they obey you, then seek no way against them. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted and Great.﴾ [34]

﴿الرِّجالُ قَوّامُونَ عَلى النِّساءِ﴾ is the plural of qawwam, meaning one who stands over affairs with management, direction and discipline. That is, they are empowered over the discipline of women; they stand over them, commanding and forbidding, as rulers stand over their subjects. This is for two reasons: an innate one and an acquired one.

He pointed to the first with His saying: ﴿بِما فَضَّلَ اللَّهُ بَعْضَهم عَلى بَعْضٍ﴾ ("because Allah has made some of them excel over others"). The pronoun refers to men and women together. That is, they are dominant over them because Allah has favoured some of them, namely the men, over others, namely the women.

They have mentioned, as the excellence of men: intellect, firmness, resolve, strength, horsemanship and archery. Among them are the prophets. Among them are the greater and lesser imamate (leadership), jihad, the adhan (call to prayer), the khutbah (sermon), testimony in the principal matters of judgement, guardianship in marriage, divorce and revocation, the number of wives permitted, the greater share of inheritance, and agnatic inheritance (ta'sib). They are the people of beards and turbans. And one who is complete in himself has the right of guardianship over one who is deficient.

He pointed to the second with His glorified saying: ﴿وبِما أنْفَقُوا مِن أمْوالِهِمْ﴾ ("and because they spend from their wealth"), in their dowries and their maintenance. Thus they have become like slaves. And since the maintainers are in the position of masters, obedience to them is obligatory upon the women, just as obedience to masters is obligatory upon slaves.

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "A man from the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a woman. She said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Indeed, my husband, so-and-so the son of so-and-so the Ansari, struck me, and it left a mark on my face.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'He has no right to that.' (p-1219) Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿The men are the maintainers of women﴾ concerning discipline. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I desired a matter, and Allah desired otherwise.'" Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it as a mursal report (one whose chain omits a companion) through several routes.

Al-Suyuti said: "Its supporting reports strengthen one another." ʿAli ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding this verse: "That is, rulers over them, meaning that she obeys him in what Allah has commanded her of obedience. And her obedience is that she be good to his family and guard his property."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If I were to command anyone to prostrate to another, I would command the woman to prostrate to her husband."

﴿فالصّالِحاتُ﴾ ("So the righteous women"), that is, among women, ﴿قانِتاتٌ﴾ ("are devoutly obedient"), that is, obedient to Allah concerning their husbands, ﴿حافِظاتٌ لِلْغَيْبِ﴾ ("guarding in the absence"). Al-Zamakhshari said: "al-ghayb (الغَيْب) is the opposite of al-shahadah (presence). That is, they guard what is obligatory to guard when the husbands are not present: they guard their private parts, their property and their homes during the absence." ﴿بِما حَفِظَ اللَّهُ﴾ ("with what Allah has guarded"), that is, by Allah's guarding of them and their preservation through granting them success in guarding in the absence. So the one who is guarded is the one whom Allah guards; that is, guarding is not made easy for them except by Allah's grant of success. Or the meaning is: with what Allah has guarded for them of the rights they are owed by men. That is, they must guard the husband's rights in return for Allah having guarded their rights over their husbands, since He commanded the men to deal justly with them, to keep them honourably, and to give them their due. Thus His saying "with what Allah has guarded" follows the pattern of the saying "this for that", meaning in exchange for it.

Al-Mahayimi took the preposition (ba') to indicate seeking help, saying: "seeking help through His guarding, out of fear that their souls might overcome them, even if they reach whatever level of righteousness they reach." End of quotation.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "The best of women is the woman who, when you look at her, pleases you; when you command her, she obeys you; and when you are absent, she guards you in herself and your property." He said: "Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿The men are the maintainers of women﴾ to its end."

(p-1220) Imam Ahmad narrated from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When a woman prays her five (prayers), fasts her month, guards her private parts and obeys her husband, it will be said to her: 'Enter Paradise by whichever of its gates you wish.'"

* *

Note:

Al-Suyuti said in "al-Iklil", concerning His saying ﴿The men are the maintainers of women﴾: indeed the husband takes charge of the upbringing of his wife, her discipline, and preventing her from going out. She is obliged to obey him except in disobedience to Allah. This is because of the maintenance that is owed to her from him. The scholars understood from this that whenever he is unable to maintain her, he is no longer her maintainer, and his right to prevent her from going out lapses.

Those who permit her to seek annulment (faskh) in such a case take this as evidence, and because when he ceases to be her maintainer, he has departed from the purpose intended by marriage.

Whoever makes it a right of the husband to restrict his wife in her person and property, so that she may not dispose of it except with his permission, also takes evidence from the verse, because He made him (qawwaman), in the form of intensification, meaning one who watches over a thing and guards it.

It has also been argued from it that a woman is not permitted to hold the office of judge, as with the greater imamate, because He made men maintainers over them, so it is not permitted for them to stand over men. End of quotation.

﴿واللاتِي تَخافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ﴾ ("And those from whom you fear nushuz"), that is, their disobedience, their bad conduct, and their elevating themselves above submitting to you. It derives from (al-nashz, النَّشْز), which is a raised part of the ground. It is said: "The woman rebelled (nashazat) against her husband, or over her husband": she defied him, rose above him, disliked him and departed from his obedience.

﴿فَعِظُوهُنَّ﴾ ("admonish them"), that is, frighten them with words, such as: "Fear Allah, and know that your obedience to me is an obligation upon you, and beware of Allah's punishment for disobeying me." This is because Allah has made the husband's right over her and his obedience obligatory, and has forbidden her to disobey him, because of his favour and bounty upon her. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If I were to command anyone to prostrate to another, I would command the woman to prostrate to her husband." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi from Abu Hurayrah, and Imam Ahmad (p-1221) from Muʿadh, and al-Hakim from Buraydah.

Al-Bukhari narrated from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If a man calls his wife to his bed and she refuses, and he spends the night angry with her, the angels curse her until morning."

Muslim narrated it, and his wording is: "If a woman spends the night abandoning her husband's bed, the angels curse her until morning."

﴿واهْجُرُوهُنَّ﴾ ("and abandon them"), after that, if admonition and advice do not benefit, ﴿فِي المَضاجِعِ﴾ ("in the beds"), that is, the sleeping places. Do not bring them under the covers and do not be intimate with them. This is a metaphor for intercourse.

Hammad ibn Salamah al-Basri said: "It means marriage (intercourse)." ʿAli ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: "Abandonment (al-hajr) is that he does not have intercourse with her, lies beside her on her bed, and turns his back to her." Likewise said more than one scholar.

Others, including al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, ʿIkrimah and Ibn ʿAbbas (in one narration), added: "And he does not speak to her or converse with her during that." It was also said: "The beds" means the sleeping places at night; that is, do not spend the night with them.

In the Sunan and the Musnad, it is narrated from Muʿawiyah ibn Haydah al-Qushayri that he said: "O Messenger of Allah! What is the right of one's wife over him?" He said: "That you feed her when you eat, clothe her when you are clothed, do not strike the face, do not disfigure her, and do not abandon her except within the house."

﴿واضْرِبُوهُنَّ﴾ ("and strike them"), if what you have done of admonition and abandonment does not succeed, a strike that is not severe (ghayra mubarrih), that is, not harsh or painful, as is established in Sahih Muslim from Jabir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said during the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Fear Allah concerning women, for they are captives (ʿawan) with you. You have over them that they must not let anyone you dislike onto your beds. If they do that, then strike them with a strike that is not severe."

(p-1222) The jurists said: it means that he must not wound her, nor break a bone of hers, nor leave any mark, and he must avoid the face, because it is the gathering place of beauty. The strike should be spread over her body and not concentrated in one place, lest its harm become great.

Some said: the striking should be with a rolled-up cloth, or with his hand, not with a whip or a stick. ʿAta' said: "A strike with a tooth-stick (siwak)."

Al-Razi said: "In sum, leniency is observed in this matter in the most emphatic way. What indicates this is that He, exalted is He, began with admonition, then ascended from it to abandonment in the beds, then ascended from it to striking. This is a warning, operating as a near-explicit statement, that whenever the purpose is achieved by the gentler means, it is obligatory to suffice with it, and it is not permitted to proceed to the harsher means. This is the view of those who say that the ruling of this verse is applied in sequence, for although the wording of the verse indicates combination, the import (fahwa) of the verse indicates sequence."

ʿAli ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: "He abandons her in the bed. If she responds, well and good; otherwise Allah has permitted you to strike her with a strike that is not severe and does not break her bone. If she responds, well and good; otherwise Allah has made it lawful for you to receive ransom from her (fidyah)."

Others said: "This sequence is observed when the fear of nushuz exists. But once it is established, there is no harm in combining all of them."

It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Hang the whip where the household can see it, for that is more disciplining for them." Narrated by ʿAbd ibn Humayd and al-Tabarani from Ibn ʿAbbas, and Abu Nuʿaym in al-Hilyah (Hilyat al-Awliya') from Ibn ʿUmar.

﴿فَإنْ أطَعْنَكم فَلا تَبْغُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ سَبِيلا﴾ ("But if they obey you, then seek no way against them"), that is, if they return from nushuz at this discipline to obedience in all that is required of them, in what Allah has permitted of them, then there is no way for men over them after that, by rebuke, harming them with striking or abandonment. ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيًّا كَبِيرًا﴾ ("Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted and Great"), so beware of Him. This is a warning to husbands against wronging women without cause. For though they are weak in repelling your injustice and unable to take retribution from you, Allah, glorified is He, is Exalted, Dominant, Great and Capable. He takes vengeance upon whoever wrongs them and transgresses against them. So do not be deceived by your being higher in strength than them and greater in rank than them (p-1223), for Allah is higher than you and more capable over you than you are over them. Thus concluding the verse with these two names contains complete suitability.

When He, exalted is He, mentioned the ruling on the aversion and nushuz of the wife, He mentioned what applies when the aversion is from both spouses, by His saying:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 4, verse 35:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

﴿And if you fear a breach between the two, appoint an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family. If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will bring about harmony between them. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Acquainted.﴾ [35]

﴿And if you fear a breach between the two﴾: its original form is "shiqaqan baynahuma" (a breach between them), so the word "shiqaq" (breach, discord) was attributed to the adverbial phrase "bayn" (between). This may be by treating it as if it were the object (a broad usage), as in His words: ﴿Rather, it is the plotting of the night and the day﴾ [Saba': 33], whose original form is "bal makrun fi al-layli wa al-nahar" (rather, a plot in the night and the day); or by treating it as if it were the subject, making the "bayn" (the space between them) the one who opposes, and the night and the day the ones who plot, as in your saying: "Your day is fasting." The pronoun refers to the spouses, although they have not been mentioned, because what indicates them has been mentioned, namely the men and the women. That is: if you know of a disagreement that divides them, and it is unclear to you whether it comes from his side or from hers, and the husband does not make reconciliation, nor forgiveness, nor separation, and the wife does not fulfil the right nor offer the ransom.

﴿Then appoint﴾: that is, to the spouses, for the reform of their relationship and the clarifying of the matter. ﴿an arbiter﴾: a man suitable for judging, reconciling, and restraining the wrongdoer from wrongdoing. ﴿from his family﴾: that is, from the relatives of the husband. ﴿and an arbiter from her family﴾ of the same description as the first, for relatives know the inner states of affairs better and are more eager for reconciliation. It is therefore incumbent upon them both to meet privately and uncover the true state of affairs, so that they may know whether the desire of the couple is for continuation or for separation. ﴿If they both desire﴾: that is, the two arbiters ﴿reconciliation, Allah will bring about harmony between them﴾: that is, He will place agreement between them, so that they agree upon one word and support one another in seeking accord until the aim is achieved and the purpose is accomplished. Or the first pronoun refers to the two arbiters and the second to the spouses, meaning: if they intend the reconciliation of the relationship, and their intention is sound and their hearts sincerely seek the countenance of Allah, then their mediation is blessed, and Allah, through the goodness of their effort, will place harmony and affection between the spouses, and cast into their souls love and mercy.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing﴾ of the outward and inward states of the two arbiters, and if they intend corruption, He will requite them for it; otherwise He will requite them for reconciliation.

Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas: Allah, mighty and majestic, commanded that they send a righteous man from the husband's family and a similar one from the wife's family, and they should look into which of them is the wrongdoer. If the husband is the wrongdoer, they prevent him from his wife and restrict him to maintenance; and if the wife is the wrongdoer, they restrict her to her husband and withhold maintenance from her. If their opinion agrees to separate or to unite, their decision is permissible. If they see fit to unite, and one of the spouses is pleased while the other dislikes it, and then one of them dies, the one who was pleased inherits from the one who was not, but the one who disliked it does not inherit from the one who was pleased.

'Abd al-Razzaq narrated in his (Musannaf) from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: I and Mu'awiyah were sent as arbiters. Ma'mar said: It has reached me that 'Uthman sent them, and said to them: If you see fit to unite, unite; and if you see fit to separate, separate.

It is related (and it is attributed) from Ibn Abi Mulaykah that 'Aqil ibn Abi Talib married Fatimah bint 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, and she said: "You will come to me, and I will spend upon you." Whenever he entered upon her, she would say: "Where are 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah and Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah?" He said: "On your left, in the Fire, when you enter." So she tightened her garments around herself and came to 'Uthman and mentioned that to him, and he laughed. He sent for Ibn 'Abbas and Mu'awiyah. Ibn 'Abbas said: "I will certainly separate them." Mu'awiyah said: "I would not separate two persons from the sons of 'Abd Manaf." So they went to them and found that they had closed their doors upon themselves, and they returned.

It is related (and it is attributed) from 'Ubaydah who said: I witnessed 'Ali, when a woman and her husband came to him, each with a group of people. He brought out one arbiter from these and one from those. 'Ali said to the two arbiters: "Do you know what is incumbent upon you? If you see fit to unite them, unite them." The woman said: "I am content with the Book of Allah, for me and against me." The husband said: "As for separation, no." 'Ali said: "You have lied, by Allah! You shall not depart until you are content with the Book of Allah, for you and against you." Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir also narrated it.

The Hafiz Ibn Kathir said: The scholars have unanimously agreed that the two arbiters have the authority both to unite and to separate, to the point that Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: If the two arbiters wish to separate them by one divorce, or two, or three, they may do so; and this is a narration from Malik.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: The two arbiters judge regarding union, not regarding separation. Likewise said Qatadah and Zayd ibn Aslam, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Abu Thawr, and Dawud held this view. Their basis is His words: ﴿If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will bring about harmony between them﴾, and He did not mention separation. As for when the two are agents from the side of the spouses, their judgment is executed in both union and separation without disagreement. End of quotation.

In (al-Iklil): Ibn Mansur reported that those commanded to send are the rulers.

It is related from al-Suddi that it refers to the spouses themselves. On the first view, whoever holds that they are appointed by the judge uses it as evidence, so the consent of the spouses is not required for what they do of divorce or otherwise. On the second view, whoever holds that they are agents of the spouses uses it as evidence, so consent is required.

Ibn Kathir said: The majority hold the first view, namely that they are appointed from the side of the judge, based on His words: ﴿appoint an arbiter﴾ etc., for He called them "arbiters", and it is the nature of an arbiter to judge even without the consent of the one judged against; and this is the apparent meaning of the verse.

Al-Shafi'i and Abu Hanifah held the second view, based on 'Ali's words to the husband (when he said: "As for separation, no"), where he said: "You have lied," until you acknowledge what she has acknowledged.

They said: If they were arbiters, the husband's acknowledgment would not have been required. And Allah knows best.

In the verse there is an indication that whoever sets right his intention in what he seeks, Allah, exalted is He, grants him success in his aim.

* *

Note:

Al-Hakim said: The verse indicates that whenever one fears separation and strife, it is permissible for him to send two arbiters. Amir al-Mu'minin also cited it against the Kharijites regarding the arbitration he carried out. The shaykhs of the Mu'tazilah said: Since the copies of the Qur'an were raised (as a stratagem), and division appeared in his army, and he feared for his own life, arbitration became permissible, and indeed obligatory. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) made peace on the day of Hudaybiyyah, and on this basis the peace of al-Hasan (peace be upon him) is to be understood.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

﴿And worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents, and to relatives, orphans, the needy, the neighbor who is near of kin, the neighbor who is a stranger, the companion at your side, the wayfarer, and those whom your right hands possess. Indeed, Allah does not love one who is self-deluded and boastful﴾ [36]

﴿And worship Allah and associate nothing with Him﴾ He, Exalted is He, commands that He alone be worshipped and that worship be made sincere to Him, by His words: ﴿and associate nothing with Him﴾, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Al-Bayyinah: 5].
