So the meaning is: it suffices you to use the earth on two members: the face and the hand." He referred to the hand with "the palm," and there is no need to use it on the whole body. On this basis, the number of strikes, the delimitation of the hand, and the obligation or non-obligation of order are established by other evidences, such as the hadith: "Tayammum is one strike for the face and one strike for the forearms up to the elbows," and other things, for it is sahih, as some of the memorizers stated, and it is given to know the number of strikes and the delimitation of the hand, so it takes precedence over what is not given for that purpose. And Allah knows best. End of his words."

As for his saying "it is a sahih hadith," there is in it what has been stated before.

Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in "Zad al-Ma'ad," in the section "His guidance (ﷺ) regarding tayammum," verbatim: "He (ﷺ) would perform tayammum with one strike for the face and the two palms, and it is not authentically reported from him that he performed tayammum with two strikes, nor up to the elbows."

Al-Imam Ahmad said: "Whoever says that tayammum is up to the elbows has only added something of his own. Likewise, he would perform tayammum on the ground on which he prayed, whether it was dust, saline soil, or sand."

And it is authentically reported from him that he said: "Wherever the prayer reaches a man of my community, there is his mosque and his purifier (tahur)." This is an explicit text that whoever is reached by the prayer in sand, then sand is for him a purifier.

When he (ﷺ) and his companions traveled on the expedition of Tabuk, they crossed those sands on their way, and their water was extremely scarce, yet it is not reported from him that he carried dust with him, nor commanded it, nor did any of his companions do so, while it is certain that in the wilderness sand is more abundant than dust, and likewise the land of the Hijaz and elsewhere. Whoever reflects on this will be certain that he used to perform tayammum with sand, and Allah knows best. This is the view of the majority.

As for what is mentioned concerning the description of tayammum, namely placing the inner surfaces of the fingers of the left hand on the backs of the right hand, then drawing it to the elbow, then turning the palm of the hand over the inner forearm, and raising the left thumb like the muezzin until it reaches the right thumb, then closing it over it: it is known with certainty that the Prophet (ﷺ) did not do this, nor taught it to anyone of his companions, nor commanded it, nor approved of it. This is his guidance, to which judgment is referred. Likewise, it is not authentically reported from him that tayammum is performed for each prayer; rather it was stated absolutely, and he made it a substitute for wudu', and this requires that its ruling be the ruling of wudu', except where evidence indicates otherwise. End of quote.

(Seventh point) Here Ibn Kathir mentioned the cause for the legislation of tayammum, saying: "We mention this here because this verse in al-Nisa' was revealed before the verse of al-Ma'ida. Its explanation is that this one was revealed before the prohibition of wine, and wine was prohibited shortly after Uhud, during the Prophet's (ﷺ) siege of Banu al-Nadir. As for al-Ma'ida, it is among the last things revealed, especially its beginning, so it is fitting to mention the cause here. And with Allah is success."

Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from 'A'isha, that she borrowed a necklace from Asma', and it was lost, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent men to search for it, and they found it, but the prayer time came upon them while they had no water, so they prayed without wudu'. They complained of this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed tayammum. Usayd ibn al-Hudayr said to 'A'isha: May Allah reward you with good; by Allah, whenever a matter you dislike befalls you, Allah makes for you and the Muslims in it some good.

(Another route) Al-Bukhari said: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Malik informed us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from 'A'isha, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on one of his journeys, until when we were at al-Bayda', or Dhat al-Jaysh, my necklace broke. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stayed to search for it, and the people stayed with him, though they were not near water, and they had no water with them. So the people came to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and said: Do you not see what 'A'isha has done? She has kept the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the people, and they are not near water, and they have no water with them. So Abu Bakr came while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had his head on my thigh, asleep, and he said: You have detained the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the people, and they are not near water and have no water with them. 'A'isha said: Abu Bakr rebuked me and said what Allah willed him to say, and he began poking me in the side with his hand, and nothing prevented me from moving except the place of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) head on my thigh. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) got up (p-1271) until morning came without water, so Allah revealed the verse of tayammum, and they performed tayammum." Then Usayd ibn al-Hudayr said: "This is not the first of your blessings, O family of Abu Bakr."

She said: "We sent the camel I was riding, and we found the necklace beneath it."

Al-Bukhari also narrated it from Qutayba ibn Sa'id, from Malik. Muslim narrated it from Yahya ibn Yahya, from Malik.

End of Ibn Kathir's words.

Al-Wahidi also cited this hadith when mentioning the verse of al-Nisa', in "Asbab al-Nuzul."

Ibn al-'Arabi said: We do not know which of the two verses 'A'isha meant.

Ibn Battal said: It is the verse of al-Nisa' or the verse of al-Ma'ida.

Al-Qurtubi said: It is the verse of al-Nisa', and he justified this by saying that the verse of al-Ma'ida is called the verse of wudu', while the verse of al-Nisa' has no mention of wudu' in it, so it is apt to specify it as the verse of tayammum.

The hafiz Ibn Hajar said in "al-Fath": What was clear to al-Bukhari was hidden from all of them, namely that the intended verse is the verse of al-Ma'ida without any doubt, due to the narration of 'Amr ibn al-Harith, in which he explicitly said: "Then it was revealed: 'O you who believe, when you rise to prayer...' [al-Ma'ida 5:6]" and so on.

The hafiz also said earlier: It has been used as evidence (i.e., the hadith of 'A'isha) that wudu' was obligatory for them before the revelation of the verse of wudu', and this is why they regarded their situation of being without water as serious, and what Abu Bakr said to 'A'isha occurred.

Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: It is known to all the scholars of the military expeditions that the Prophet (ﷺ) did not pray since prayer was made obligatory upon him except with wudu', and only an ignorant or obstinate person would deny this.

He said: In the phrase in this hadith, "the verse of tayammum," there is an indication that the knowledge that came to them at that time was the ruling of tayammum, not the ruling of wudu'. He said: The wisdom in the revelation of the verse of wudu', despite the earlier practice of it, is so that its obligation would be recited through revelation.

Al-Suyuti said in "Lubab al-Nuqul," after affirming this statement: The obligation of wudu' was together with the obligation of prayer in Makkah, and the verse is Madani. End of quote.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar also said, regarding the statement of Usayd ("This is not the first of your blessings"): it indicates that this incident occurred after the incident of the slander (al-ifk), which strengthens the view of those who held that the loss of the necklace happened more than once. Among those who affirmed this definitively was Muhammad ibn Habib al-Akhbari, who said: "The necklace of 'A'isha was lost during the Battle of Dhat al-Riqa' and during the Battle of Banu al-Mustaliq."

Ibn Abi Shaybah related from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: "When the verse of tayammum was revealed, I did not know how to act..." (the hadith continues).

This indicates that it was revealed after the Battle of Banu al-Mustaliq, since Abu Hurayrah's conversion took place in the seventh year, and that (the battle) came after it without any disagreement.

He said: It will come in the chapter on the campaigns (al-maghazi) that al-Bukhari holds that the Battle of Dhat al-Riqa' took place after the arrival of Abu Musa, and his arrival was at the time of Abu Hurayrah's conversion. Among what also indicates that the narrative came after the incident of the slander is what al-Tabarani related through the chain of 'Abbad ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, from 'A'isha, who said: "When the matter of my necklace happened, and the people of the slander said what they said, I went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on another campaign, and my necklace fell again, so that the people were detained searching for it. Abu Bakr said to me: 'O daughter! Will you be a burden and a trial to the people on every journey?' Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the concession (al-rukhsah) of tayammum."

Abu Bakr said: "Indeed you are blessed" (three times). In its chain is Muhammad ibn Humayd al-Razi, and there is criticism of him.

Among the benefits in its context is the explanation of Abu Bakr's reproach, which was left vague in the hadith of the chapter, and the clarification that the loss of the necklace occurred twice, in two campaigns. And Allah knows best. End of the words of al-Hafiz.

Imam Shams al-Din Ibn al-Qayyim said in "Zad al-Ma'ad," under (The Campaign of al-Muraysi', which is the Campaign of Banu al-Mustaliq): it took place in Sha'ban of the fifth year. After mentioning it, he said: Ibn Sa'd said: "In this campaign the necklace of 'A'isha fell, and they were detained searching for it, and the verse of tayammum was revealed." Then he cited the hadith of al-Tabarani mentioned earlier, and said: This indicates that the story of the necklace for which tayammum was revealed was after this campaign, and this is the apparent view. But in that campaign occurred the incident of the slander because of the loss of the necklace and its search, so some people confused one of the two stories with the other. End.

The cause of revelation of the aforementioned verse has also been related from 'Ammar ibn Yasir (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) camped at al-Ulat al-Jaysh, and 'A'isha was with him, and a necklace of hers of Dhafari onyx broke. The people were detained seeking her necklace until dawn broke, and there was no water with the people. Abu Bakr became angry with her and said: 'You have detained the people, and there is no water with them!' So Allah, Exalted, revealed to His Messenger (ﷺ) the concession of purifying with clean earth (al-sa'id al-tayyib). The Muslims stood with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), struck their hands upon the earth, then raised their hands, taking nothing of the dust, and wiped with them their faces and their hands up to the shoulders, and from the undersides of their hands to the armpits."

Ibn Jarir also related it from Abu al-Yaqzan (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when a necklace of 'A'isha was lost, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained until dawn broke, and Abu Bakr became angry with 'A'isha, and the concession was revealed to him: wiping with clean earth. Abu Bakr entered and said to her: 'Indeed you are blessed; a concession has been revealed concerning you.' So we struck our hands once for our faces and once for our hands up to the shoulders and armpits."

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh related another version concerning the cause of revelation, from al-Asla' ibn Shurayk (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "I used to saddle the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I became junub on a cold night, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wanted to depart. I disliked saddling the she-camel of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while I was junub, and I feared that if I washed with cold water I would die or fall ill. So I ordered a man from the Ansar, and he saddled it. Then I heated stones and heated water with them and washed. Then I caught up with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions, and he said: 'O Asla', what is it that I see your saddle has changed?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I did not saddle it; a man from the Ansar saddled it.' He said: 'And why?' I said: 'I became junub, and I feared the cold for myself, so I ordered him to saddle it, and I heated stones and heated water with them and washed with it.' Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾ up to His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾."

Ibn Kathir said: It has been related through another route from him.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 4, verse 44:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They purchase error and wish that you [believers] would go astray from the way.﴾ [44]

﴿Have you not considered﴾ is from the sight of the heart, and it is taken to include the meaning of reaching (intihaʾ), i.e., "Has your knowledge not reached them?" Or it is from the sight of the eye, i.e., "Have you not looked at" ﴿those who were given a portion of the Scripture﴾, meaning a share of knowledge of the Torah, and they are the rabbis (aḥbar) of the Jews. The scholar Abu al-Su'ud said: What is meant by that which they were given is what was made clear to them therein of rulings and knowledge, among which is what they knew of the attributes of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the truth of Islam. The expression of it as a "portion" (naṣīb), which indicates that it is a right of theirs that must be observed and preserved, is for the announcement of the complete baseness of their opinions, in that they wasted it with total waste.

Its tanwin is for magnification (tafkhim), supporting the reproach against them and the wonder at their condition. The expression of them by the relative pronoun (al-mawsul) serves to draw attention, through what is in the clause of relation, to the complete abomination of them, and to indicate the place of what has been omitted from mention in the transaction described about them, of the guidance which is one of the two counter-values: ﴿They purchase error﴾, which is remaining upon Judaism, after the signs had become clear to them regarding the validity of the prophethood of the Messenger (ﷺ) and that he is the Prophet announced in the Torah and the Gospel. That is, they take error and abandon the guidance they were given, in order to buy a small price of the wreckage of this world.

The omission of mention of what is abandoned is only for the sake of making the matter evident, especially after the aforementioned indication. The expression of that by "purchasing" (ishtira'), which is an expression for exchanging a commodity for a price, that is, taking it as a substitute for it, a taking arising from desire for it and aversion from the other, is for the announcement of the complete eagerness of theirs for error, which ought to be turned away from entirely, and their aversion from guidance, for which competitors compete. In this is a registering of the extremity of the folly of their minds and the utmost baseness of their opinions, which is not hidden, since their condition is depicted in the form of something that hardly anyone of even minimal discernment would engage in, as said by Abu al-Su'ud.

﴿And they wish that you would go astray from the way﴾, that is: they are not content with the straying of themselves, but rather they wish, by what they did of concealing his attributes (ﷺ), that you, O believers, would go astray from the path of truth as they went astray, and they love that you would disbelieve in what has been sent down to you of guidance and beneficial knowledge.

The discussion of the words of His exalted saying:

﴿And Allah knows best your enemies. And sufficient is Allah as protector, and sufficient is Allah as helper.﴾ [4:45]

﴿And Allah knows best﴾ i.e., better than you, ﴿your enemies﴾ i.e., while He has already informed you of their enmity toward you and what they intend for you. So beware of them, do not seek their counsel in your affairs, and do not consult them. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as protector﴾ who takes charge of your affairs, ﴿and sufficient is Allah as helper﴾ who gives you victory. That is: trust in His guardianship and His support rather than theirs, (p-1276) and do not take as allies anyone other than Him. Or it means: do not concern yourselves with them or with the evil they inflict upon you, for He, exalted is He, will suffice you against their plotting and their harm. In this there is both a promise and a warning.

**The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying:**

﴿Among those who are Jews, there are those who distort words from their places, and they say, "We hear and we disobey," and "Hear, without being made to hear," and "Ra'ina," twisting their tongues and slandering the religion. Had they said, "We hear and we obey, and hear, and look at us," it would have been better for them and more upright. But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe, except a few.﴾ [4:46]

﴿Among those who are Jews﴾ explains the relative pronoun in ﴿those who were given a portion of the Scripture﴾ [An-Nisa: 44]. It encompasses the People of the Two Books (the Jews and the Christians). Between them is inserted what has been inserted, for greater emphasis on specifying the object of censure and wonder, and for a swift warning to the believers to stay away from them, to avoid mixing with them, and to be concerned with leading them to trust in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and to be content with His protection and support.

His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿they distort words from their places﴾, together with what is conjoined to it, is an explanation of the aforementioned purchasing (of error), and a detailing of the kinds of their misguidance. In the noble composition, the method of explanation after vagueness and detailing after generality has been observed, aiming at an increase in confirmation required by the situation. This was stated by Abu al-Su'ud.

Imam Ibn Kathir said: His saying, ﴿they distort words from their places﴾, means that they take it in other than its (intended) interpretation, and explain it in other than what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, intended, deliberately and by fabrication.

Al-Allamah al-Razi said: Regarding the manner of distortion, there are several aspects:

The first: they used to replace a word with another word.

Then he said:

The second: the meaning of distortion is casting false doubts and corrupt interpretations, and diverting a word from its true meaning to a false meaning through verbal tricks, as the people of innovation do in our time with verses that contradict their doctrines. This is the most correct view.

The third: they used to enter upon the Prophet (ﷺ) and ask him about a matter, and he would inform them so that they might act upon it. But when they left his presence, they distorted his words. End of quotation.

(p-1277) Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said in *Ighathat al-Lahfan*: There is disagreement about the Torah that is in their hands: is it altered, or did the alteration occur in the interpretation and not in the revelation? There are three opinions:

One group said: all of it, or most of it, is altered. Some of them went to extremes, to the point of saying: it is permissible to use it for cleaning after excretion.

A group of the imams of hadith, jurisprudence and theology said: the alteration occurred only in the interpretation.

Al-Bukhari said in his *Sahih*: "They distort" means "they remove." No one removes a word from the books of Allah, but they interpret it in other than its intended meaning. This is also the choice of al-Razi.

I heard our shaykh say: a dispute arose among the scholars. One of them permitted this view and rejected the other, so he was denounced. Then he presented fifteen reports supporting it. Among the arguments of these people is that the Torah has spread across the eastern and western parts of the earth, and has dispersed to the south and north, and no one knows the number of its copies except Allah. Therefore it is impossible for people to have conspired to alter and change all those copies, so that no copy remains on earth except an altered one. This is something reason rejects. They said: Allah has said to His Prophet, ﴿Say, "Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful."﴾ [Al 'Imran: 93]. They said: They have agreed on abandoning the obligation of stoning, and they could not change it from the Torah. Therefore, when they read it before the Prophet (ﷺ), the reader placed his hand over the verse of stoning, and Abdullah ibn Salam said to him: "Lift your hand." He lifted it, and beneath it the verse was shining.

A group took a middle position and said: some small things have been added to it and changed. Our shaykh chose this view in *al-Jawab al-Sahih liman Baddala Din al-Masih*. He said: This is like what is in their Torah: that Allah, Glory be to Him, said to Ibrahim: "Sacrifice your son, your firstborn, or your only one, Ishaq." Then he said: I say: the addition is false for ten reasons. Then he enumerated them. Return to it. Imam Siddiq Khan has transmitted this from him here, so consult his *Fath al-Rahman* in his tafsir.

(p-1278) A subtle point:

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask: why is ﴿from their places﴾ said here, while in al-Ma'idah it is ﴿from after their places﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 41]? I say: As for ﴿from their places﴾, it is according to what we explained, namely removing it from its place, which the wisdom of Allah required placing it in, by what their desires required, replacing it with something else in its place. As for ﴿from after their places﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 41], the meaning is that it had places it was fitting for it to occupy, but when they distorted it, they left it like a stranger who has no place after its places and its dwellings. The two meanings are close.

Al-Razi said: Allah mentioned here ﴿from their places﴾, and in al-Ma'idah ﴿from after their places﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 41]. The difference is that if we explain distortion by false interpretations, then here His saying ﴿they distort words from after their places﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 41] means that they mention corrupt interpretations of those texts, and there is no indication that they remove that word from the Book. But the verse mentioned in Surat al-Ma'idah indicates that they combined both matters: they mentioned corrupt interpretations and also removed the word from the Book. So His saying ﴿they distort the words﴾ refers to false interpretation, and His saying ﴿from after their places﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 41] refers to removing it from the Book.

Al-Nasir said in *al-Intisaf*: The apparent meaning is that the distorted words in this context are intended as in ﴿without being made to hear﴾ and ﴿Ra'ina﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 104]. Here the intention is not the alteration of rulings. Its placement between the two words, between His saying ﴿they distort﴾ and His saying ﴿twisting their tongues﴾, and what is intended is also a visible and clear distortion, of which these two words and their like are examples. As for Surat al-Ma'idah, the apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that by "words" (kalim) there is meant the rulings, and their distortion and alteration is like their replacing stoning with flogging. Do you not see that He followed it with His saying ﴿If you are given this, take it, and if you are not given it, beware﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 41]? Because the intended meaning of "words" differs between the two surahs, in Surat al-Ma'idah it was said: ﴿they distort the words from after their places﴾, that is, they transfer it from the place where Allah placed it, so it became its home and abode, to another place, so it remained like a stranger, lamented, of whom it is said: "This is a stranger, after his places and abodes." This meaning is not found in words like ﴿Ra'ina﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 104] and ﴿without being made to hear﴾, and even if it is found in them at a distance, the linguistic placement is not as significant in its transfer from its place as the legal placement. Had this transfer not involved mockery and derision, its matter would not have been so grave. Therefore here it came as ﴿they distort the words from their places﴾, not accompanied by what accompanied the first in the form of lamentation. And Allah knows best. End of quotation.

Al-Allamah Abu al-Su'ud said: The intended meaning of distortion here is either what is in the Torah specifically, or what is more general than that, including the well-known statements uttered by them during their dialogue with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which will be mentioned later. There is no room for restricting it to those statements alone, by making the conjunction of His saying, ﴿and they say, "We hear and we disobey"﴾ and what follows it an explanatory conjunction to what precedes it. This would require that the ruling of the conditional clause that follows and what comes after it be restricted to those statements, without any reference to their distortion of the Torah, although that is the greatest of their crimes. Their saying ﴿we hear and we disobey﴾ should be taken in its absolute sense, without restriction to a time or place, and without specifying one matter over another. Rather, it should be understood in the more general sense than the literal statement, including what their obstinacy and stubbornness express. That is: they say in every matter that contradicts their corrupt desires, whether in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ) or not, by tongue of speech or of state: ﴿we hear and we disobey﴾, out of obstinacy or to make their opposition certain. End of quotation.

Ibn Kathir said: And they say: ﴿We hear﴾, that is: we have heard what you have said, O Muhammad, and we will not obey you in it. This is how Mujahid and Ibn Zayd explained it, and it is the intended meaning. This is more eloquent in expressing their disbelief and obstinacy, and that they turn away from the Book of Allah after having understood it, while they know what sin and punishment are upon them for that.

﴿And hear, without being made to hear﴾ is conjoined to ﴿we hear and we disobey﴾ and falls under the statement, that is: they say that during their address to him, peace be upon him, specifically. It is a statement with two faces, capable of evil: it may be taken to mean "Hear," while you are one who is not made to hear any speech at all, by deafness or death, that is, one upon whom it is prayed: "May you not hear!" Or one who is not made to hear words you would be pleased with. And it is capable of good: it may be taken to mean "Hear from us, while you are made to hear nothing disliked." They used to address the Prophet (ﷺ) with this as mockery of him, may the curse of Allah be upon them, showing him the latter meaning while concealing the former, reassured by it.

﴿Ra'ina﴾ is conjoined to what precedes it, that is: they say this too during their address to him (ﷺ). It is also a word with two faces, capable of good, by taking it to mean "Watch over us and look at us, and we will speak to you," and capable of evil, by taking it as similar to a Hebrew word they used to insult one another with, or as abuse by ignorance, that is, foolishness. In sum, mocking the religion and deriding the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they used to speak to him with words capable of two meanings, intending by them insult and humiliation, while showing by them respect and honor.

﴿Twisting their tongues﴾: that is, twisting with them, and diverting speech from one aspect to another, and distorting it. That is, they twist the truth into falsehood with their tongues, when they place ﴿Ra'ina﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 104] in the place of ﴿look at us﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 104], and ﴿without being made to hear﴾ in the place of "may you not be made to hear anything disliked." Or they twist with their tongues what they conceal of insult into what they display of respect, as hypocrisy.

If you ask: how did they come with the ambiguous, two-faced statement after they had openly said, ﴿we hear and we disobey﴾? I say: All the disbelievers used to confront him with disbelief and disobedience, and did not confront him with abuse and evil supplication. It is possible that they said this among themselves, and it is possible that they did not utter it at all, but since they did not believe, they were treated as if they had uttered it. Thus it is in al-Kashshaf.

The origin of ﴿la'yan﴾ is la-wayan, because from "lawaytu" (I twisted), the waw was assimilated into the ya' because it preceded it with sukun. Similar to it is "al-tayy" (folding).

﴿And slandering the religion﴾: that is, defaming it with mockery and derision. Both words are in the accusative of causation governed by ﴿they say﴾, with reference to its connection to the last two statements, that is: they say that in order to turn speech away from its proper sense toward abuse and slander of the religion. Or they are in the accusative of circumstance, that is: twisting and slandering the religion. This was stated by Abu al-Su'ud.

﴿Had they said﴾: that is, when they heard what was recited to them of His commands, Exalted is He: ﴿We hear and we obey﴾, that is, instead of their saying: ﴿We hear and we disobey﴾. The word "say" here, as in the preceding, is more general, whether by tongue of speech or by tongue of state. ﴿And hear﴾: that is, had they said when addressing the Prophet (ﷺ) instead of their saying just "Hear" without adding ﴿without being made to hear﴾, which is capable of evil, ﴿and look at us﴾, meaning instead of their saying ﴿Ra'ina﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 104], which is capable of the corrupt meaning as previously mentioned. ﴿It would have been better for them and more upright﴾, in this world by preserving their blood and the elevation of their rank through the encompassing of the heavenly books, and in the Hereafter by doubled reward. This was stated by al-Mahayimi.

قال أبو السعود: وصيغةُ التفضيل إمّا على بابها، واعتبارُ أصلِ الفضلِ في المفضَّلِ عليه بناءً على اعتقادِهم، أو بطريق التهكُّم. وإمّا بمعنى اسمِ الفاعل. ﴿ولكن لعنهم الله بكفرهم﴾ أي: ولكن لم يقولوا ذلك، واستمرّوا على كفرهم، فطردهم الله عن رحمته وأبعدهم عن الهدى بسبب كفرهم. ﴿فلا يؤمنون إلا قليلا﴾ منصوبٌ على الاستثناء من "لعنهم"، أي: ولكن لعنهم الله إلا فريقًا قليلًا منهم، آمنوا فلم يُلعنوا. أو على الوصفية لمصدرٍ محذوف، أي: إلا إيمانًا قليلًا، أي: ضعيفًا رَكيكًا لا يُعبأ به، فإنهم كانوا يؤمنون بالله والتوراةِ وموسى، ويكفرون ببقية المرسلين وكتبِهم المنزَّلة.

ورجّح أبو علي الفارسي (Abu 'Ali al-Farisi) هذا، قال: لأنّ "قليلًا" لفظٌ مفرد، ولو أُريد به (ناسٌ) لجُمع، نحو قوله: ﴿إن هؤلاء لشرذمةٌ قليلون﴾ [الشعراء: 54] [الشُّعَراء: 54]. ويمكن أن يُجاب عنه بأنه قد جاء فعيلٌ مفردًا والمراد به الجمع، قال تعالى: ﴿وحسن أولئك رفيقًا﴾ [النساء: 69] [النِّساء: من الآية 69]، وقال: ﴿ولا يسأل حميمٌ حميمًا﴾ [المعارج: 10] [المَعارِج: 10] (يُبَصَّرونَهُم: "يُرَوْنَهم"). أفاده الرازي (al-Razi). وقد جُوِّز على هذا أن يُراد بالقلّة العدمُ بالكلية، كقوله:

*قليلُ التشكّي للمُهمِّ يُصيبُه* *كثيرُ الهوى شتّى النوى والمسالك*

(p. 1282) أي: هو كثيرُ الهمّ مختلفُ الوجوه والطرق، لا يقف أملُه على فنٍّ واحد، بل يتجاوزه إلى فنونٍ مختلفة، صبورٌ على النوائب لا يكادُ يتشكّى منها، فاستعمل لفظ (قليل) وأراد به نفيَ الكل.

أو منصوبٌ على الاستثناء من فاعل "لا يؤمنون"، أي: فلا يؤمن منهم إلا نفرٌ قليل. وأما قولُ الخفاجي (al-Khafaji): كان الوجهُ فيه الرفعَ على البدل، لأنه من كلامٍ غيرِ موجِب، وقولُ أبي السعود: بأن فيه نسبةَ القرّاء إلى الاتفاق على غير المختار، فمردودٌ بأنّ النصبَ عربيٌّ جيّد، وقد قُرئ به في السبعِ في (قليلٌ) من قوله تعالى: ﴿ما فعلوه إلا قليلٌ منهم﴾ [النساء: 66] [النِّساء: من الآية 66]، وفي (امرأتُك) من قوله تعالى: ﴿ولا يلتفتْ منكم أحدٌ إلا امرأتَك﴾ [هود: 81] [هود: من الآية 81]، كما قاله ابن هشام (Ibn Hisham) في التوضيح.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 4, verse 47:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿O you who were given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their backs, or curse them as We cursed the People of the Sabbath. And the command of Allah is ever executed.﴾ [4:47]

﴿O you who were given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down﴾ meaning the Qur'an. ﴿Confirming what is with you﴾ i.e., agreeing with the Torah. ﴿Before We obliterate faces﴾ i.e., erase the outline of their forms: the eyes, eyebrows, nose and mouth. Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: "Its obliteration is that they become blind."

﴿And turn them back on their backs﴾ i.e., We will make them in the shape of their backs, which are the napes, obliterated like them, as a recompense for disbelief; so the fa' (فَ) here indicates causation (tasbib). Or: We reverse them after the obliteration, returning the faces to the place of the napes and the napes to the place of the faces; and only the more severe of the two is mentioned, so the fa' indicates sequence (ta'qib).

Al-Razi said: This meaning was made a punishment by Allah because it involves disfigurement of creation, mutilation and disgrace, for at that point grief and regret become great.

﴿Or curse them as We cursed the People of the Sabbath﴾ i.e., or We will do to them something more severe than that, namely expelling them from humanity by a total transformation (maskh) as a recompense for their transgression by rejecting faith, just as We humiliated their predecessors, the People of the Sabbath, as a recompense for their transgression against the Sabbath by resorting to trickery in hunting; so We transformed them into apes.

﴿And the command of Allah﴾ i.e., what He commands ﴿is ever executed﴾ i.e., it is effective and will certainly occur. There is another interpretation of the verse, namely that the intended meaning of obliterating faces is figurative, namely diverting them from the truth, turning them back to falsehood, and their returning from the white path to the way of misguidance, rushing and walking backwards on their backs.

Ibn Kathir said: This is like what some of them said regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have put on their necks shackles, and they reach to the chins, so they are held up [with heads raised]﴾ [36:8] ﴿And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them, so they do not see﴾ [36:9]: i.e., this is an evil example that Allah set for them in their misguidance and their being barred from guidance.

Mujahid said: ﴿Before We obliterate faces﴾ means: from the path of truth; ﴿and turn them back on their backs﴾ i.e., into misguidance.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Something similar was related from Ibn 'Abbas and al-Hasan.

As-Suddi said: ﴿and turn them back on their backs﴾ — We prevent them from the truth, returning them as disbelievers.

Al-Razi said: The purpose according to this is to explain their being cast into kinds of abandonment and darkness of misguidance. A parallel to it is His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart and that to Him you will be gathered﴾ [8:24].

The summary of the matter regarding it: man, at the beginning of his creation, became accustomed to this sensible world; then when he reflects and worships, it is as if he travels from the world of the sensible to the world of the intelligible. In front of him is the world of the intelligible, and behind him is the world of the sensible. So the forsaken one is the one who turns back from in front of him to behind him, as He said in describing them: ﴿Their heads bowed down﴾ [32:12].

Then al-Razi said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: This threat has already befallen the Jews and passed. He interpreted it as referring to the expulsion of Qurayzah and an-Nadir to Syria, so Allah turned their faces back on their backs when they returned to Adhri'at and Ariha in the land of Syria, from where they had come. And the "obliteration of faces" according to this interpretation may have two meanings:

The first: making their form ugly; it is said: "Allah obliterated his form," like His saying: "May Allah disfigure his face."

The second: removing their traces from the lands of the Arabs and erasing their conditions from them.

There is also another interpretation, namely that the intended meaning of "faces" is the notables, with obliteration meaning change in general, i.e., before We change the conditions of their notables, depriving them of their honour and prestige, and clothing them in humiliation and reversal.

Some of them said: The more apparent reading is to take His saying "or curse them" etc. as the common meaning of cursing. He said: Do you not see His saying: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that as to recompense from Allah? Those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He became angry and made of them apes and swine﴾ [5:60]? In it He separated cursing from their transformation into apes and swine.

I say: It is not hidden that all the interpretations mentioned, other than the first, are not supported by the context of intensifying the threat and generalizing the warning, for what is immediately understood from the wording is the literal meaning, and one does not turn to the figurative unless the literal is impossible, and it is not impossible here. Likewise, what is immediately understood from "cursing" — compared to the cursing of the People of the Sabbath — is transformation (maskh), and this is what the eloquence of the revelation requires, for in it there is an ascent to the more dreadful threat. We do not deny that these interpretations may be included in the wording of the verse; rather the dispute is over the claim that they are intended to the exclusion of what precedes them. The truth is that what is immediately understood from the noble text is the first, because it is more effective in deterrence.

This is supported by what is related: that Ka'b al-Ahbar embraced Islam when he heard this verse. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related it, and its wording after its chain is: From Abu Idris 'A'idhullah al-Khawlani, who said: Abu Muslim al-Jalili was Ka'b's teacher, and he would blame him for his delay in coming to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: So he sent him to look and see whether he was indeed [the Prophet]. Ka'b said: I rode until I came to Madinah, and suddenly there was a reciter reciting the Qur'an saying: ﴿O you who were given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their backs﴾. So I performed ghusl, and I began to touch my face out of fear that it would be obliterated. Then I embraced Islam.

It was also related by other routes, similarly.

If it is said: The indicator of figurative meaning is the non-occurrence of what was threatened. The answer: Its non-occurrence does not determine that the figurative meaning is intended, since there is no indication in the verse that its occurrence is certain if they do not believe. Even if this were understood from it at first glance, their faith after it would be faith under compulsion and necessity, which contradicts legal responsibility, since Allah's custom has not been like this. Rather, the noble text in this context is initially open to the certainty of what is threatened occurring, or to its occurrence being contingent upon His command and will, and this is what is intended, as His saying indicates: ﴿And the command of Allah is ever executed﴾ [33:37], i.e., what He commands and wills to occur. And if the threat is tied to His command, glorified is He, then He may carry it out in its literal sense, or He may turn it to what He knows best. However, the revelation of the verse in this form of address, which is immediately understood as unconditional occurrence, is for greater intimidation and a deterrent against opposing the command. This is how it has appeared to us now, and it is closer than what the exegetes here have followed, that the punishment is awaited, or that it is conditional on non-belief, and other such views. Al-'Allamah Abu al-Su'ud has refuted all of these, then chose that the intended threat is the otherworldly one, saying: Because its occurrence has not become clear. This too is distant, for such address is not apt to intend the otherworldly threat, especially since the second clause with which they were threatened, namely cursing them as the People of the Sabbath, had a worldly punishment. So the view we have established is correct. The verse resembles in its threat the verse of Ya-Sin, namely His saying: ﴿And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes, and they would race to the path, but how could they see?﴾ [36:66] ﴿And if We willed, We would have transformed them in their places, so they would not be able to proceed or return﴾ [36:67]. Indeed, this (verse) is for me an explanation of that, and the Qur'an explains one part of it by another, so the obscurity is cleared, and praise be to Allah.

A subtle point:

The pronoun in (نَلْعَنَهُمْ) refers to the owners of the faces, or to ﴿those who﴾ according to the manner of iltifat (shift of address), or to "the faces" if by them is meant the notables.

**On the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:**
﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills. And whoever associates partners with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin.﴾ [4:48]

﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him.﴾ Abu al-Su'ud said: This is a resumed statement, brought to confirm the warning that precedes it and to affirm the obligation of compliance with the command of faith, by explaining that forgiveness is impossible without it. They used to do what they did of distortion (tahrif) and still hoped for forgiveness, as in His words: ﴿Then there succeeded them an heir who inherited the Book, [who] takes the goods of this lower world and says, "It will be forgiven for us"﴾ [al-A'raf: 169] [al-A'raf: part of 169], meaning: by means of distortion. ﴿and says, "It will be forgiven for us"﴾ [al-A'raf: 169]. The intended meaning of "shirk" (association of partners) is absolute disbelief (kufr), which encompasses the disbelief of the Jews in an initial sense, since the Law has explicitly stated the association of all the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab), and has decreed the eternal abiding of the categories of disbelievers in the Fire. Its revelation regarding the Jews, as Muqatil said, is the most suitable to the context of the noble composition, but its context does not require that it be restricted to their disbelief. Its inclusion of them is sufficient and certain. Indeed, there is no basis for it at all, since it would imply the permissibility of forgiving forms of disbelief less severe than theirs. That is, Allah does not forgive disbelief for one who is characterized by it without repentance and faith, because the legislative wisdom requires closing the door to disbelief, and permitting its forgiveness without faith would lead to opening it. Also, the darknesses of disbelief and sins are only veiled by the light of faith; whoever has no faith, nothing of disbelief or sins is forgiven for him. End.

Al-Shihab said: The word "shirk" can mean the belief that Allah has a partner, and it can mean disbelief in general, which is what is intended here. This has been stated explicitly in His words in Surat al-Bayyinah: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 6] [al-Bayyinah: part of 6], so no doubt remains about its generality. End.

Al-Razi said: This verse indicates that the Jew is called a mushrik (one who associates partners) in the usage of the Law, and two arguments point to this:

The first: The verse indicates that everything other than shirk is forgiven. If Judaism were different from shirk, it would have to be forgiven by the ruling of this verse. But by consensus (ijma', the agreement of the scholars) it is not forgiven. This indicates that it is included under the name of shirk.

[p-1288]

The second: The connection of this verse with what precedes it is because it contains a threat to the Jews. If Judaism were not included under the name of shirk, the matter would not be this way. If it is said: His words, ﴿Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 69], up to His words, ﴿and those who associated partners﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 82] [al-Ma'idah: part of 82], where the polytheist is conjoined to the Jew, and this requires difference. We say: The difference is established through the linguistic meaning, and the unity is established through the legal meaning, and we must resort to what we have mentioned, to avoid contradiction. End.

A subtle point:
Abu al-Baqa' said: Shirk has types:
Shirk of independence (shirk al-istiqlal), which is affirming two independent gods, like the shirk of the Magians.
Shirk of partition (shirk al-tab'id), which is composing God from gods, like the shirk of the Christians.
Shirk of proximity (shirk al-taqrib), which is worshipping other than Allah in order to bring oneself nearer to Allah, like the shirk of the earlier pre-Islamic people.
Shirk of imitation (shirk al-taqlid), which is worshipping other than Allah following others, like the shirk of the later pre-Islamic people.
Shirk of causes (shirk al-asbab), which is attributing causal effect to customary causes, like the shirk of the philosophers, the naturalists, and those who followed them in that.
Shirk of aims (shirk al-aghrad), which is acting for other than Allah.
The ruling for the first four is disbelief by consensus. The ruling for the sixth is sin without disbelief, by consensus. The ruling for the fifth is detailed. Whoever says that customary causes affect by their own nature has had the consensus reported regarding his disbelief, and whoever says that they affect by a power Allah has placed in them is a sinner. End.

﴿and He forgives what is less than that﴾, meaning: what is less than shirk, of sins, minor or major, ﴿for whomever He wills﴾, out of His bounty and kindness.

Ibn Jarir said: This verse has made clear that every person who commits a major sin is subject to the will of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. If He wills, He pardons him, and if He wills, He punishes him for it, so long as it is not shirk with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Its apparent meaning is that forgiveness from Him, Glorified is He, occurs for whomever His will requires, out of His bounty and mercy, even if that sinner does not repent. The Mu'tazilah restricted this to repentance. His words, Exalted is He, have already preceded: ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾ [al-Nisa': 31] [al-Nisa': part of 31], and this indicates that Allah, Glorified is He, forgives the misdeeds of those who avoid the major sins, so the one who avoids major sins is among those for whom Allah has willed the forgiveness of their misdeeds. For this reason al-Razi said: This verse is among the strongest proofs for us regarding the pardoning of the people of major sins. Then he refined the aspects of the argument, among them: that everything other than shirk includes major sin before repentance; and among them: that forgiveness of a major sin after repentance and forgiveness of a minor sin are definitively established and are not conditioned on the will; so it is obligatory that the forgiveness mentioned in this verse is the forgiveness of a major sin before repentance, and that is what is sought.

Al-Zamakhshari interpreted this verse according to his school: the negated verb and the affirmed verb are both directed to His words, ﴿for whomever He wills﴾, according to the rule of tanazu' (grammatical dispute, where two verbs share one complement), as if it were said: Indeed Allah does not forgive for whomever He wills shirk, and He forgives for whomever He wills what is less than shirk, with the meaning that the first refers to one who does not repent and the second to one who repents. He said: The parallel of this is your saying: Indeed the commander does not give the dinar and gives the qintar to whomever he wills, meaning he does not give the dinar to one who does not deserve it, and he gives the qintar to one who deserves it. End.

Naser al-Din said in al-Intisaf: The creed of the People of the Sunnah is that shirk is absolutely not forgiven, and what is less than it of major sins is forgiven for whomever Allah wills to forgive him. This is with the absence of repentance. As for with repentance, both are forgiven. The verse was revealed concerning one who did not repent, and no repentance is mentioned in it, as you see. Therefore Allah, Exalted is He, absolutely negated the forgiveness of shirk and affirmed the forgiveness of what is less than it, conjoined with the will, as you see. This is the way the verse applies to the creed of the People of the Sunnah. As for the Qadariyyah, they assume an equivalence between shirk and what is less than it of major sins, in that each of the two types is not forgiven without repentance, and Allah did not will to forgive either of them except for those who repent. When al-Zamakhshari presented this belief to this verse, the verse rejected it and disowned it, since forgiveness is negated in it regarding shirk and affirmed for what is less than it, conjoined with the will. As for the possibility that what is meant by both is the one who does not repent, there is no basis for the preference between them by tying forgiveness in one to the will and tying it in the other absolutely, since they are equal in the impossibility of forgiveness. As for the possibility that what is meant by both is the one who repents, he has said regarding shirk "He does not forgive," yet the one who repents from shirk is forgiven. At that point al-Zamakhshari began to cut one of them off from the other, making what is meant with shirk the absence of repentance and with major sins the repentance, so that the verse falls in line with his belief, and so he burdens it with two matters that it does not bear:
The first: attributing repentance to the will, though it is not mentioned, and there is no evidence for it in what he mentioned. Also, if it were intended, it would be the cause that necessitates forgiveness according to their claim by reason, and the will could not be connected to its opposite according to their opinion in reason. So how is it fitting to remain silent about mentioning what is the foundation and the cause, and to mention what has no bearing on this corrupt belief?
The second: that after establishing repentance, he passed judgment and restricted it to one of the two categories without the other. This is nothing but making the Qur'an subordinate to opinion. We seek refuge in Allah from that.

As for the Qadariyyah, with this belief, the well-known proverb applies to them: "The master gives, and the slave withholds," because Allah, Exalted is He, clearly declares His generosity in forgiving the one who persists in major sins, if He wills, while they reject this declaration and deem forgiveness impossible on the basis of the principle of what is best and most beneficial (al-aslah wa'l-salah), which is more deserving and entitled to be corrupt. End.

Benefit:
Hadiths related to this noble verse have been transmitted:

The first: From A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The registers with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are three: a register that Allah does not regard at all; a register from which Allah leaves nothing; and a register that Allah does not forgive.

As for the register [p-1291] that Allah does not forgive, it is shirk with Allah. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾, and so on, and He said: ﴿Indeed, whoever associates partners with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 72] [al-Ma'idah: part of 72].

As for the register that Allah does not regard at all, it is the servant's wronging of himself in what is between him and his Lord, such as fasting a day he abandoned or a prayer he abandoned. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forgives that and overlooks it if He wills.

As for the register from which Allah leaves nothing, it is the wronging of servants of one another, retaliation without doubt."" Narrated by Imam Ahmad, and he alone transmitted it.

The second: From Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Wrongdoing is of three kinds: a wrong that Allah does not forgive, a wrong that Allah forgives, and a wrong from which Allah leaves nothing.

As for the wrong that Allah does not forgive, it is shirk; and He said: ﴿Indeed, shirk is a tremendous wrong﴾ [Luqman: 13] [Luqman: part of 13].

As for the wrong that Allah forgives, it is the servants' wronging of themselves in what is between them and their Lord.

As for the wrong that He does not leave, it is the servants' wronging of one another, until retaliation is exacted from one for another." Narrated by Abu Bakr al-Bazzar in his Musnad.

The third: From Mu'awiyah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Every sin, Allah may forgive it, except a man who dies a disbeliever, or a man who kills a believer deliberately." Narrated by Imam Ahmad and al-Nasa'i.

The fourth: From Abu Dharr: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'No servant says, "There is no god but Allah," and then dies upon that, except that he enters Paradise.' I said: 'Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals?' He said: 'Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals.' I said: 'Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals?' He said: 'Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals' — three times — then he said in the fourth: 'In spite of the nose of Abu Dharr.'

Abu Dharr went out dragging his garment, saying: 'Even if the nose of Abu Dharr is rubbed in the dust.'

Abu Dharr used to narrate this afterwards and say: 'Even if the nose of Abu Dharr is rubbed in the dust.'" Narrated by Imam Ahmad and the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim).

In a narration of the two Shaykhs from Abu Dharr: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Gabriel said to me: 'Give glad tidings to your nation that whoever dies without associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise.' I said: 'O Gabriel! Even if he steals and even if he commits adultery?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Even if he steals and even if he commits adultery?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Even if he steals and even if he commits adultery?' He said: 'Yes, even if he drinks wine.'"

The fifth: From Jabir, who said: "A Bedouin came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! What are the two things that necessitate?' He said: 'Whoever dies without associating anything with Allah enters Paradise, and whoever dies associating partners with Him enters the Fire.'" Narrated by Muslim, and by Abd ibn Humayd in his Musnad.

The sixth: From Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever dies without associating anything with Allah enters Paradise." Narrated by Imam Ahmad.

The seventh: From Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Whoever knows that I am capable of forgiving sins, I will forgive him and I do not mind.'" Narrated by al-Tabarani.

The eighth: From Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever Allah promises a reward for a deed, He will certainly fulfill it for him; and whoever He threatens with punishment for a deed, then He has the choice regarding it." Narrated by al-Bazzar and Abu Ya'la.

**Ninth:** From Ibn ʿUmar, who said: "We, the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), did not doubt that the killer of a soul, the one who consumes the property of an orphan, the false witness, and the one who severs the ties of kinship would be (destined for the Fire), until this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾. So we refrained from testifying (that such people were lost)." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir.

In a narration of Ibn Abi Hatim: "When we heard it, we held back from testifying, and we deferred the matters to Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

**Tenth:** From ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, upon him be peace, who said: "Nothing in the Qur'an is dearer to me than this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who said: "A hasan gharib hadith."

**Eleventh:** From Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah, the Exalted, said: O son of Adam, as long as you call upon Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you for what you have done, and I will not mind.

O son of Adam, if your sins reached the clouds of the sky and then you sought My forgiveness, I would forgive you, and I would not mind.

O son of Adam, if you came to Me with earth's worth of sins and then met Me without associating anything with Me, I would bring you earth's worth of forgiveness." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who said: "A hasan gharib hadith, which we know only through this route."

Imam Ahmad narrated something similar from Abu Dharr, and his wording from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: O My servant, as long as you worship Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you for what you have done. O My servant, if you meet Me with an earth's worth of sin, provided you did not associate anything with Me, I will meet you with an earth's worth of forgiveness."

The reports on this matter are abundant, and this amount suffices.

﴿And whoever associates partners with Allah has indeed fabricated a tremendous sin﴾, meaning: he has invented and fabricated, committing a sin whose magnitude cannot be measured, and in comparison to which all other sins are considered trivial. Therefore, forgiveness definitively does not attach to it.

Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his book *al-Jawab al-Kafi* (The Sufficient Answer): "Associating partners with the Lord, exalted is He, is of two kinds: association with Him in His names and attributes, and setting up other gods alongside Him; and association with Him in one's dealings with Him. The second kind may not necessarily require entry into the Fire, even though it nullifies the deed in which one associated others with Allah. This kind is the greatest of all sins, and it includes saying about Allah without knowledge concerning His creation and His command. Whoever is among the people of these sins has disputed with Allah, glorified and exalted is He, His lordship and His dominion, and has set up a rival (*nidd*) for Him. This is the greatest sin in the sight of Allah, and no deed benefits alongside it."

He then said after that: "The unveiling of this matter is that it is said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent His messengers, revealed His books, and created the heavens and the earth, so that He may be known, worshipped, and declared one; so that the religion is entirely for Him, all obedience is to Him, and the call is to Him. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 56]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth﴾ [Al-Hijr: 85]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah is the One who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof; the command descends among them, that you may know that Allah is capable of all things and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾ [At-Talaq: 12]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah has made the Kaaba, the Sacred House, a means of stability for the people, and the sacred month, and the sacrificial animals, and the garlands. That is so you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth and that Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 97]. So He, glorified is He, informed that the purpose of creation and command is that He be known through His names and attributes, that He be worshipped alone without partners being associated with Him, (p. 1295) and that people establish justice (*qist*), which is the justice by which the heavens and the earth stand. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿We have certainly sent Our messengers with clear evidences and sent down with them the Scripture and the balance that mankind may maintain justice﴾ [Al-Hadid: 25]. So He, glorified is He, informed that He sent His messengers and revealed His books so that people might establish justice, which is justice. Among the greatest forms of justice is monotheism (*tawhid*); indeed, it is the foundation of justice and its pillar. Association (*shirk*) is a tremendous wrong, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, association is a tremendous injustice﴾ [Luqman: 13]. Thus association is the worst of injustices, and monotheism is the most just of justices. Whatever is most contrary to this purpose is the greatest of the major sins, and their gradation in ranks corresponds to how much they contradict it. Whatever most conforms to this purpose is the most obligatory of obligations and the most required of acts of obedience."

"So reflect deeply on this principle, and consider its details through it, and you will know, through it, the Most Wise of judges and the Most Knowing of knowers, regarding what He prescribed for His servants and what He forbade them, and the differing levels of obedience and disobedience. Since association with Allah is by its very nature contrary to this purpose, and since it is the greatest of the major sins absolutely, Allah forbade Paradise to every associator, made their blood and property lawful to the people of monotheism, and made them slaves to them because they abandoned the performance of His worship. Allah, glorified is He, refused to accept any deed from an associator, or to accept intercession for him, or to answer his supplication in the Hereafter, or to overlook his slip there. For the associator is the most ignorant of the ignorant regarding Allah, since he set up for Him a rival from among His creation, and that is the utmost ignorance of Him, just as it is the utmost wrong toward Him. Although the associator has not wronged his Lord, rather he has wronged himself."

"There arose a question: namely, that the associator intends only to magnify the presence of the Lord, blessed and exalted is He; and that because of His greatness it is not fitting to approach Him except through intermediaries and intercessors, as with the case of kings. So the associator does not intend to belittle the lordship, but intends to magnify it."

"He said: I only worship these intermediaries so that they bring me closer and admit me to Him; He is the one intended, and these are means and intercessors."

(p. 1296) "Why, then, would this degree of association be a cause for His wrath and anger, blessed and exalted is He, and a cause for eternal abiding in the Fire, and a cause for the shedding of the blood of His adherents and the violation of their sanctities and property? From this arises another question: Is it permissible for Allah, glorified is He, to legislate for His servants drawing near to Him through intercessors and intermediaries? If so, the prohibition of this would have been learned only from the Law. Or is it, rather, something ugly in natural disposition and intellect, such that no Law could bring it, but rather the Law came to confirm what natural disposition and intellect already recognize of its ugliness, which is the most ugly of all ugliness? And what is the reason that He does not forgive it, unlike all other sins? As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾. So reflect deeply on this question, gather your heart and mind upon its answer, and do not take it lightly, for by it is distinguished the associators from the monotheists, those who know Allah from those who are ignorant of Him, and the people of Paradise from the people of the Fire."

"We say (and success and support are from Allah, and from Him we seek help and guidance; for whomever Allah guides is truly guided, and whomever He leaves astray has no guide, and none can withhold what He gives or give what He withholds):

Association is of two kinds: association that pertains to the essence of the worshipped one, His names, His attributes, and His acts; and association in His worship and dealings, even if its practitioner believes that He, glorified is He, has no partner in His essence, nor in His attributes, nor in His acts. The first kind of association is of two types:

The first: *shirk al-taʿtil* (associating through negation), which is the worst type of association, like the association of Pharaoh when he said: ﴿And what is the Lord of the worlds?﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 23]. And Allah, exalted is He, said, relating about him that he said: ﴿And Pharaoh said: O Haman, build for me a tower that I may reach the ways﴾ [Ghafir: 36], ﴿the ways of the heavens, so I may look at the God of Moses, though I think he is a liar﴾ [Ghafir: 37]. So association and negation (*taʿtil*) are interrelated: every associator is a negator, and every negator is an associator. However, association does not necessarily entail the root of negation; the associator may acknowledge the Creator, glorified is He, and His attributes, but he has neglected the right of monotheism. The root and foundation of association, to which it returns, is negation, and it is of three kinds:

Negating the created from its Creator; negating the Creator, glorified is He, from His sacred perfection by denying His names, attributes, and acts; and negating His dealings from what is obligatory upon the servant regarding the reality of monotheism.

Among this is the association of the people of *wahdat al-wujud* (the unity of existence), who say: There is no creator and created, nor are there two things here; rather the Transcendent Truth is the very essence of the created, the likened. Also among it is the association of the atheists who hold that the world is eternal and everlasting, and that it was never non-existent at all, but has always been and always will be; and that all events, in their totality, are attributed by them to causes and intermediaries that necessitated their existence, which they call the intellects and the souls.

From here, whoever negated the names, attributes, and acts of the Lord, exalted is He, has associated, among the extremist Jahmiyya and Qaramita, for they affirmed for Him neither name nor attribute. Rather, they made the created more perfect than Him, since the perfection of the essence is by its names and attributes.

* * *

**Section**

The second type: the association of one who sets up another god alongside Him while not negating His names, lordship, and attributes, like the association of the Christians who made Him the third of three, making Jesus a god and his mother a god.

From this is the association of the Magians, who attribute events of good to the Light and events of evil to the Darkness.

From this is the association of the Qadariyya, who hold that the animal is the one who creates its own acts, and that they occur without Allah's will, power, and volition; therefore they were among those resembling the Magians.

From this is the association of the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord: ﴿When Abraham said, "My Lord is He who gives life and causes death," he said, "I give life and cause death"﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 258]. This one made himself a rival to Allah, giving life and causing death by his claim, just as Allah gives life and causes death. Abraham, upon him be peace and the mercy and blessings of Allah, obliged him to follow his own reasoning: that if he could bring the sun from other than the direction in which Allah brings it, then he would be correct. This was not, as some dialecticians claim, a mere shift in argument, but a binding of the argument to its logical conclusion, if it is sound.

From this is the association of many who associate partners with the celestial bodies, making them governing lords of this world, as is the doctrine of the Sabians and others of the associators.

From this is the association of the worshippers of the sun, the worshippers of fire, and others.

Among these people are those who claim that their worshipped one is the true God. Among them are those who claim it is the greatest of the gods. Among them are those who claim it is one god among the gods, and that if it is singled out for worship, devotion, and exclusive attachment, it will turn toward them and show them care.

Among them are those who claim that it is their lesser deity, bringing them closer to the deity above it, and the higher one brings it closer to whoever is above it, until those gods bring it near to Allah, glorified is He. Sometimes intercession multiplies and sometimes it diminishes.

* * *

**Section**

As for association in worship, it is easier than this and lighter in matter. It arises from one who believes that there is no god but Allah, that none harms, benefits, gives, or withholds except Allah, and that there is no god besides Him and no lord other than Him; but he does not sincerely devote his dealings and worship to Allah. Rather, he works for the sake of his own self's desire at times, for the pursuit of worldly things at times, and for the pursuit of elevated rank, status, and standing among people at other times. So there is a share of his deed and effort for Allah, a share for his self, his desire, and his passions, a share for Satan, and a share for the people. This is the state of most people, and it is the association about which the Prophet (ﷺ) said, as narrated by Ibn Hibban in his *Sahih*: "Association in this nation is more hidden than the crawling of an ant." They said: "How can we be saved from it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Say: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from associating anything with You knowingly, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I do not know."

Thus all showing off (*riyaʾ*) is association. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: I am only a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your God is one God. So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous work and not associate anything in the worship of his Lord﴾ [Al-Kahf: 110].

(p-١٢٩٩) That is, just as He is the one God, with no god besides Him, so likewise worship should be directed to Him alone. Just as He is singular in divinity, He must be singled out in servitude. Thus righteous deeds are those free from *riya'* (showing off to people), and bound by the *Sunnah* (the Prophet's way). It was among the supplications of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him: "O God, make all my deeds righteous, make them purely for Your sake, and do not allow anyone any share in them." This *shirk* (associating partners with God) in worship nullifies the deed, and one may be punished for it if the deed was obligatory, for it places him in the position of one who did not perform it, so he is punished for abandoning the command. God, glorified is He, only commanded that He be worshipped sincerely. He said: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship God, being sincere to Him in religion, inclining toward truth﴾ [Al-Bayyinah: 5].

Whoever is not sincere to God in his worship has not done what he was commanded. Rather, what he has done is something other than what was commanded, so it is neither valid nor accepted from him. God says: "I am the most independent of partners in need of association. Whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his association."

This *shirk* is divided into that which is forgiven and that which is not forgiven, and into major and minor. The first type is divided into the lesser and the greater, and none of it is forgiven.

Among it is associating others with God in love and veneration, by loving the created being as one loves God. This is of the *shirk* that God does not forgive, and it is the *shirk* of which He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And among people are those who take, besides God, equals (rivals)﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 165], the verse.

The companions of this *shirk* said to their gods, when they were gathered in Hellfire: ﴿By God, we were certainly in clear error, when we equated you with the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 97–98]. It is known that they did not equate them with Him, glorified is He, in creation, provision, giving death and life, sovereignty and power. They only equated them with Him in love, in deifying them, in submission to them and humbling themselves before them. This is the utmost ignorance and injustice. How can one who was created from dust be equated with the Lord of lords? How can slaves be equated with the Owner of necks? How can one who is poor in his essence, weak in his essence, incapable in his essence, and needy in his essence, who has nothing of himself except non-existence, be equated with the Self-sufficient in His essence, the Powerful in His essence, whose self-sufficiency, power, dominion, existence, beneficence, knowledge, mercy, and absolute perfect completeness are inherent in His essence? What injustice is uglier than this? What judgment is more unjust than this? Because he made equal to the Incomparable with His creation, as He said: ﴿Praise be to God who created the heavens and the earth and made the darkness and the light; yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ [Al-An'am: 1]. The polytheist equated the One who created the heavens and the earth and made the darkness and light with one who does not possess for himself or others an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth. How great is this "justice" that contains the greatest and ugliest injustice!

* *

**Section**

Following this *shirk* is associating others with Him in statements, actions, intentions and wills. *Shirk* in actions includes prostrating to other than Him, circumambulating other than His House, shaving the head as an act of servitude and submission to other than Him, kissing stones other than the Black Stone, which is "the right hand of God on earth," or kissing graves, touching them for blessing, and prostrating to them. The Prophet ﷺ cursed those who take the graves of prophets and righteous people as places of worship in which they pray. How then is the case of one who takes graves as idols that he worships besides God? In the two *Sahihs* it is related from him that he said: "The curse of God is upon the Jews and Christians who took the graves of their prophets as places of worship."

In the *Sahih* from him: "Among the worst of people are those upon whom the Hour will come while they are alive, and those who take graves as places of worship."

Also in the *Sahih* from him: "Indeed those before you used to take graves as places of worship. Beware, do not take graves as places of worship, for I forbid you from that."

In the *Musnad* of Imam Ahmad, may God be pleased with him, and the *Sahih* of Ibn Hibban, from him ﷺ: "The Messenger of God ﷺ cursed women who visit graves, and those who take graves as places of worship and place lamps upon them."

He also said: "The anger of God has intensified against a people who took the graves of their prophets as places of worship."

He also said: "Indeed, among those before you, when a righteous man died among them, they built a place of worship over his grave and made images in it. Those are the worst of creation in the sight of God on the Day of Resurrection."

So this is the condition of one who prostrates to God in a mosque built over a grave; how then is the condition of one who prostrates to the grave itself? The Prophet ﷺ said: "O God, do not make my grave an idol that is worshipped." The Prophet protected the side of *tawhid* with the greatest protection, to the extent that he forbade voluntary prayer to God at sunrise and at sunset, lest it become a *dhari'ah* (a means leading to something) to resembling the sun-worshippers who prostrate to it at these two times. He blocked this means by prohibiting prayer after the afternoon and dawn prayers, because these two times are linked to the two times when the polytheists prostrate to the sun.

As for prostrating to other than God, he said: "It is not fitting for anyone to prostrate to anyone except God."

The expression "it is not fitting" (*la yanbaghi*) in the speech of God and His Messenger ﷺ is used for what is absolutely impermissible in the Law, as in His saying: ﴿And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son﴾ [Maryam: 92], and His saying: ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him﴾ [Ya-Sin: 69], and His saying: ﴿The devils did not bring it down, nor is it befitting for them﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 210–211], and His saying about the angels: ﴿It is not for us to take any allies besides You﴾ [Al-Furqan: 18].

* *

**Section**

Among the *shirk* against Him, glorified is He, is *shirk* in speech, such as swearing by other than Him. As Ahmad and Abu Dawud related from him ﷺ that he said: "Whoever swears by anything besides God has committed *shirk*." Al-Hakim and Ibn Hibban declared it sound.

Among this is the saying of someone to a created being: "What God wills and you will." As was established from the Prophet ﷺ: a man said to him, "What God wills and you will," and he said: "Have you made me an equal to God? Say: what God alone wills." This is so even though God has affirmed a will for the servant, as in His saying: ﴿For whoever among you wills to be upright﴾ [At-Takwir: 28]. So how about one who says: "I am reliant upon God and upon you, I am in the sufficiency of God and yours, I have nothing but God and you, this is from God and from you, this is from the blessings of God and yours, God is for me in the heavens and you are for me on the earth"? Or one who says: "By God and the life of so-and-so," or says: "a vow to God and to so-and-so," "I repent to God and to so-and-so," "I hope in God and so-and-so," and similar things. Weigh these expressions against the saying "What God wills and you will," then consider which of them is more shameful. It will become clear to you that the speaker of these is more deserving of the Prophet's ﷺ rebuke to the one who uttered that phrase, and that if he made him a rival to God by it, then this one has made one who is not comparable to the Messenger of God ﷺ in anything, perhaps even one of his enemies, a rival to the Lord of the worlds.

So prostration and worship, reliance and turning in repentance, piety and fear, seeking refuge and repentance, vows and oaths, glorification and magnification, declaring God's oneness and praising Him, seeking forgiveness, shaving the head in humility and servitude, circumambulation of the House, and supplication, all of this is the exclusive right of God; it is not fitting or appropriate for anyone else, whether an honored angel or a sent prophet.
