And Allah swore that no one believes who does not make him judge in whatever he disputes with himself or others, then is content with his judgment, finds no discomfort within himself regarding what he decided, and submits to it with full submission. Allah the Exalted said: "It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair" [al-Ahzab: 36]. So Allah the Exalted cut off choice after His command and the command of His Messenger. It is not for a believer to choose anything after the command of the Prophet (ﷺ); rather, when he commands, his command is binding. Choice exists only in the words of others, when his command is not clear and that other is among the people of knowledge of him and his Sunnah. By these conditions, the words of another are permissible to follow, not obligatory to follow. It is not obligatory upon anyone to follow the words of anyone other than him; at most, it is permissible for him to follow it, and if he leaves off taking the words of another, he is not disobeying Allah and His Messenger. How far is this from one whom all the mukallafun are obliged to follow, whose opposition is forbidden to them, and upon whom it is obligatory to abandon every saying in favour of his saying! No judgment remains for anyone in his presence, nor any saying for anyone in his presence, just as no legislation remains for anyone in his presence. Every living person other than him is to be followed only in what he says when he commands what the Prophet commanded and forbids what the Prophet forbade. He is a pure conveyor and informer, not an originator and founder. Whoever originates sayings and establishes rules according to his own understanding and interpretation, it is not obligatory upon the Ummah to follow them or to adjudicate by them until they are presented to what he (ﷺ) brought. If they agree with it and conform to it and bear witness to its soundness, they are accepted then. If they contradict it, it is obligatory to reject and discard them. If neither of the two matters becomes clear regarding them, they are held in suspension, and the best of their states is that judgment and giving fatwa by them is permissible. As for it being obligatory and binding, no. End of quote.

And the words of Allah the Exalted:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 4, verse 66:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them. But if they had done what they were being admonished with, it would have been better for them and stronger in firming them up.﴾ [66]

﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them.﴾ Al-Razi said: Know that this verse is connected to what preceded concerning the hypocrites and their being encouraged toward sincerity and abandoning hypocrisy. The meaning is: If We had imposed heavy obligations upon people, such as commanding them to kill and to leave their homelands, it would have been difficult for them, and none would have done it except the few, and at that point their disbelief and obstinacy would have become manifest. (p-1383) But since We did not do that, out of mercy from Us toward Our servants, and rather We limited their obligations to easy matters, let them accept them sincerely and let them abandon defiance and obstinacy, so that they may attain the good of both abodes. End of quote.

He transmitted it afterward from Ibn 'Abbas, and according to this the pronoun in (upon them) refers to the hypocrites. There is another view, that it refers to all people, and the intended meaning of (the few) would be the believers. As for the pronoun in His words, ﴿But if they had done﴾, it is specific to the hypocrites. It is not far-fetched that the beginning of the verse is general and its end specific, as Al-Razi established.

Ibn Jurayj narrated with his chain to Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i who said: "When the verse ﴿And if We had decreed for them﴾ was revealed, a man said: 'Had we been commanded, we would have done it, and praise be to Allah who has spared us.' This reached the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: 'Among my community are men whose faith is firmer in their hearts than the towering mountains.'" Ibn Abi Hatim narrated something similar to it.

He also reported from al-Suddi who said: Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas and a man from the Jews boasted, and the Jew said: "By Allah, Allah has prescribed killing for us, so we killed ourselves." Thabit said: "By Allah, if it had been prescribed for us, 'Kill yourselves,' we would have done it." So the verse was revealed.

He also reported from 'Amir ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr that when this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Had it been revealed, Ibn Umm 'Abd would have been among them."

He also reported from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd who said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse, he pointed with his hand to 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah and said: 'If Allah had prescribed that, this man would be among those few.'"

* *

Remarks:

First: Some exegetes said: It means the actual killing and leaving of homes. It was also said: It means exposing oneself to being killed through jihad, and by leaving homes it means emigration (hijrah). The meaning is: If the hypocrites were commanded as the believers were commanded, they would not have done it. End of quote.

The second view is distant, because one does not depart from the literal meaning except by necessity, and because it contradicts the clear reports mentioned in the first.

Second: The pronoun in (they did it) refers to what was prescribed, encompassing killing and leaving, since (We prescribed) indicates it; or it refers to one of the two verbal sources. Al-Khafaji said: Because of the conjunction with (aw, or), the pronoun must be singular. End of quote.

I say: Shaykh Khalid in "al-Tasrih" mentioned that using the singular pronoun after the conjunction (aw) is the view of the Basrans, while the dual is the view of the Kufans, so he established that both are permissible. His annotator, the scholar Yasin, said: What Ibn Malik stated explicitly is that (aw) which indicates doubt and vagueness is followed by a singular pronoun, while (aw) which indicates classification agrees (in number), as in His words: ﴿If he be rich or poor, Allah is more entitled to both of them﴾ [al-Nisa: 135]. Ibn Hisham also stated this in "al-Mughni" under the topic of the parenthetical sentence, saying regarding this verse: The apparent answer is "Allah is more entitled to both of them," and the dual pronoun does not contradict this as some have imagined, because (aw) here is for classification, and its ruling is like that of (waw) in requiring agreement. Al-Abadi stated this, and it is the truth. End of quote.

From this it is known that what is well known, that when two conjoined items are mentioned with (aw) the pronoun returns to one of them, is not general.

Third: Ibn 'Amir read (qalilan) with a fatha as an exception, and the rest read it with a damma as a substitute for the pronoun of the subject.

﴿But if they had done what they were being admonished with﴾ That is: following the Messenger ﷺ, obeying him, and submitting to what he rules, outwardly and inwardly. The commands and prohibitions of Allah were called admonitions (mawa'iz) because they are accompanied by promise and threat. ﴿it would have been better for them﴾ That is: their doing so would have been better for them in their immediate affairs, ﴿and stronger in firming them up﴾ That is: for their faith, and further from wavering.

(p-١٣٨٥) The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And We would surely have given them from Us a great reward﴾ [67]

﴿And We would surely have given them from Us﴾ i.e., from Our presence, ﴿a reward﴾ i.e., a recompense, ﴿great﴾, meaning Paradise.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And We would have guided them to a straight path﴾ [68]

﴿And We would have guided them to a straight path﴾ i.e., We would have made them firm in this world upon an upright religion that We approve, which is Islam. Then Exalted is He explained the virtue of obedience and that its fruit is companionship with the nearest of Allah's servants to Allah and the highest of them in rank with Him, so He said:

The discourse of God Most High:

﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – then they will be with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the sincere affirmers of truth (al-siddiqin), the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.﴾ [69]

﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger – then they will be with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor﴾: He did not mention what the favor was, indicating that expression falls short of detailing and explaining it. ﴿Of the prophets﴾, those to whom Allah conveyed the most perfect beliefs and rulings, and whom He commanded to convey them to creation, each according to his capacity. ﴿And the siddiqin﴾ (plural of siddiq), the one who is exceedingly truthful in his outward conduct through his dealings, and in his inner state through vigilance; or the one whose speech is confirmed by his action. So it is related in "al-Madarik".

Al-Razi said: The exegetes have several views concerning the siddiq:

First: Whoever affirms the entire religion without any doubt entering him is a siddiq. The evidence is His saying: ﴿And those who believed in Allah and His messengers – those are the siddiqun﴾ [al-Hadid: 19].

Second: Some said: the siddiqun are the most excellent companions of the Prophet (peace be upon him).

Third: The siddiq is the name for one who was first to affirm the Messenger (peace be upon him), thus becoming an exemplar for all people. If this is the case, then Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) is the most worthy of creation of this description. Then al-Razi elaborated on his precedence (may Allah be pleased with him) in affirmation, and on his being an exemplar for people in that, so consult it.

﴿And the martyrs﴾, those who were martyred in the way of Allah Most High. ﴿And the righteous﴾, those whose states were sound and whose deeds were good. ﴿And excellent are those﴾: a reference to the prophets, the siddiqin, and what follows them. ﴿As companions﴾: meaning in Paradise. The rafiq is the companion, named so because of the ease (irtifaq) you gain through him and his companionship. The word rafiq is singular while describing a plural, because the Arabs use it to express both the singular and the plural, as with siddiq and khalit. The sentence is a concluding statement confirming what came before it, emphasizing encouragement and eagerness.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It carries the sense of wonder, as if it were said: "How excellent those companions are!" And because it functions independently with the meaning of wonder, it was read as (wa-hasna) with a sukun on the sin.

* *

Remarks:

First: Al-Razi said: The meaning of those who obey Allah and obey the Messenger being "with the prophets and the siddiqin..." etc. is not that all are at one rank, for that would require equality in rank between the superior and the inferior, which is impermissible. Rather, the meaning is that they are in Paradise in such a way that each of them can see the others, even if the place is distant, because when the veil is removed, some of them see others; and if they wish more, they are able to do so. This is the meaning of this companionship.

Second: The verse indicates that there is no rank after prophethood in excellence and knowledge except this attribute, namely that a person be a siddiq. Therefore wherever the siddiq and the prophet are mentioned together in the Qur'an, no intermediary is placed between them.

As Allah said describing Isma'il: ﴿Indeed, he was true to his promise﴾ [Maryam: 54], and describing Idris: ﴿Indeed, he was a siddiq, a prophet﴾ [Maryam: 56]. And in this verse He said: ﴿Of the prophets and the siddiqin﴾, meaning: if you rise from the state of siddiqiyya you reach prophethood, and if you descend from prophethood you reach siddiqiyya, with no intermediary between them. In another verse He said: ﴿And the one who brought the truth and confirmed it﴾ [al-Zumar: 33], and did not place any intermediary between them.

Just as these proofs indicate the negation of an intermediary, Allah has granted this Ummah, described as the best nation, success such that they chose Abu Bakr as imam after the Messenger (peace be upon him) by consensus. When he (may Allah be pleased with him) died, they buried him beside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This was only because Allah Most High removed the intermediary between the prophets and the siddiqin in this verse. Undoubtedly, the intermediary between them was removed in the aspects we have enumerated, as related by al-Razi.

Third: al-Tabari narrated concerning its occasion of revelation, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "A man from the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was grieved. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: 'O so-and-so! What is it that I see you grieved?' He said: 'O Prophet of Allah! Something I have been thinking about.' He said: 'What is it?' He said: 'We come to you in the morning and evening, look upon your face and sit with you, but tomorrow you will be raised with the prophets and we will not reach you.' The Prophet (ﷺ) did not answer him, and then Jibril came to him with this verse: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger﴾, etc. So the Prophet (ﷺ) sent for him and gave him glad tidings."

This report has been narrated as mursal from Masruq, 'Ikrima, 'Amir al-Sha'bi, Qatada, and from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and it is among the best in chain. al-Tabari said: al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said concerning this verse: "The companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'We know that the Prophet (ﷺ) has his excellence over those who believed in him in the ranks of Paradise, among those who followed him and affirmed him. So how will they be when they are gathered in Paradise, that one sees another?' So Allah revealed this verse concerning that. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then said: 'Indeed, those on high descend to those below them, and they gather in its gardens, mention what Allah has bestowed upon them, and praise Him. The people of the higher ranks come down to them, and they strive for them with what they desire and what they ask for. They are in a garden, made joyful and enjoying blessings therein.'"

Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through another route, raised to the Prophet, from Aisha, who said: "A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! You are more beloved to me than my own self, more beloved to me than my family, more beloved to me than my children. When I am in the house I remember you, and I cannot bear it until I come to you and look at you. When I remember my death and yours, I know that when you enter Paradise you will be raised with the prophets, and if I enter Paradise I fear I will not see you.' The Prophet (ﷺ) did not answer him until there was revealed upon him: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah﴾, the verse." Thus al-Hafiz Abu 'Abd Allah al-Maqdisi narrated it in his book "Sifat al-Jannah" with a chain of which he said: "I see no harm in it."

Fourth: Numerous reports have been transmitted in the Sunnah concerning the meaning of this verse. Among them, in Sahih Muslim, from Rabi'a ibn Ka'b al-Aslami, who said: "I used to spend the night with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I would bring him water for ablution and his needs. He said to me: 'Ask!' I said: 'I ask you for your companionship in Paradise.' He said: 'Is there anything other than that?' I said: 'That is it.' He said: 'Then help me against yourself by much prostration.'"

Among them, in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from 'Amr ibn Murrah al-Juhani, who said: "A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah, I pray the five prayers, I pay the zakat of my wealth, and I fast the month of Ramadan.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever dies upon that will be with the prophets, the siddiqin, and the martyrs on the Day of Resurrection, like this' – and he raised his two fingers – 'so long as he does not disobey his parents.'" Ibn Kathir said: Ahmad alone narrated it.

Among them is what Imam Ahmad also narrated, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh ibn Anas, from his father, that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever recites a thousand verses in the way of Allah, Blessed and Most High, will be recorded on the Day of Resurrection with the prophets, the siddiqin, the martyrs, and the righteous, and excellent are those as companions.'" If Allah wills.

Among them is what al-Tirmidhi narrated from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The truthful, trustworthy merchant is with the prophets, the siddiqin, and the martyrs."

Ibn Kathir said: Greater than all of this as good news is what is established in the Sahih and the Masanid and other collections, through multiple chains from a group of the Companions, that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about a man who loves a people but has not yet joined them, and he said: 'A person is with those he loves.'"

Anas said: "The Muslims never rejoiced as they rejoiced at this hadith."

In another report from Anas, he said: "Indeed I love the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I love Abu Bakr and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), and I hope He will resurrect me with them, even if I do not act like their deeds."

From Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, the people of Paradise will see the people of the chambers above them as one sees the bright star that is set on the horizon in the east or the west, due to the difference in their ranks.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Those are the dwellings of the prophets, which no one else reaches.' He said: 'Yes, by Him in whose hand is my soul, men who believed in Allah and affirmed the messengers.'" Related by al-Bukhari and Muslim in the Sahihayn from the hadith of Imam Malik, and the wording is Muslim's.

And the words of Allah Most High:

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

﴿That is the bounty from Allah, and sufficient is Allah as Knower.﴾ [70]

﴿That﴾ is a subject (mubtada'), a demonstrative referring to what the obedient have of reward, increase in guidance, and companionship with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour. Or it refers to the bounty and distinction of those favoured. Thus the thing pointed to is either all that precedes it or what immediately follows it. ﴿The bounty﴾ is an attribute (sifah), and ﴿from Allah﴾ is its predicate (khabar), meaning: that great bounty is from Allah, Exalted, and from no other. (p-1391) Or ﴿the bounty﴾ is the predicate, and ﴿from Allah﴾ is a circumstantial phrase (hal), whose governing element is the sense of the demonstrative, meaning: that reward, for the completeness of its rank, is as if it were itself the bounty, and everything else is nothing, existing and coming into being from Allah, Exalted is He, not that the deeds of the responsible persons necessitate it.

Al-Nasir said in al-Intisaf: Our belief, we the people of the Sunnah, is that the acts of obedience and deeds by which these elite are distinguished are the creation and action of Allah, Exalted is He, and that their capacities have no effect on their deeds. Rather, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, creates the acts of obedience through them and rewards them for these. So obedience is, then, from His bounty; to Him belongs the bounty in every state, and the favour in the beginning and in the end. And the saying of the Master of mankind suffices as proof and example in this, for he, upon whom be the most excellent prayers and peace, said: "None of you will enter Paradise by his deeds." It was said: "Not even you, Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His bounty and mercy." ﴿Say: By the bounty of Allah and His mercy, so let them rejoice in that﴾. O Allah! Seal our lives with adherence to the Sunnah, and admit us by Your pure bounty into Paradise. End of al-Nasir's words.

The hadith mentioned was narrated by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) from Abu Hurayrah.

﴿And sufficient is Allah as Knower﴾ of the reward of whoever obeys Him, and of the measures of the bounty and the deservingness of its people.

Al-Razi said: It has a great place in confirming what preceded of the encouragement to obey Allah, because He, Exalted, by this alerted that He knows the manner of obedience and the manner of the reward and bounty, and this is among what encourages the responsible person to perfection in obedience and to guarding against falling short in it. Then, after the encouragement to obey Him and to obey His Messenger, Exalted is He repeated the command to the jihad that had preceded, because it is the most arduous of acts of obedience and the greatest of matters by which the strengthening of the religion is achieved. Then He, glorified is He, said:

(p-1392) The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

﴿O you who have believed, take your precaution and either go forth in parties or go forth all together﴾ [71]

﴿O you who have believed, take your precaution﴾ meaning: be alert and guard yourselves against the enemy, and do not let him gain access to you. It is said: "akhadha hadhrahu" (he took his precaution) when he became alert and guarded himself against what he feared. It is as if he made caution his instrument by which he protects himself. Also, "al-hadhar" (caution) is applied to that by which one takes precaution and protects oneself, such as weapons and measures of prudence; that is, prepare yourselves against the enemy. On this understanding, "al-hadhar" is literal, while on the first understanding it is metaphorical (kinaya and takhyil), by likening caution to weapons and the instrument of protection.

In "al-Iklil" he said: in it is a command to take up weapons, and that this does not contradict reliance on God (tawakkul).

Some exegetes said: the verse indicates the obligation of jihad and the employment of caution, which is prudence regarding the enemy and the avoidance of negligence. Likewise, what they take precaution with, which is the use of weapons according to one of the two explanations, so training through racing and wagering with horses is among the acts of jihad.

﴿Then go forth﴾ meaning: set out to jihad ﴿in parties (thubat)﴾, the plural of "thubah" meaning a group, as in the Qamus; that is, groups dispersed, one expedition after another, and one company after another, to display boldness.

﴿Or go forth all together﴾ meaning: assembled, all of you as one single body; to instill awe through increasing the numbers, and out of exaggeration in guarding against danger.

Al-Hakim said: the scholars agreed that this is left to the judgment (ijtihad) of the imam (ruler).

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

﴿And indeed among you is one who will certainly lag behind. So if a misfortune strikes you, he says, "Allah has certainly favored me, for I was not present with them as a witness."﴾ [72]

﴿And indeed among you is one who will certainly lag behind﴾ means: he will certainly be sluggish and will hold back from jihad and from going out with the community, out of hypocrisy. Or its meaning is: he will discourage others, just as the hypocrites used to discourage others. This was the habit of the hypocrite ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, who discouraged people on the Day of Uhud. It has been narrated from many of the Successors (tabiʿun) that the verse (p-1393) was revealed concerning the hypocrites, since what is related about them is their customary conduct. It was also said: the address is to the believers, keeping with the beginning of the verse, for He said: ﴿O you who have believed﴾ [an-Nisa': 71], then He said ﴿And indeed among you﴾, whereas Exalted is He said about the hypocrites: ﴿They are not of you﴾ [al-Mujadila: 14].

Al-Hakim said: The sense according to the first opinion is: "And indeed among you" — according to his claim — in outward appearance, or in the judgment of the Sharia.

﴿So if a misfortune strikes you﴾ such as a defeat, a martyrdom, or the enemy's overpowering of you, due to the wisdom of Allah in that matter. ﴿He says﴾, that is, the one who lags behind, rejoicing in his own doing and pleased with his own opinion: ﴿Allah has certainly favored me﴾ by sitting out ﴿for I was not present with them as a witness﴾, that is, present in the battle so that what befell them would befall me. He counts that as one of Allah's blessings upon him, and does not consider what he missed of the reward for patience or for martyrdom had he been killed.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And if a bounty from Allah reaches you, he will surely say, as if there had never been any affection between you and him: "Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I could have achieved a great achievement."﴾ [73]

﴿And if a bounty from Allah reaches you﴾ means a conquest, booty, victory, or success. Attributing the reaching of bounty to Him, exalted is He, while not attributing the reaching of calamity to Him, is one of the noble, revealed patterns of speech, as in His saying: ﴿And when I am ill, it is He who cures me﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 80] [al-Shu'ara': 80].

﴿He will surely say﴾ out of regret for his hesitation and his sitting back, out of his eagerness for the trifles of this world, and out of grief over missing it. ﴿As if there had never been any affection between you and him﴾, that is, a bond in religion and a familiarity from companionship. ﴿Oh, I wish I had been with them, so I could have achieved a great achievement﴾, so that I would have obtained many spoils and a full share.

His saying, "as if there had never been," and so on, is an i'tiraḍ (a parenthetical interjection) placed between the verb, which is "will surely say," and its object, which is "Oh, I wish," and so on. It serves to draw attention to the weakness of their belief, and to the fact that this statement of theirs is the statement of one with whom no prior affection existed between him and you. This is because the hypocrites used to show affection and friendship toward the believers outwardly, even though they plotted harm for them inwardly. There is also in it a note of wonder at the statement they have made.

Some of the commentators said: The fruit of this is the affirmation of the obligation of jihad and the prohibition of discouraging from it. End of quotation.

When Exalted is He had censured those who lag behind from jihad, He encouraged the believers toward it with His saying, glorified is He:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 4, verse 74:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

﴿So let those fight in the way of Allah who sell the worldly life for the Hereafter. And whoever fights in the way of Allah and is killed or achieves victory, We will give him a great reward.﴾ [74]

﴿So let those fight in the way of Allah who sell the worldly life for the Hereafter﴾ means: they sell it in exchange for it. They are the believers who prefer the deferred (the Hereafter) over the immediate (this world) and exchange the one for the other. The meaning is: if those in whose hearts is a disease hold back, then let the sincere, who spend themselves in seeking the Hereafter, fight. It is also said that the relative clause refers to the hypocrites who hang back, i.e., those who buy the worldly life and choose it over the Hereafter. In that case it is an admonition to them to replace their hesitation with jihad.

﴿And whoever fights in the way of Allah and is killed﴾ means: is martyred. ﴿Or achieves victory﴾ means: prevails over the enemy. ﴿Then We will give him﴾ means: We will bestow on him ﴿a great reward﴾, i.e., abundant reward.

Al-Shaykhan (Bukhari and Muslim) narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah guarantees for whoever goes out in His way, and whose going out is motivated by nothing but jihad in My way, faith in Me, and belief in My messengers, that He is bound, by My own guarantee, to admit him to Paradise or to return him to the dwelling from which he set out, with whatever reward or spoils he has gained." (The wording is that of Muslim.)

[p. 1395]

**The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:**

﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the way of Allah and [for] the oppressed among men, women, and children, who say, "Our Lord, bring us out from this city whose people are wrongdoers, and appoint for us from Yourself a guardian, and appoint for us from Yourself a helper"?﴾ [75]

﴿وَمَا لَكُمْ لَا تُقَاتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ is an address to those who were commanded to fight, in the manner of *iltifat* (a shift in grammatical address), for the sake of intensifying the exhortation to it and emphasizing its obligation.

His words, exalted is He, ﴿وَالْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ﴾ are in the genitive case by coordination (*'atf*) with the word "Allah," meaning: in the way of the oppressed, who are like yourselves, and that is freeing them from captivity and protecting them from the enemy. Or [it is in the genitive] by [the omission of a noun and] the word "way" being governed by it, meaning: in the liberation of the oppressed. Or it is in the accusative case by specification (*ikhtisas*), meaning: "And I specify, from the way of Allah, the liberation of the oppressed." This is because the way of Allah is general to every good, while the liberation of the Muslim oppressed from the hands of the disbelievers is among the greatest and most specific of goods.

Al-Razi said in *al-Intisaf*: In the accusative case there is an emphasis on urging their liberation from two aspects:

The first: specification after generalization, for this requires the implicit governing word, which is "I specify" (*akhussu*). Were it not for the accusative, the specification would be understood from singling them out by mention. But this understood matter was emphasized by way of implication, by bringing it out into speech.

﴿مِنَ الرِّجَالِ وَالنِّسَاءِ وَالْوِلْدَانِ﴾ is an explanation (*bayan*) of "the oppressed," or a circumstantial clause (*hal*) from them. They are the Muslims whom the polytheists prevented from emigrating (*hijrah*), so they remained in Makkah, humiliated and oppressed, suffering severe harm from them. The Prophet ﷺ used to supplicate for them, saying: "O Allah, deliver al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Salamah ibn Hisham, Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah, and the oppressed among the believers," as in the *Sahih*.

[p. 1396] He mentioned "the children" (*al-wildan*) with them only to complete the appeal for compassion and to draw mercy, and as an alert to the extreme extent of the polytheists' oppression, to the point that their harm reached the children; and as an announcement of the answering of the supplication that follows, due to the children's participation in the supplication.

﴿الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ﴾ because of the harm and humiliation inflicted on them by the people of Makkah, disavowing dwelling in it: ﴿رَبَّنَا أَخْرِجْنَا مِنْ هَذِهِ الْقَرْيَةِ الظَّالِمِ أَهْلُهَا﴾ meaning: by polytheism, which is a great wrong, and by harming the Muslims. "This city" is Makkah, and "whose people are wrongdoers" is its attribute. Its masculine form is for the sake of agreement with what is attributed to it. For when an active or passive participle is applied to something other than the one it belongs to, it behaves like the verb in masculinity and femininity according to what governs it. This was stated by Abu al-Su'ud.

﴿وَاجْعَلْ لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ وَلِيًّا﴾ meaning: make subservient for us from Your presence a guardian who will protect our religion for us. ﴿وَاجْعَلْ لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ نَصِيرًا﴾ a helper who will repel the harms of our enemies from us. Or the meaning is: "And appoint for us from Yourself guardianship and support," that is, "Let You Yourself be our guardian and our helper." Allah, mighty and majestic, has answered their supplication, for He facilitated for some of them the going out to Madinah, and He made for those who remained among them the best of guardians and the most mighty of helpers, so He granted Makkah to His Prophet ﷺ, and He took charge of them in the best of charge, and gave them the best of support, until they became the most honored of its people.

Al-Bukhari narrated with his chain to Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "I and my mother were among the oppressed." And with the same chain to him, he said: "My mother was among those whom Allah excused."

[p. 1397] Al-Razi said: The meaning of the verse is: you have no excuse for abandoning fighting, when the state of the oppressed among the Muslims has reached what it has reached of weakness. This is a strong exhortation to fighting, and an explanation of the cause for which fighting became obligatory, which is what fighting contains of liberating these believers from the hands of the disbelievers. For this gathering [of causes], together with jihad, operates in the manner of ransoming a captive. End.

* *

**An admonition:**

Some of the exegetes said: The fruit of this verse is the emphasis on the obligation of jihad, for He, exalted is He, rebuked those who abandon it. The verse indicates the obligation of rescuing the Muslim from the hands of the disbelievers, and the like of this rescue comes from every harm, from a wrongdoer, a thief, and other than that. The basis for this derivation is that He, exalted is He, made that like the cause for the cutting off of attachment to Him. It also indicates that the ruling for the children is the ruling for the fathers, because the apparent meaning is that He intended the young ones.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It is permissible that by "the men and the women" be meant the free men and free women, and by "the children" be meant the male and female slaves, because a male slave and a female slave are called *al-walid* and *al-walidah*. It was also said that "the children and the female children" are called *al-waldan* (the masculine form), by giving predominance to the males over the females, as one says "the fathers and the brothers." The verse also indicates that the supplicant has a right with Allah, for He made that a specification for His support. It indicates the obligation of emigration from the abodes of disbelief, and that the believer does not humble himself by making himself oppressed, for He, exalted is He, made fighting obligatory to remove domination over them. And in these verses there are successive emphases on the obligation of jihad.

**A subtle point:**

Nasir al-Din said in *al-Intisaf*: I came upon a fine subtle point in this verse, which is that every town mentioned in the Noble Book has wrongdoing attributed to it by way of metaphor (*majaz*), like His saying: ﴿And Allah struck an example: a town that was secure and at rest...﴾ [an-Nahl: 112] up to His saying: ﴿...so it denied the favors of Allah﴾ [an-Nahl: 112], and His saying: [p. 1398] ﴿And how many a town have We destroyed which exulted in its livelihood﴾ [al-Qasas: 58]. As for this town here (in Surat an-Nisa'), wrongdoing is attributed to its people in reality, because what is meant by it is Makkah. So it was held in honor from having wrongdoing attributed to it, as an ennoblement of it, which Allah, exalted is He, ennobled. Then, exalted is He, encouraged and enticed the believers to jihad with His saying: ...

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 4, verse 76:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the Taghut (the tyrant, i.e., Satan or any object of worship or obedience other than Allah). So fight against the allies of Satan. Indeed, the plotting of Satan is ever weak.﴾ [76]

﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah﴾ meaning: in obedience to Him, to raise high His word. So He is their Protector and their Helper. ﴿And those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the Taghut﴾ meaning: in obedience to Satan, who commands the utmost transgression, such as harming the oppressed among the believers and fighting their strong ones. ﴿So fight against the allies of Satan﴾ i.e., his army.

Abu al-Su'ud said: He mentioned them with this title (the allies of Satan) to indicate that this is a consequence of their fighting in the cause of Satan, and to convey that the believers are the allies of Allah, Exalted is He, since their fighting is in His cause. All of this is to strengthen the eagerness of the believers for fighting and to reinforce their resolve upon it, for the guardianship of Allah, Exalted is He, is a sign of might and strength, just as the guardianship of Satan is an example of humiliation and weakness. It is as if it were said: If the matter is so, then fight, O allies of Allah, against the allies of Satan. Then He stated the reason explicitly, saying: ﴿Indeed, the plotting of Satan is ever weak﴾ i.e., in itself; how much more so in comparison with the power of Allah, Exalted is He. The strength of His majesty was not explicitly described, as its manifestation is considered evident.

They said: The benefit of including (kāna) in such contexts is emphasis, by showing that since it has existed, it has been so. The meaning is: the plotting of Satan, since it has existed, has been described as weak. End of quotation.

(Al-Kayd, "plotting"): striving to corrupt a situation by way of scheming against it. One says: kādahu yakīduhu when he strives to bring harm upon him by way of trickery. Related by al-Razi.

[p-1399]

**The discussion on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:**

﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands, establish prayer, and give zakah"? But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a faction of them fear the people as they fear Allah, or with greater fear. And they say, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You had delayed us to a near term." Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, and you will not be wronged even the thread (of a date-seed)."﴾ [4:77]

﴿Have you not seen those who were told﴾: they were the believers, when they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for permission to fight before they were commanded to do so. ﴿Restrain your hands﴾: that is, from fighting, for you have not been commanded to it. ﴿Establish prayer and give zakah﴾: that is, complete the five prayers with their ablutions, their bowings, their prostrations, and what is obligatory in them at their proper times, and give the zakah of your wealth. ﴿But when it was prescribed﴾: that is, enjoined ﴿for them, fighting﴾: that is, jihad in the way of Allah, when their condition became strong. ﴿Behold, a faction of them﴾: that is, a group among them, and they are the hypocrites, who are counted among the believers because of what they displayed of themselves, that they were of them. ﴿Fear the people﴾: that is, they fear the disbelievers of Makkah lest they kill them. ﴿As they fear Allah﴾: that is, as they fear Allah lest He send down His punishment upon them. ﴿Or with greater fear﴾: that is, with more fear of them.

If it is said: the apparent meaning of His words, ﴿or with greater fear﴾, suggests doubt, and that is impossible for the Knower of the unseen. (It is answered:) the "or" (أوْ) is either in the sense of "rather" (بَلْ), or it is for classification, meaning that the fear of some of them is like the fear of Allah, and the fear of others is greater than it. Or it is for obscuring to the listener, meaning that they are in one of the two states, either equal or more intense. This is close to His words: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾ [37:147], meaning that whoever sees them would say, "They are a hundred thousand or more."

* *

**A note:**

The exegetes relate here a narration from Ibn Abbas that this verse was revealed concerning a group of the Companions among the Emigrants (al-Muhajirun), who used to suffer severe harm from the polytheists of Makkah before the Hijrah. They would complain of this to the Prophet (ﷺ) and say: "Permit us to fight them." The Prophet (ﷺ) would say to them: "Restrain your hands, for I have not been commanded to fight them, and occupy yourselves with establishing your religion through prayer and zakah." Then, after the Hijrah to Madinah, when they were commanded to fight them at the Battle of Badr, some of them disliked it, and the verse was revealed.

In my view, this verse, like what precedes it, was revealed concerning the hypocrites, as a rebuke to them and a warning to the sincere ones who are of their kind. The claim that it was revealed concerning some of the believers is not sound, for several reasons:

Among them: in its chain of narration from Ibn Abbas there is someone who does not meet the conditions of the sound (narrations).

Among them: that their request for jihad while they were in Makkah, with few in number and few in equipment, and with the enemy aiding one another against them from every side, is far-fetched in the extreme.

Among them: the context concerns the hypocrites, and the discourse about them began from His words: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you, desiring to seek judgment from the tyrant?﴾ [4:60], up to His later words: ﴿So do not take from them allies﴾ [4:89] and the verse, as is apparent from sincere reflection.

Among them: this context includes matters that indicate it is specific to the hypocrites. For He, may He be exalted, said in describing them: ﴿They fear the people as they fear Allah, or with greater fear﴾, and this description applies only to a disbeliever or a hypocrite. He, may He be exalted, also related of them that they said: ﴿And they say, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us?"﴾, and this is not known from the believers. Rather, what is preserved is their eagerness for jihad, as Ibn Ishaq narrated in "al-Sirah": "The Prophet (ﷺ) consulted the people at the Battle of Badr. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq stood and said well, then Umar ibn al-Khattab stood and said well, then al-Miqdad ibn Amr stood and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, proceed with what Allah has shown you, for we are with you. By Allah, we will not say as the Children of Israel said to Musa: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are sitting right here﴾ [5:24]. Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight; indeed, we are fighting along with you. By He who sent you with the truth, if you were to take us to Bark al-Ghimad, we would fight beside you until you reached it.'

Then Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said: 'Proceed, O Messenger of Allah, with what you intend, for we are with you. By He who sent you with the truth, if you were to lead us into this sea and plunge into it, we would plunge in with you. Not one man of us would stay behind, and we do not dislike that you should meet our enemy with us tomorrow. Indeed, we are patient in war and truthful in encounter.'"

Among them: He, may He be exalted, mentioned after that His words: ﴿And if a good thing befalls them, they say, "This is from Allah"; and if a bad thing befalls them, they say, "This is from you (O Muhammad)"﴾ [4:78]. There is no doubt that this is the speech of the hypocrites. Then He, may He be exalted, explicitly addressed them at the end of the discourse by His words: ﴿So what is [the matter] with you that you have become two groups concerning the hypocrites?﴾ [4:88], and so the confusion was removed and the obscurity cleared.

Similar to these verses is His words in (Surat Muhammad): ﴿And those who believe say, "Why has a surah not been revealed?"﴾ [47:20], meaning, "Why do You not command us to jihad?" ﴿But when a decisive surah is revealed and fighting is mentioned therein, you see those in whose hearts is a disease looking at you﴾ [47:20], up to His words: ﴿Or do those in whose hearts is a disease think that Allah will not bring out their resentments?﴾ [47:29].

﴿And they say, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us?"﴾: that is, jihad in Your way. ﴿If only You had delayed us to a near term﴾: that is, why did You not spare us and leave us until we die at our appointed times? ﴿Say﴾: that is, to discourage them from what they hope for by sitting idle, from the perishing enjoyment, and to encourage them toward what they attain through jihad of enduring bliss. ﴿The enjoyment of this world﴾: that is, what is enjoyed and benefited from in this world ﴿is little﴾: swift to pass away, near to cease, even if you are delayed until that appointed term.

﴿And the Hereafter﴾: that is, its reward, of which the reward attached to jihad is a part ﴿is better﴾: that is, for you than that perishing enjoyment, because of its abundance, its non-cessation, and its purity from turbidities. It was said: ﴿for those who fear Allah﴾ only to urge them to guard against disobedience and against neglecting what the obligation requires. ﴿And you will not be wronged even the thread﴾: this is a conjunction with an implied element that the discourse entails, meaning: you will be recompensed, and you will not be diminished in the least of the rewards of your deeds, of which your striving in the matter of fighting is a part, so do not turn away from it.

(And the "fatil" (فَتِيلا)) is the thread that is in the split of the date-seed, which is used as a proverb for smallness and insignificance.

It was also read as "yuzlamun" (يُظْلِمُونَ) with the "ya'" (i.e., "they will not be wronged"), returning the pronoun to the apparent meaning of "those who" (مَن), as Abu al-Sa'ud noted.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, saying: al-Hasan recited: "Say, the enjoyment of this world is little," and said: "May Allah have mercy on a servant who keeps company with it according to its true measure. The whole world, its beginning and its end, is nothing but like a man who sleeps a nap and sees in his dream some of what he loves, then wakes up." Ibn Mu'in said: Abu Mas'har used to recite:

*"There is no good in this world for one who has no portion from Allah in the abode of permanence,*
*So if the world pleases men, indeed it is*
*a little enjoyment, and its passing is near."*

Then He, may He be exalted, explained that fleeing from death will not benefit them, because there is no escape for them from it, by His words:

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be within towers built up high.⦆ And if good befalls them, they say, "This is from Allah," but if evil befalls them, they say, "This is from you." Say, "All is from Allah." So what is wrong with these people that they can hardly understand any statement?﴾ [78]

﴿Wherever you may be﴾, that is, in whatever place you are when the appointed term comes, ﴿death will overtake you﴾, namely, the death from which you flee fighting, thinking it lies in its own place, and you love to sit back from it, supposing that it is a means of escape from it. That is, since death is unavoidable, then for it to befall you in a manner that leads to everlasting happiness is better than that it should not be so. A parallel to this verse is His saying: ﴿Say, "Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing, and then you will not be given enjoyment except for a little."﴾ [al-Ahzab: 16].

﴿Even if you were within towers﴾ (p-1403), that is, fortresses, ﴿built up high﴾, that is, raised and well-fortified, which no human killer can reach, but they do not prevent the divine Killer, as Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma said:

"Whoever fears the causes of death, they will reach him, even if he tries to climb the causes of the heavens with a ladder."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim have here mentioned a lengthy narration from Mujahid, and the relevant part of it is that she had been told she would die by a spider. So her husband built for her a high, impregnable palace to protect her from that. Then one day they found a spider on the ceiling, and he showed it to her. She said, "Is this the one you fear for me? By Allah, none will kill it but I." So they brought it down from the ceiling, and she deliberately stepped on it with the big toe of her foot and killed it, but some of its poison flew and lodged between her nail and flesh, and her foot turned black, and in that was her end, and she died.

When He, Exalted, related about the hypocrites that they were reluctant to fight, fearful of death, not desiring the happiness of the Hereafter, He followed this with a more shameful trait of theirs, in His saying: ﴿And if good befalls them﴾, such as fertility, provision of fruits, crops, children and the like, ﴿they say, "This is from Allah"﴾, that is, from Him (p-1404), since He knew good in us; ﴿but if evil befalls them﴾, such as drought, dearth, high prices, loss in crops and fruits, death of children and offspring, and the like, ﴿they say, "This is from you"﴾, meaning: from your ill omen, as Allah, Exalted, said about the people of Pharaoh: ﴿But when good came to them, they said, "This is ours." And if evil befell them, they ascribed it to bad omen from Moses and those with him﴾ [al-A'raf: 131], and about the people of Salih: ﴿They said, "We consider you and those with you a bad omen"﴾ [al-Naml: 47].

Abu al-Su'ud said: The Prophet ﷺ was commanded to refute their false claim, guide them to the truth, and silence them with a clear statement that everything is attributed to Allah, Exalted, in summary, since they would not dare to oppose the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when it was said: ﴿Say, "All is from Allah"﴾, that is, each of the blessing and the affliction comes from Allah, Exalted, by creation and bringing into existence, without my having any part in the occurrence of any of them in any way as you claim. Rather, the occurrence of the first is from Him, Exalted, directly by grace, and the occurrence of the second is through the sins of those afflicted with it, as a punishment, as its explanation will come. So this summary answer is in the meaning of what was said in refutation of their predecessors, in His saying: ﴿Indeed, their omen is with Allah﴾ [al-A'raf: 131], that is, the cause of their good and bad, or the cause of the affliction of evil, which is their sins, is with Allah, Exalted, not with anyone else, so that they would attribute it to Him and take bad omen from Him.

﴿So what is wrong with these people﴾, meaning the hypocrites, ﴿that they can hardly understand any statement﴾, that is, any speech? The sentence is parenthetical, brought to rebuke them for ignorance, to disparage their condition, and to express wonder at the completeness of their dullness, for if they understood anything, they would know from what they are admonished with that Allah is the One who withholds and extends, that blessing from Him, Exalted, is by way of grace and kindness, and affliction by way of punishment for the sins of the servants.

(p-١٤٠٥) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself. And We have sent you to mankind as a messenger, and sufficient is Allah as a witness.﴾ [79]

﴿Whatever good befalls you﴾, i.e., blessing, ﴿is from Allah﴾, i.e., from His blessing and His favour, initially. ﴿And whatever evil befalls you﴾, i.e., affliction, ﴿is from yourself﴾, i.e., from its ill omen, due to your committing the sins that necessitate it. Although, in terms of its creation, it is attributed to Him, Exalted is He, and descends from Him as a punishment, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And whatever disaster strikes you, it is for what your hands have earned; and He pardons much.﴾ [al-Shura: 30] [al-Shura: 30].

Ibn 'Asakir narrated, from al-Bara', may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "No stumble, no twitch of a vein, and no scratch from a stick occurs except by what your hands have put forward, and Allah pardons more."

And al-Tirmidhi narrated, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "No speck befalls a servant, nor what is above it or below it, except by a sin, and Allah pardons more than that." He said: [the Prophet] recited: ﴿And whatever disaster strikes you, it is for what your hands have earned; and He pardons much.﴾ [al-Shura: 30].

(p-١٤٠٦) A subtle point:

The address in ﴿befalls you﴾ is general to everyone who is addressed by it, not specific to the Prophet ﷺ, as in the verse:

"If you honour the noble, you possess him."

It includes those mentioned by initial inclusion. It is also permissible that the address is to him ﷺ, as is the case before and after it, but not to explain his state ﷺ; rather, to explain the state of the disbelievers by way of depiction. Perhaps this is to show the complete displeasure and anger towards them, and to indicate that, due to their extreme ignorance and dullness, they are far from deserving to be addressed, especially with such an elegant wisdom. Abu al-Su'ud established this.

Some exegetes said: The fruit of the verse is the refutation of superstitious omen-taking (tatayyur) and ill-omen belief (tashå'um).

﴿And We have sent you to mankind as a messenger﴾ is an explanation of the greatness of his rank ﷺ and his station with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, after explaining the falsehood of their corrupt claim concerning him, peace and blessings be upon him, based on their ignorance of his noble status. The definiteness of (mankind) is for comprehensiveness, as Abu al-Su'ud indicated. That is: from where could ill omen be imagined for you, when you have been sent as a caller to all people to goodness? You are the source of every good and mercy. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾, i.e., as a witness to your message and truthfulness, by manifesting the miracles at your hands. That is: if your message is established, then blessing lies in obeying you, and ill omen lies in opposing you.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 4, verse 80:

(p-1407) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah, and whoever turns away — We have not sent you as a guardian over them.﴾ [80]

﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ because he, upon him be prayers and peace, is the conveyer of His command and His prohibition, so the return of obedience and its absence is to Allah, glorified and exalted is He. ﴿And whoever turns away﴾ from his obedience, ﴿We have not sent you as a guardian over them﴾, i.e., as a guarantor who keeps watch over their deeds, calls them to account for them, and punishes them according to them. ﴿Your duty is only to convey, and upon Us is the reckoning﴾ [al-Ra'd: 40] [al-Ra'd: 40].

When the Exalted had explained the obligation of obeying the Messenger, He followed it with mention of their dealings with him, saying:

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 4, verse 81:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

﴿And they say, "Obedience." But when they leave you, a faction of them plans by night other than what you say. And Allah records what they plan by night. So turn away from them and rely upon Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾ [81]

﴿And they say﴾: i.e., the hypocrites, when you command them with something while they are in your presence, ﴿"Obedience"﴾ with nominative case (ṭāʿatun), meaning: our matter and our affair is obedience. It is also permissible to read it in the accusative (ṭāʿatan), in the sense of "We obey you with obedience," just as the one who submits says: "Sam'an wa-ṭāʿatan" (We hear and obey), and "sam'un wa-ṭāʿatun."

Sībawayh said: We heard some trustworthy Arabs being asked, "How did you wake up?" and he would say, "Ḥamdu Allāhi wa-thanāʾun ʿalayhi" (praise of Allah and commendation of Him), as if he had said: "My matter and my affair is praise of Allah and commendation of Him." If "ḥamda Allāhi" were put in the accusative, it would be as a verb, whereas the nominative indicates the stability and constancy of the obedience.

﴿But when they leave﴾: i.e., go out, ﴿from your presence﴾: i.e., from your assembly, ﴿a faction of them plans﴾: i.e., arranges by night (bayyata), ﴿a faction of them﴾: i.e., of those mentioned who speak, and they are their leaders, ﴿other than what you say﴾: i.e., contrary to what they said to you of acceptance and pledge of obedience; because they persist in rejection and disobedience, and they only show what they show out of hypocrisy.

Two remarks:

The first: In the "Qamus" and its commentary: "Bayyata al-amr" means he did it or arranged it by night.

al-Zajjaj said: Everything that is thought over or deliberated upon at night has been "bayyata." It is said: "bayyata bi-laylin" and "dabbara bi-laylin" with one meaning.

In a hadith: "He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would not keep (yubayyitu) wealth overnight nor let it remain until midday (yaqīluhu)," meaning: when wealth came to him, he would not hold it until night nor until the afternoon rest, but would hasten its distribution. End.

al-Razi also related from al-Zajjaj: that every matter which one reflects upon and considers at length regarding its benefits and harms is called "mubayyat." Regarding its derivation there are two views:

The first: It is from "al-baytūtah" (spending the night), because the best time for thinking is for a person to sit in his house at night, where thoughts are freer and distractions fewer. Since a person usually is in his house at night, and usually thoroughly pursues thoughts at night, the thought that is thoroughly pursued is therefore called "mubayyat."

The second: Its derivation is from lines of poetry (abyat al-shiʿr), because the poet arranges and levels them. al-Akhfash said: When the Arabs wanted to compose poetry, they exerted great effort in reflecting upon it, so they called the thing reflected upon and thoroughly pursued "mubayyat," likening it to a line of poetry, in that it is leveled and arranged.

The second remark: The verb is masculine because the feminine of "ṭāʾifah" is not real, and because it carries the sense of "fawj" (group) and "farīq" (party). Ascribing it to "a faction of them" is to show that they are the ones who directly take this up, and the rest are followers of them in that, not because the rest are steadfast in obedience.

﴿And Allah records what they plan by night﴾: i.e., He establishes it in the pages of their deeds, by what He commands His guardian recording angels assigned to the servants, and He will recompense them for it.

Ibn Kathir said: The meaning of this threat is that He, exalted is He, informs that He knows what they conceal and keep secret among themselves, and what they agree upon at night of opposing the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and disobeying him, even though they have shown him obedience and agreement, and He will recompense them for that. End.

It is also permissible that the meaning is: "And Allah records it among what is revealed to you in His Book, so He informs you of their secrets, so that they do not suppose that their concealment will avail them." The aim, on the first reading, is to threaten them, and on the second, to warn them against hypocrisy, because Allah reveals it.

﴿So turn away from them﴾: i.e., keep away from them and do not punish them. ﴿And rely upon Allah﴾: i.e., trust in Allah regarding their affair, for Allah will suffice you against their evil and will avenge Himself upon them. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾: a guardian who is sufficient for victory and dominance for you over them.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 4, verse 82:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Will they not then reflect upon the Qur'an? Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy.﴾ [82]

﴿Will they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?﴾ This is a rebuke and a condemnation of their failure to reflect upon the Qur'an and their turning away from contemplating what it contains of the requirements of faith, so that they might know that it is from Him, exalted is He, by observing the evidences within it, among which is this truthful revelation and the explicit text that exposes their hypocrisy as it actually is.

The root meaning of tadabbur (reflection) is contemplation and consideration of the outcomes and final consequences of a matter specifically, and then it was used for every kind of contemplation, whether it is looking into the reality of a thing and its parts, or its antecedents and causes, or its consequences and outcomes.

﴿Had it been﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿from other than Allah﴾, exalted is He, as they claim, ﴿they would have found in it much discrepancy﴾, in that some of its reports would not correspond to reality, since there is no knowledge of the unseen matters, whether past or future, for anyone other than Him, glorified is He. And since all of them corresponded to reality, it is established that it is from Him, exalted is He.

Al-Zajjaj said: Had it not been from Allah, exalted is He, what it contains of reports about the unseen, of what the hypocrites conceal and what they plot in secret, would have been discrepant, some of it true and some of it false, because the unseen is known only to Allah, exalted is He.

Abu Bakr al-Asamm said: These hypocrites used to conspire in secret in many kinds of deceit and scheming, and Allah, exalted is He, would inform the Messenger, upon him be blessings and peace, of that and tell him of it in detail. It was said to them that if that had not come about through the information of Allah, exalted is He, the truthfulness of it would not have been consistent, and discrepancy would have occurred in it. Since that never happened at all, it is known that it was through His informing. As for interpreting "discrepancy" as contradiction and variation in the eloquence of the composition, this is something that neither the immediate context (siyaq) nor the broader context (sibaq) supports. Abu al-Su'ud conveyed this.

* *

(p-1410) Note:

The verse indicates the obligation of reflection and reasoning, and the view that imitation (taqlid) is invalid, because He, exalted is He, commanded the hypocrites to reason by this proof concerning the soundness of His prophethood. Al-Razi conveyed this.

Also in the verse is an exhortation to reflect upon the Qur'an so that its miraculous nature may be recognized, from its agreement with the sciences, its inclusion of many benefits, the perfection of its proofs and its supreme eloquence, the harmony of its rulings with wisdom, and its past reports agreeing with the books of the earlier peoples and its future reports agreeing with reality.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: Whoever delves deeply into the meanings of the Book of Allah, adhering to what has come in its interpretation from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and from his Companions who witnessed the revelation, and derives from it the rulings that can be deduced from its explicit and implicit meanings, and likewise the meanings of the Sunnah and what it indicates, limiting himself to what is fit to serve as evidence from them, this is the one who is praised and benefits from it, and upon this is to be understood the practice of the jurists of the regions among the Successors and those after them. End quote.

Al-Bukhari related in his Sahih, as a suspended report (ta'liq), from Ibn 'Awn (he is 'Abd Allah al-Basri, one of the younger Successors) that he said: There are three things I love for myself and for my brothers: that they learn this Sunnah and ask about it, that they understand the Qur'an and ask people about it, and that they leave people alone except for good. In another narration, "that they reflect upon it" (fayatadabbaruhu) instead of "that they understand it" (yatafahhamuhu).

Al-Kirmani said: He said "understand it" regarding the Qur'an and "learn it" regarding the Sunnah, because the usual case is that a Muslim learns the Qur'an at the beginning of his affairs, so he does not need to be advised to learn it; therefore he advised understanding its meaning and grasping its explicit content. End quote.

And in the remainder of the verse there is an excuse for the authors regarding the discrepancies and contradictions that occur in their works, because freedom from that is one of the distinctive features of the Qur'an,

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 4, verse 83:

Then He mentioned, may He be exalted, another kind of the corruptions of the hypocrites: their disclosure of the secrets of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and their hastening to spread news of the military expeditions (sarayا) and making it public, in His saying, may He be exalted:

(p-1411) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted:

﴿And when there comes to them a matter of security or fear, they spread it around. But if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them, those who [can] draw it out would have known it from them. And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few.﴾ [83]

﴿And when there comes to them a matter of security or fear﴾ i.e., of that which necessitates one of them, ﴿they spread it around﴾ i.e., they disseminated it. Their spreading of it becomes a corruption from several aspects:

The first: such rumours (irjafat) are never free of much falsehood.

The second: if that news concerned security, they add many embellishments to it, and when those embellishments are not found, this leaves a doubt among the weak regarding the truthfulness of the Messenger (ﷺ), because the hypocrites were narrating those rumours on the authority of the Messenger. And if it concerned fear, the matter becomes confused on account of it for the weak among the Muslims, and they fall into bewilderment and agitation over it. Thus those rumours were a cause of tribulation from this aspect.

The third: rumour is a cause of arousing strong motives toward intense inquiry and thorough investigation, and that is a cause of the exposure of secrets, and that does not accord with the interest of Madinah.

The fourth: the fierce enmity was established between the Muslims and the disbelievers, so whatever was security for one of the two parties was fear for the second party. If news of security for the Muslims arose, and the army and instruments of war were obtained for them, the hypocrites spread rumours about it, and the news reached the disbelievers in the swiftest time, so they began to fortify themselves against the Muslims and to guard against their gaining mastery over them. And if news of fear befell the Muslims, they exaggerated in that and added to it, and cast terror into the hearts of the weak and the destitute. From this it becomes clear that those rumours were generating tribulations and calamities from every aspect. Since the matter was so, Allah, may He be exalted, censured that dissemination and that publicizing, and forbade them from it. Al-Razi related this.

﴿But if they had referred it﴾ i.e., that matter which came to them ﴿to the Messenger and to those of authority among them﴾: they are the senior Companions, the discerning in affairs, may Allah be pleased with them; or those among them who are appointed to command, and they were as if they had not heard it. ﴿would have known it﴾ i.e., the matter (p-1412) ﴿those who draw it out﴾ i.e., who seek to learn it and investigate it, and they are the hypocrites who spread it, ﴿from them﴾ i.e., from the Messenger and those of authority. The meaning is: if they had said, "We will remain silent until we hear it from the Messenger and those mentioned with him, and we will learn the state of the matter from them," they would have known its soundness and whether it is of what should be publicized or not. The relative pronoun was placed in the position of the pronoun, meaning he did not say "they would have known it," for the sake of further establishing the purpose for which the speech is directed, or to censure them, or to alert to their error in probing to extract and reveal the hidden part of that matter.

An-Nasir said in "al-Intisaf": In this verse there is a lesson for everyone who narrates everything he hears, and falsehood is enough for him with that, especially concerning matters such as the expeditions and the enemies who oppose us and those stationed in the very face of the enemy. How great is the corruption in the common people's constant talk about every piece of news they hear from them, good or otherwise. End.

Muslim narrated from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "It is enough of a lie for a man that he narrates everything he hears."

In Abu Dawud and al-Hakim, from him: "It is enough of a sin for a man..." and al-Hakim also narrated it from Abu Umamah.

Furthermore, al-Razi related another view regarding the relative clause, namely that what is meant by it is a group of those of authority. He said: the implied meaning is: "If the hypocrites had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority, the knowledge of it would have been obtained by those among those of authority who derive these events." That is because those of authority are of two groups: some of them are those who derive, and some are not like that.

So His saying "from them" means: those who derive the hidden matters from the groups of those of authority would have known it.

If it is said: if those whom Allah commanded to refer these reports to the Messenger and to those of authority are the hypocrites, how then did He make those of authority "from them" in His saying "and to those of authority among them"? We say: He made those of authority "from them" according to the apparent sense, because the hypocrites (p-1413) display about themselves that they believe.

Its parallel is His saying, may He be exalted: "And indeed among you is he who will surely lag behind" [An-Nisa: 72] and His saying: "They did not do it, except a few of them" [An-Nisa: 66]. End.

On this view is to be understood the statement of al-Suyuti in "al-Iklil": His saying "But if they had referred it..." up to the end of the verse is a great foundation in deduction (istinbat) and ijtihad.

And the statement of al-Mahayimi: So if they found in the Qur'an what appears to be contradiction, it would have been obligatory for them to seek clarification from the Messenger and the scholars who are the people of authority, so that the mujtahids among them would teach them the aspects of reconciliation in deduction.

Some of the Imamiyyah said: the fruit of the verse is that it is obligatory to conceal what its disclosure harms the Muslims, that disseminating it is ugly, that one should not report what has not been known to be sound, and it indicates the prohibition of spreading rumours among the Muslims, and that it is obligatory to refer to scholars in legal opinions, and it indicates the validity of qiyas and ijtihad, because it is istinbat. End.

* *

Note:

What al-Zamakhshari related, and al-Baydawi and Abu al-Su'ud and others followed him in, that His saying "And when there comes to them" refers to a group of the weak among the Muslims: if by the weak they meant the hypocrites, then it is correct; otherwise it is extremely far-fetched, as is known from the context and the flow of the verse. Likewise what they listed of sayings regarding its meaning: all of it has missed the target. What sound taste gives in the verse is the first aspect, and it has an indication of the second aspect which it does not reject. So reflect, and do not be a captive of imitation.

﴿And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾ by sending the Messenger and sending down the Book, ﴿you would have followed Satan﴾ into disbelief and misguidance, ﴿except for a few﴾ i.e., except a few of you, those upon whom Allah bestowed sound reason, so they were guided by it to the truth and the right, and He protected them from following Satan, like those who were guided to the truth in the era of the interval (fatrah), such as Quss ibn Sa'idah and his likes, and they are ten. I have clarified their matter in my book "Idah al-Fitrah fi Ahl al-Fatrah," in the fourteenth chapter, so consult it.

Al-Razi related from Abu Muslim al-Isfahani that what is meant by the bounty of Allah and His mercy here is His victory and His aid, which the hypocrites meant by their saying "that I would achieve a great triumph." i.e., were it not for the successive victory and triumph, you would have followed Satan, and turned away, except a few of you from the believers, from the people of insight, who know that the criterion of truth does not rest on victory at every time. Al-Razi approved this view and said: it is the closest to verification. Al-Khafaji said: because it connects with what follows it.

Furthermore, some claimed that His saying, may He be exalted, "except a few" is an exception from "they spread it" or "would have known it," and they used this to argue that an exception is not necessarily restricted to what precedes it. He said: because if it were an exception from the clause "you would have followed," the meaning would be corrupted, since it would become that the non-following of the few of Satan is not by the bounty of Allah, and that is not sound. The proof of its necessity is that "lawla" is a particle of prohibition of something for the existence of something else, and it has made clear the prohibition of the believers following Satan; so if you make the exception from the last clause, you have necessarily negated the effect of Allah's bounty in preventing following from the excepted part, and made those excepted independent in belief and in disobeying Satan by themselves. Do you not see that if you say to someone you remind of your right over him: "Had it not been for my support of you, your wealth would have been plundered, except a little," how you did not make your support have an effect in preserving the little for the addressee, but you only bestowed upon him the favour of your support's effect in preserving most of his wealth, not all of it. And it is impossible that a Muslim believe that he was protected from any following of Satan except by Allah's bounty upon him. This is the summary of what the author of "al-Intisaf" established, and he exaggerated in it. It is not hidden that restricting the exception to what is adjacent to it and connected with it, since it is the immediate sense, is preferable to restricting it to a distant thing. The necessity claimed is disputed, because the bounty and mercy are meant in a specific sense, which is what we have explained; for the non-following, if it is not by this specific bounty, does not preclude that it be by another bounty. And His saying, may He be exalted:

(p-1415) The Discourse on the Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

﴿So fight in the way of God. You are not burdened except with yourself. And urge the believers. Perhaps God will restrain the might of those who disbelieve. God is stronger in might and stronger in punishment.﴾ [84]

﴿So fight in the way of God﴾ is a change of address (*iltifat*, a shift from one grammatical person to another) and a turning of the address toward the Messenger of God (ﷺ). It is the response to an omitted condition that the noble composition implies. That is, "If the matter is as has been related regarding the disobedience and scheming of the hypocrites, then fight, you alone, paying no mind to what they do." So said Abu al-Su'ud.

﴿You are not burdened except with yourself﴾ means: you are not burdened except with your own action, by advancing to jihad. God is your helper, not the troops. If He wills, He will give you victory alone, just as He gives you victory while thousands are around you. That is, whoever holds back, there is no blame upon you for it, and you will not be held accountable for it.

Al-Razi said: The verse indicates that he (ﷺ) was the bravest of all creatures and the most knowledgeable of how to fight, because God would not have commanded him with this unless he (ﷺ) possessed these qualities. Abu Bakr (may God be pleased with him) followed his example when he sought to go out alone to fight those who withheld the zakat. Whoever knows that the whole matter is in the hand of God, and that no affair occurs except by God's decree, will find this easy.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Abu Ishaq, who said: I asked al-Bara' ibn 'Azib about a man who meets a hundred of the enemy and fights them, and whether he is among those about whom God said: ﴿And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾ [al-Baqarah: 195]? He said: God Almighty said to His Prophet: ﴿So fight in the way of God. You are not burdened except with yourself.﴾

Imam Ahmad also related it from him, who said: I said to al-Bara': A man charges against the polytheists. Is he among those who throw themselves into destruction? He said: No. God sent the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: ﴿So fight in the way of God. You are not burdened except with yourself.﴾ That only applies to spending.

﴿And urge the believers﴾ means: to go out with you and to fight. Encourage them toward it, incite them to it, and strengthen them in it, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said to them on the day of Badr while he was straightening the rows: "Rise up to a Garden whose breadth is the heavens and the earth." Many hadiths have come concerning the encouragement of this, among them:

What al-Bukhari related from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in Paradise there are one hundred levels, which God has prepared for those who strive in the way of God. Between each two levels is the distance between the heaven and the earth."

﴿Perhaps God will restrain﴾: that is, will prevent ﴿the might﴾: that is, the fighting ﴿of those who disbelieve﴾, namely the disbelievers of Makkah. That is, by your urging them to fight, your resolve will move them to confront the enemies and to defend the domain of Islam and its people, to resist them and to persevere against them.

Abu al-Su'ud said: His words, exalted is He, ﴿perhaps﴾ and so on, are a promise from Him, glorified and exalted, whose fulfilment is certain, to restrain the severity and the harm of the disbelievers. What is introduced with *la'alla* and *'asā* (the particles of "perhaps") is established as certain to occur from His, mighty and majestic, side. And so it was, for it is related in the biography (*sirah*) that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) promised Abu Sufyan, after the battle of Uhud, a meeting at the Lesser Badr in Dhu al-Qa'dah. When the appointed time came, he called the people to go out, and he went out in Sha'ban of the fourth year with seventy riders. They reached the appointed place, and God cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, so they turned back from Marr al-Zahran. End of the quotation, with addition.

'Abdullah ibn Rawahah said about this (it is also said it was Ka'b ibn Malik):

We promised Abu Sufyan at Badr, but we found no truthfulness in his appointment, and it was not fulfilled.

I swear, if you had met us and encountered us, you would have returned disgraced, having lost your companions.
