He said: The Banu Ubayriq had said, while we were asking in the house: 'By Allah, we do not think your companion is anyone but Labid ibn Sahl, a man from among us who is righteous and Muslim.' When Labid heard of that, he drew his sword, then came to the Banu Ubayriq and said: 'By Allah, this sword will certainly reach you, or you will make the theft clear!' They said: 'Keep away from us, O man! By Allah, you are not its perpetrator.' We asked in the house until we did not doubt that they were its perpetrators. My uncle said: 'O nephew! If only you would go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mention this to him.'

Qatadah said: So I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! A household among us, people of rudeness, attacked my uncle Rifa'ah, breached his storeroom, and took his weapons and his food. Let them return our weapons to us, but as for the food, we have no need of it.'

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I will look into the matter.' When the Banu Ubayriq heard of that, they came to a man from among them called Usayr ibn 'Urwah, spoke to him about it, and a group of people from the household gathered around him. They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man and his uncle attacked a household from among us, people of Islam and righteousness, accusing them of theft without evidence or certainty.' Qatadah said: 'So I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and spoke to him, and he said: "You attacked a household—among whom are mentioned Islam and righteousness—accusing them of theft without evidence or certainty?"' He said: 'So I returned, and I wished I had lost some of my property (p-1534) and had not spoken to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it. I came to my uncle Rifa'ah, and he said: "O nephew! What have you done?" I told him what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said to me, and he said: "Allah is the One sought for help."'

Not long after, the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, meaning: the Banu Ubayriq.

﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 106], i.e., for what you said to Qatadah. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa: 106]. ﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾ [An-Nisa: 107], i.e., the Banu Ubayriq. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is treacherous and sinful﴾ [An-Nisa: 107]. ﴿They conceal themselves from the people﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], up to His saying: ﴿then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa: 110], i.e., if they seek forgiveness of Allah, He will forgive them. ﴿And whoever earns sin, he earns it only against himself, and ever is Allah Knowing and Wise﴾ [An-Nisa: 111]. ﴿And whoever earns a sin or transgression and then attributes it to an innocent person has borne a slander and a manifest sin﴾ [An-Nisa: 112]. This was their saying to Labid: ﴿Were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, a party of them would have intended to mislead you﴾ [An-Nisa: 113], meaning Usayr and his companions. ﴿But they do not mislead except themselves, and they cannot harm you at all. And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom﴾ [An-Nisa: 113], up to His saying: ﴿then We will give him a great reward﴾ [An-Nisa: 114].

When the Qur'an was revealed, the weapons were brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he returned them to Rifa'ah.

Qatadah said: "When I brought the weapons to my uncle—and he was an old man who had become decrepit in the Jahiliyyah—and I used to think his Islam was tainted, when I brought him the weapons he said: 'O nephew! It is in the way of Allah.' I knew then that his Islam was sound."

(p-1535) When the Qur'an was revealed, Bushayr joined the polytheists, and he stayed with Sulafah, the daughter of Sa'd ibn Shuhayd. Allah revealed concerning him: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers﴾ [An-Nisa: 115], up to His saying: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly strayed far astray﴾ [An-Nisa: 116].

When he stayed with Sulafah, Hassan ibn Thabit satirized him with verses of poetry. So she took his saddle, placed it on her head, went out with it, and threw it in al-Abtah, then said: "You brought me the poetry of Hassan! You never brought me anything good."

Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a strange hadith; we know of no one who transmitted it with a full chain except Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Harrani."

Yunus ibn Bukayr and others narrated this hadith from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah as a mursal report, without mentioning "from his father, from his grandfather."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Hashim ibn al-Qasim al-Harrani, from Muhammad ibn Salamah, part of it. (p-1536) Ibn al-Mundhir narrated it in his "Tafsir" with his chain from Muhammad ibn Salamah, mentioning it in full.

Abu al-Shaykh al-Isfahani narrated it in his "Tafsir" with his chain from Muhammad ibn Salamah, then said at its end: Muhammad ibn Salamah said: "Yahya ibn Ma'in, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Ishaq ibn Isra'il heard this hadith from me."

Al-Hakim narrated it in his "Mustadrak" with his chain, from Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, in a similar meaning, more complete than it, and in it is the poetry. Then he said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of Muslim, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." Thus Ibn Kathir quoted it.

Al-Suyuti said in "al-Lubab": Ibn Sa'd recorded in "al-Tabaqat," with his chain, from Mahmud ibn Labid, who said: "Bushayr ibn al-Harith attacked the upper room of Rifa'ah ibn Zayd, the uncle of Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man, breached it from its back, and took his food and two coats of mail with their equipment. Qatadah came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him of that. He summoned Bushayr and questioned him, and he denied it, and he attributed it to Labid ibn Sahl, a man from the household who had lineage and nobility. So the Qur'an was revealed refuting Bushayr and clearing Labid: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾, the verses. When the Qur'an was revealed concerning Bushayr and he was exposed, he fled to Mecca as an apostate, and he stayed with Sulafah, daughter of Sa'd. He began to slander the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Muslims, and it was revealed concerning him: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger﴾ [An-Nisa: 115], [An-Nisa: from verse 115], the verse. Hassan ibn Thabit satirized him until he returned. That was in the month of Rabi' in the fourth year after the Hijrah." End of quotation.

As for the clarification of the words of the verses and their fruits, we say: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾ means: by what He made you know, informed you of, and revealed to you. That knowledge is called "seeing" because certain knowledge free of doubt operates like sight in strength and clarity.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It is narrated from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him): "None of you should say: 'I judged by what Allah has shown me,' for Allah did not grant that except to His Prophet (ﷺ). Rather, let him exert his opinion (*ijtihad*), for the opinion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was correct, because Allah used to show it to him. As for us, it is conjecture and presumption."

I say: al-Bayhaqi in "al-Madkhal" and Ibn 'Abd al-Barr narrated this report with a similar wording.

Ibn al-Furs said: In this verse is the establishment of opinion (*ra'y*) and analogy (*qiyas*). Al-Suyuti refuted him with what Ibn Abi Hatim recorded (p-1537) from Ibn Abbas that he said: "Beware of opinion, for Allah, Exalted is He, said to His Prophet: ﴿that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾ and did not say: 'by what you saw.'"

Then al-Suyuti said: Others said: His saying ﴿by what Allah has shown you﴾ may include both revelation and independent reasoning (*ijtihad*) together. End of quotation.

Ibn Kathir said: Those among the scholars of usul (legal theory) who hold that the Prophet ﷺ had the right to judge by ijtihad (independent reasoning) have argued from this verse, and from what is established in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) on the authority of Umm Salamah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard the clamour of litigants at the door of his chamber, so he came out to them and said: "Indeed I am only a human being, and I judge only according to what I hear. Perhaps one of you is more eloquent in his argument than another, so I rule in his favour. Whomever I rule in favour of with the right of a Muslim, it is merely a piece of the Fire, so let him take it or leave it."

Imam Ahmad also narrated it from her with the wording: "Two men from the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disputing about inheritances between them which had become obscure, and there was no proof between them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'You bring your disputes to me, and I am only a human being. Perhaps some of you is more eloquent in his argument (or he said: for his argument) than another, so I judge between you according to what I hear. Whoever I give him something of his brother's right, let him not take it, for I am only cutting for him a piece of the Fire, which he will bring on his neck as a collar on the Day of Resurrection.' The two men wept, and each of them said: 'My right is for my brother.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'As for when you have said that, go and divide it, then seek out the right between you, then draw lots, then let each of you absolve his companion.'"

Abu Dawud narrated it and added: "Indeed I judge between you by my opinion, regarding matters on which nothing has been revealed to me." End quote.

(p-1538) Al-Suyuti said: In the verse there is a refutation of those who permit the judge to be non-knowledgeable, because Allah the Exalted delegated judgment to ijtihad, and one who has no knowledge, how can he perform ijtihad?! End quote.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾, meaning: do not argue on their behalf or defend them, and they are Tu'mah and whoever supports him from his people in what has preceded. ﴿Disputant﴾, meaning: one who disputes. In it is that it is not permissible for anyone to dispute on behalf of anyone unless he knows that he is in the right.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 106], meaning: for what you said to Qatadah, as has preceded explained.

Al-Razi said: Those who hold that sins may proceed from the prophets have clung to this verse, and they said: If no sin had occurred from the Messenger ﷺ, he would not have been commanded to seek forgiveness. Then he answered that with several points.

Qadi Iyad said in "al-Shifa": The actions of the prophets, peace be upon them, in matters they were neither forbidden from nor commanded to do, and then were reproached for because of them, or did them by way of interpretation, are only sins in relation to the exaltedness of their station and the perfection of their obedience, not like the sins and disobediences of others, and he extended discussion on this point and pleased with it.

Then he said: Also, in repentance and seeking forgiveness there is another subtle meaning which some scholars indicated, which is seeking the love of Allah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are oft-repenting and loves those who purify themselves﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 222] [Al-Baqarah: part of verse 222]. End quote.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾ [An-Nisa: 107], meaning: they betray them through disobedience. The disobedience of the disobedient is made a betrayal by them of themselves, just as it is made an injustice to themselves, because its harm returns to them.

Al-Razi said: Know that in the verse there is a severe warning, because when the Prophet ﷺ's inclination slightly tilted toward the side of Tu'mah, while it was in Allah's knowledge that Tu'mah was a wicked man, Allah the Exalted reproached His Messenger for that degree of assisting the wrongdoer. So how is the state of one who knows of the oppressor that he is an oppressor, then assists him in that oppression, indeed drives him to it and encourages him to it with the utmost encouragement?! End quote.

It was said "for the treacherous" (p-1539) (and "yakhtanun") although the treacherous is one person, because what is meant by it is him and whoever supported him from his people, and they knew that he was a thief; or it was mentioned in the plural form so that it would include him and everyone who betrays his betrayal. Just as it was mentioned in the form of intensification in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is habitually treacherous and sinful﴾ [An-Nisa: 107], because He, the Exalted, knew of him that he was excessive in betrayal and in committing sins, and what supports this is that he fled to Makkah and apostatized, as we have mentioned earlier.

It is said: If you stumble upon an evil deed from a man, know that it has siblings. It is related from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he ordered the cutting off of the hand of a thief, and his mother came weeping and said: "This is the first theft he has committed, so pardon him." He said: "You have lied; indeed Allah does not take His servant to account for the first time."

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They hide from people﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], meaning: they conceal themselves out of shame before them and fear of their harm. ﴿And they cannot hide from Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], so they are not shy before Him. ﴿And He is with them﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], meaning: He is aware of them and watches over them; nothing of their secret is hidden from Him.

Al-Zamakhshari said: This verse is sufficient as a rebuke of people for what they are in of little shame and fear of their Lord, while they know, if they are believers, that they are in His presence, with no concealment, no heedlessness, and no absence; there remains only clear exposure and disgrace.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When they plot by night what He does not approve of in speech﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], meaning: they devise and fabricate false oaths, the slandering of the innocent, and false testimony.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Here you are—you argued on their behalf in this worldly life﴾ [An-Nisa: 109] and the rest of the verse. Mujadalah is the most intense contention. The meaning: suppose you disputed on behalf of the thief and his people in this world, who will dispute on their behalf in the Hereafter when Allah seizes them with His punishment?!

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or who will be a guardian over them?﴾ [An-Nisa: 109], meaning: a protector and defender from the might and vengeance of Allah the Exalted.

Some of the commentators of the Zaydiyyah said: The fruit of these verses is the obligation to judge without favouritism or inclination, and the prohibition of partisanship and of disputing on behalf of every treacherous and disobedient person. The restriction of the prohibition on disputing to "those who betray themselves" indicates the permissibility of disputing. End quote.

Know that when He, the Exalted, mentioned the threat in this matter, He followed it with a call to repentance, with His saying, Glorified is He:

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 4, verses 105–109 (part 1 of 2):**

(p-1530) On the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the treacherous.﴾ [105]

﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [An-Nisa: 106] [106]

﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not love one who is treacherous and sinful.﴾ [An-Nisa: 107] [107]

﴿They conceal themselves from the people, but they cannot conceal themselves from Allah, and He is with them when they plot at night in speech that does not please Him. And ever is Allah, of what they do, encompassing.﴾ [An-Nisa: 108] [108]

﴿There you are, those who argued on their behalf in this worldly life, but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their guardian?﴾ [An-Nisa: 109] [109]

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the treacherous.﴾

﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [An-Nisa: 106]

﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not love one who is treacherous and sinful.﴾ [An-Nisa: 107]

﴿They conceal themselves from the people, but they cannot conceal themselves from Allah, and He is with them when they plot at night in speech that does not please Him. And ever is Allah, of what they do, encompassing.﴾ [An-Nisa: 108]

﴿There you are, those who argued on their behalf in this worldly life, but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their guardian?﴾ [An-Nisa: 109]

(p-1531) Al-Hafiz Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through al-Awfi, from Ibn Abbas: "A group of the Ansar went out on one of the expeditions with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and a coat of mail (dir') belonging to one of them was stolen. A man from the Ansar was suspected of it (*fa-uzinna*, i.e., he was accused). The owner of the coat of mail came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'Indeed, Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq stole my coat of mail.' When the thief saw that, he went to it and threw it into the house of an innocent man, and said to a group of his tribe: 'I have hidden the coat of mail and thrown it into the house of so-and-so, and it will be found with him.'

They went to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) at night and said: 'O Prophet of Allah! Our companion is innocent, and the owner of the coat of mail is so-and-so, and we have knowledge of this matter. So excuse our companion before the people and argue on his behalf, for if Allah does not protect him through you, he will be destroyed.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, declared him innocent, and excused him before the people. So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down﴾, the verse." Then He, Exalted, said to those who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concealing themselves with falsehood: ﴿They conceal themselves from the people, but they cannot conceal themselves from Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], meaning those who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concealing themselves and argued on behalf of the treacherous.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And whoever does wrong﴾ [An-Nisa: 110], the verse, meaning those who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concealing themselves with falsehood. Then He said: ﴿And whoever earns a sin or transgression and then attributes it to an innocent person has borne a slander and a manifest sin﴾ [An-Nisa: 112], meaning the thief and those who argued on behalf of the thief.

Ibn Kathir said: "This context is unusual. Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd and others mentioned (concerning this verse) that it was revealed about the thief of the Banu Ubayriq, with differing contexts, though they are close in meaning."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated this story at length, and Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi narrated it from him, through his route, in his "Jami'" in the Book of Tafsir, from Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: (p-1532) "There was a household among us called the Banu Ubayriq: Bishr, Bushayr (Abu Dharr al-Khushani said: 'Bashir ibn Ubayriq'; thus it occurs here as *Bashir* with a fatha on the ba'; al-Daraqutni said: it is only *Bushayr* with a damma on the ba'), and Mubashshir. Bushayr was a hypocrite, and he used to compose poetry satirizing the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then he would attribute it to some of the Arabs, saying: 'So-and-so said such-and-such, or so-and-so said such-and-such.' When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard that poetry, they said: 'By Allah, no one composes this poetry except the wicked one.' He said:

*Do men compose a poem, and they are accused, and they say: 'The son of al-Ubayriq composed it'?*

He said: They were a household of poverty and need, in the Jahiliyyah and in Islam. The people's food in Medina was dates and barley. When a man had means, a caravan (*dafitah*) would come from Syria with fine flour (*al-darmak*), and the man would buy from it and reserve it for himself, while his dependents had only dates and barley. A caravan came from Syria, and my uncle Rifa'ah ibn Zayd bought a load of fine flour, and placed it in a storeroom (*mashrubah*) of his, in which he had weapons: two coats of mail, two swords, and what was needed for them. Someone attacked him from beneath the house, the storeroom was breached, and the food and weapons were taken. When morning came, my uncle Rifa'ah came to me and said: 'O nephew! You know that we were attacked during this night; our storeroom was breached, and our food and weapons were taken away.'

(p-1533) He said: I searched the house and asked, and it was said to us: 'We saw the Banu Ubayriq kindle a fire this night, and we do not think, as far as we can see, that it was except on some of your food.'

He said: The Banu Ubayriq had said, while we were asking in the house: 'By Allah, we do not think your companion is anyone but Labid ibn Sahl, a man from among us who is righteous and Muslim.' When Labid heard of that, he drew his sword, then came to the Banu Ubayriq and said: 'By Allah, this sword will certainly reach you, or you will make the theft clear!' They said: 'Keep away from us, O man! By Allah, you are not its perpetrator.' We asked in the house until we did not doubt that they were its perpetrators. My uncle said: 'O nephew! If only you would go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mention this to him.'

Qatadah said: So I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Al-Zamakhshari said: It is narrated from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him): "None of you should say: 'I judged by what Allah has shown me,' for Allah did not grant that except to His Prophet (ﷺ). Rather, let him exert his opinion (*ijtihad*), for the opinion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was correct, because Allah used to show it to him. As for us, it is conjecture and presumption."

I say: al-Bayhaqi in "al-Madkhal" and Ibn 'Abd al-Barr narrated this report with a similar wording.

Ibn al-Furs said: In this verse is the establishment of opinion (*ra'y*) and analogy (*qiyas*). Al-Suyuti refuted him with what Ibn Abi Hatim recorded (p-1537) from Ibn Abbas that he said: "Beware of opinion, for Allah, Exalted is He, said to His Prophet: ﴿that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾ and did not say: 'by what you saw.'"

Then al-Suyuti said: Others said: His saying ﴿by what Allah has shown you﴾ may include both revelation and independent reasoning (*ijtihad*) together. End of quotation.

Ibn Kathir said: Those among the scholars of usul (legal theory) who hold that the Prophet ﷺ had the right to judge by ijtihad (independent reasoning) have argued from this verse, and from what is established in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) on the authority of Umm Salamah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard the clamour of litigants at the door of his chamber, so he came out to them and said: "Indeed I am only a human being, and I judge only according to what I hear. Perhaps one of you is more eloquent in his argument than another, so I rule in his favour. Whomever I rule in favour of with the right of a Muslim, it is merely a piece of the Fire, so let him take it or leave it."

Imam Ahmad also narrated it from her with the wording: "Two men from the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disputing about inheritances between them which had become obscure, and there was no proof between them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'You bring your disputes to me, and I am only a human being. Perhaps some of you is more eloquent in his argument (or he said: for his argument) than another, so I judge between you according to what I hear. Whoever I give him something of his brother's right, let him not take it, for I am only cutting for him a piece of the Fire, which he will bring on his neck as a collar on the Day of Resurrection.' The two men wept, and each of them said: 'My right is for my brother.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'As for when you have said that, go and divide it, then seek out the right between you, then draw lots, then let each of you absolve his companion.'"

Abu Dawud narrated it and added: "Indeed I judge between you by my opinion, regarding matters on which nothing has been revealed to me." End quote.

(p-1538) Al-Suyuti said: In the verse there is a refutation of those who permit the judge to be non-knowledgeable, because Allah the Exalted delegated judgment to ijtihad, and one who has no knowledge, how can he perform ijtihad?! End quote.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾, meaning: do not argue on their behalf or defend them, and they are Tu'mah and whoever supports him from his people in what has preceded. ﴿Disputant﴾, meaning: one who disputes. In it is that it is not permissible for anyone to dispute on behalf of anyone unless he knows that he is in the right.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 106], meaning: for what you said to Qatadah, as has preceded explained.

Al-Razi said: Those who hold that sins may proceed from the prophets have clung to this verse, and they said: If no sin had occurred from the Messenger ﷺ, he would not have been commanded to seek forgiveness. Then he answered that with several points.

Qadi Iyad said in "al-Shifa": The actions of the prophets, peace be upon them, in matters they were neither forbidden from nor commanded to do, and then were reproached for because of them, or did them by way of interpretation, are only sins in relation to the exaltedness of their station and the perfection of their obedience, not like the sins and disobediences of others, and he extended discussion on this point and pleased with it.

Then he said: Also, in repentance and seeking forgiveness there is another subtle meaning which some scholars indicated, which is seeking the love of Allah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are oft-repenting and loves those who purify themselves﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 222] [Al-Baqarah: part of verse 222]. End quote.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾ [An-Nisa: 107], meaning: they betray them through disobedience. The disobedience of the disobedient is made a betrayal by them of themselves, just as it is made an injustice to themselves, because its harm returns to them.

Al-Razi said: Know that in the verse there is a severe warning, because when the Prophet ﷺ's inclination slightly tilted toward the side of Tu'mah, while it was in Allah's knowledge that Tu'mah was a wicked man, Allah the Exalted reproached His Messenger for that degree of assisting the wrongdoer. So how is the state of one who knows of the oppressor that he is an oppressor, then assists him in that oppression, indeed drives him to it and encourages him to it with the utmost encouragement?! End quote.

It was said "for the treacherous" (p-1539) (and "yakhtanun") although the treacherous is one person, because what is meant by it is him and whoever supported him from his people, and they knew that he was a thief; or it was mentioned in the plural form so that it would include him and everyone who betrays his betrayal. Just as it was mentioned in the form of intensification in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is habitually treacherous and sinful﴾ [An-Nisa: 107], because He, the Exalted, knew of him that he was excessive in betrayal and in committing sins, and what supports this is that he fled to Makkah and apostatized, as we have mentioned earlier.

It is said: If you stumble upon an evil deed from a man, know that it has siblings. It is related from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he ordered the cutting off of the hand of a thief, and his mother came weeping and said: "This is the first theft he has committed, so pardon him." He said: "You have lied; indeed Allah does not take His servant to account for the first time."

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They hide from people﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], meaning: they conceal themselves out of shame before them and fear of their harm. ﴿And they cannot hide from Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], so they are not shy before Him. ﴿And He is with them﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], meaning: He is aware of them and watches over them; nothing of their secret is hidden from Him.

Al-Zamakhshari said: This verse is sufficient as a rebuke of people for what they are in of little shame and fear of their Lord, while they know, if they are believers, that they are in His presence, with no concealment, no heedlessness, and no absence; there remains only clear exposure and disgrace.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When they plot by night what He does not approve of in speech﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], meaning: they devise and fabricate false oaths, the slandering of the innocent, and false testimony.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Here you are—you argued on their behalf in this worldly life﴾ [An-Nisa: 109] and the rest of the verse. Mujadalah is the most intense contention. The meaning: suppose you disputed on behalf of the thief and his people in this world, who will dispute on their behalf in the Hereafter when Allah seizes them with His punishment?!

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or who will be a guardian over them?﴾ [An-Nisa: 109], meaning: a protector and defender from the might and vengeance of Allah the Exalted.

Some of the commentators of the Zaydiyyah said: The fruit of these verses is the obligation to judge without favouritism or inclination, and the prohibition of partisanship and of disputing on behalf of every treacherous and disobedient person. The restriction of the prohibition on disputing to "those who betray themselves" indicates the permissibility of disputing. End quote.

Know that when He, the Exalted, mentioned the threat in this matter, He followed it with a call to repentance, with His saying, Glorified is He:

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 4, verses 105–109 (part 1 of 2):**

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the treacherous.﴾ [105]

﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [An-Nisa: 106] [106]

﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not love one who is treacherous and sinful.﴾ [An-Nisa: 107] [107]

﴿They conceal themselves from the people, but they cannot conceal themselves from Allah, and He is with them when they plot at night in speech that does not please Him. And ever is Allah, of what they do, encompassing.﴾ [An-Nisa: 108] [108]

﴿There you are, those who argued on their behalf in this worldly life, but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their guardian?﴾ [An-Nisa: 109] [109]

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the treacherous.﴾

﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [An-Nisa: 106]

﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not love one who is treacherous and sinful.﴾ [An-Nisa: 107]

﴿They conceal themselves from the people, but they cannot conceal themselves from Allah, and He is with them when they plot at night in speech that does not please Him. And ever is Allah, of what they do, encompassing.﴾ [An-Nisa: 108]

﴿There you are, those who argued on their behalf in this worldly life, but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their guardian?﴾ [An-Nisa: 109]

(p-1531) Al-Hafiz Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through al-Awfi, from Ibn Abbas: "A group of the Ansar went out on one of the expeditions with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and a coat of mail (dir') belonging to one of them was stolen. A man from the Ansar was suspected of it (*fa-uzinna*, i.e., he was accused). The owner of the coat of mail came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'Indeed, Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq stole my coat of mail.' When the thief saw that, he went to it and threw it into the house of an innocent man, and said to a group of his tribe: 'I have hidden the coat of mail and thrown it into the house of so-and-so, and it will be found with him.'

They went to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) at night and said: 'O Prophet of Allah! Our companion is innocent, and the owner of the coat of mail is so-and-so, and we have knowledge of this matter. So excuse our companion before the people and argue on his behalf, for if Allah does not protect him through you, he will be destroyed.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, declared him innocent, and excused him before the people. So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down﴾, the verse." Then He, Exalted, said to those who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concealing themselves with falsehood: ﴿They conceal themselves from the people, but they cannot conceal themselves from Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], meaning those who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concealing themselves and argued on behalf of the treacherous.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And whoever does wrong﴾ [An-Nisa: 110], the verse, meaning those who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concealing themselves with falsehood. Then He said: ﴿And whoever earns a sin or transgression and then attributes it to an innocent person has borne a slander and a manifest sin﴾ [An-Nisa: 112], meaning the thief and those who argued on behalf of the thief.

Ibn Kathir said: "This context is unusual. Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd and others mentioned (concerning this verse) that it was revealed about the thief of the Banu Ubayriq, with differing contexts, though they are close in meaning."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated this story at length, and Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi narrated it from him, through his route, in his "Jami'" in the Book of Tafsir, from Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: (p-1532) "There was a household among us called the Banu Ubayriq: Bishr, Bushayr (Abu Dharr al-Khushani said: 'Bashir ibn Ubayriq'; thus it occurs here as *Bashir* with a fatha on the ba'; al-Daraqutni said: it is only *Bushayr* with a damma on the ba'), and Mubashshir. Bushayr was a hypocrite, and he used to compose poetry satirizing the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then he would attribute it to some of the Arabs, saying: 'So-and-so said such-and-such, or so-and-so said such-and-such.' When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard that poetry, they said: 'By Allah, no one composes this poetry except the wicked one.' He said:

*Do men compose a poem, and they are accused, and they say: 'The son of al-Ubayriq composed it'?*

He said: They were a household of poverty and need, in the Jahiliyyah and in Islam. The people's food in Medina was dates and barley. When a man had means, a caravan (*dafitah*) would come from Syria with fine flour (*al-darmak*), and the man would buy from it and reserve it for himself, while his dependents had only dates and barley. A caravan came from Syria, and my uncle Rifa'ah ibn Zayd bought a load of fine flour, and placed it in a storeroom (*mashrubah*) of his, in which he had weapons: two coats of mail, two swords, and what was needed for them. Someone attacked him from beneath the house, the storeroom was breached, and the food and weapons were taken. When morning came, my uncle Rifa'ah came to me and said: 'O nephew! You know that we were attacked during this night; our storeroom was breached, and our food and weapons were taken away.'

(p-1533) He said: I searched the house and asked, and it was said to us: 'We saw the Banu Ubayriq kindle a fire this night, and we do not think, as far as we can see, that it was except on some of your food.'

He said: The Banu Ubayriq had said, while we were asking in the house: 'By Allah, we do not think your companion is anyone but Labid ibn Sahl, a man from among us who is righteous and Muslim.' When Labid heard of that, he drew his sword, then came to the Banu Ubayriq and said: 'By Allah, this sword will certainly reach you, or you will make the theft clear!' They said: 'Keep away from us, O man! By Allah, you are not its perpetrator.' We asked in the house until we did not doubt that they were its perpetrators. My uncle said: 'O nephew! If only you would go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mention this to him.'

Qatadah said: So I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! A household among us, people of rudeness, attacked my uncle Rifa'ah, breached his storeroom, and took his weapons and his food. Let them return our weapons to us, but as for the food, we have no need of it.'

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I will look into the matter.' When the Banu Ubayriq heard of that, they came to a man from among them called Usayr ibn 'Urwah, spoke to him about it, and a group of people from the household gathered around him. They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man and his uncle attacked a household from among us, people of Islam and righteousness, accusing them of theft without evidence or certainty.' Qatadah said: 'So I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and spoke to him, and he said: "You attacked a household—among whom are mentioned Islam and righteousness—accusing them of theft without evidence or certainty?"' He said: 'So I returned, and I wished I had lost some of my property (p-1534) and had not spoken to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it. I came to my uncle Rifa'ah, and he said: "O nephew! What have you done?" I told him what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said to me, and he said: "Allah is the One sought for help."'

Not long after, the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, meaning: the Banu Ubayriq.

This was their saying to Labid: ﴿Were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, a party of them would have intended to mislead you﴾ [An-Nisa: 113], meaning Usayr and his companions. ﴿But they do not mislead except themselves, and they cannot harm you at all. And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom﴾ [An-Nisa: 113], up to His saying: ﴿then We will give him a great reward﴾ [An-Nisa: 114].

When the Qur'an was revealed, the weapons were brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he returned them to Rifa'ah.

Qatadah said: "When I brought the weapons to my uncle—and he was an old man who had become decrepit in the Jahiliyyah—and I used to think his Islam was tainted, when I brought him the weapons he said: 'O nephew! It is in the way of Allah.' I knew then that his Islam was sound."

The meaning: suppose you disputed on behalf of the thief and his people in this world, who will dispute on their behalf in the Hereafter when Allah seizes them with His punishment?!

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or who will be a guardian over them?﴾ [An-Nisa: 109], meaning: a protector and defender from the might and vengeance of Allah the Exalted.

Some of the commentators of the Zaydiyyah said: The fruit of these verses is the obligation to judge without favouritism or inclination, and the prohibition of partisanship and of disputing on behalf of every treacherous and disobedient person. The restriction of the prohibition on disputing to "those who betray themselves" indicates the permissibility of disputing. End quote.

Know that when He, the Exalted, mentioned the threat in this matter, He followed it with a call to repentance, with His saying, Glorified is He:

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 4, verses 105–109 (part 1 of 2):**

(p-1530) On the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the treacherous.﴾ [105]

﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [An-Nisa: 106] [106]

﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not love one who is treacherous and sinful.﴾ [An-Nisa: 107] [107]

﴿They conceal themselves from the people, but they cannot conceal themselves from Allah, and He is with them when they plot at night in speech that does not please Him. And ever is Allah, of what they do, encompassing.﴾ [An-Nisa: 108] [108]

﴿There you are, those who argued on their behalf in this worldly life, but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their guardian?﴾ [An-Nisa: 109] [109]

﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the treacherous.﴾

﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [An-Nisa: 106]

﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not love one who is treacherous and sinful.﴾ [An-Nisa: 107]

﴿They conceal themselves from the people, but they cannot conceal themselves from Allah, and He is with them when they plot at night in speech that does not please Him. And ever is Allah, of what they do, encompassing.﴾ [An-Nisa: 108]

﴿There you are, those who argued on their behalf in this worldly life, but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their guardian?﴾ [An-Nisa: 109]

(p-1531) Al-Hafiz Ibn Mardawayh narrated, through al-Awfi, from Ibn Abbas: "A group of the Ansar went out on one of the expeditions with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and a coat of mail (dir') belonging to one of them was stolen. A man from the Ansar was suspected of it (*fa-uzinna*, i.e., he was accused). The owner of the coat of mail came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'Indeed, Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq stole my coat of mail.' When the thief saw that, he went to it and threw it into the house of an innocent man, and said to a group of his tribe: 'I have hidden the coat of mail and thrown it into the house of so-and-so, and it will be found with him.'

They went to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) at night and said: 'O Prophet of Allah! Our companion is innocent, and the owner of the coat of mail is so-and-so, and we have knowledge of this matter. So excuse our companion before the people and argue on his behalf, for if Allah does not protect him through you, he will be destroyed.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, declared him innocent, and excused him before the people. So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down﴾, the verse." Then He, Exalted, said to those who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concealing themselves with falsehood: ﴿They conceal themselves from the people, but they cannot conceal themselves from Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], meaning those who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concealing themselves and argued on behalf of the treacherous.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And whoever does wrong﴾ [An-Nisa: 110], the verse, meaning those who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concealing themselves with falsehood. Then He said: ﴿And whoever earns a sin or transgression and then attributes it to an innocent person has borne a slander and a manifest sin﴾ [An-Nisa: 112], meaning the thief and those who argued on behalf of the thief.

Ibn Kathir said: "This context is unusual. Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd and others mentioned (concerning this verse) that it was revealed about the thief of the Banu Ubayriq, with differing contexts, though they are close in meaning."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated this story at length, and Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi narrated it from him, through his route, in his "Jami'" in the Book of Tafsir, from Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: (p-1532) "There was a household among us called the Banu Ubayriq: Bishr, Bushayr (Abu Dharr al-Khushani said: 'Bashir ibn Ubayriq'; thus it occurs here as *Bashir* with a fatha on the ba'; al-Daraqutni said: it is only *Bushayr* with a damma on the ba'), and Mubashshir. Bushayr was a hypocrite, and he used to compose poetry satirizing the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then he would attribute it to some of the Arabs, saying: 'So-and-so said such-and-such, or so-and-so said such-and-such.' When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard that poetry, they said: 'By Allah, no one composes this poetry except the wicked one.' He said:

*Do men compose a poem, and they are accused, and they say: 'The son of al-Ubayriq composed it'?*

He said: They were a household of poverty and need, in the Jahiliyyah and in Islam. The people's food in Medina was dates and barley. When a man had means, a caravan (*dafitah*) would come from Syria with fine flour (*al-darmak*), and the man would buy from it and reserve it for himself, while his dependents had only dates and barley. A caravan came from Syria, and my uncle Rifa'ah ibn Zayd bought a load of fine flour, and placed it in a storeroom (*mashrubah*) of his, in which he had weapons: two coats of mail, two swords, and what was needed for them. Someone attacked him from beneath the house, the storeroom was breached, and the food and weapons were taken. When morning came, my uncle Rifa'ah came to me and said: 'O nephew! You know that we were attacked during this night; our storeroom was breached, and our food and weapons were taken away.'

(p-1533) He said: I searched the house and asked, and it was said to us: 'We saw the Banu Ubayriq kindle a fire this night, and we do not think, as far as we can see, that it was except on some of your food.'

He said: The Banu Ubayriq had said, while we were asking in the house: 'By Allah, we do not think your companion is anyone but Labid ibn Sahl, a man from among us who is righteous and Muslim.' When Labid heard of that, he drew his sword, then came to the Banu Ubayriq and said: 'By Allah, this sword will certainly reach you, or you will make the theft clear!' They said: 'Keep away from us, O man! By Allah, you are not its perpetrator.' We asked in the house until we did not doubt that they were its perpetrators. My uncle said: 'O nephew! If only you would go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mention this to him.'

Qatadah said: So I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! A household among us, people of rudeness, attacked my uncle Rifa'ah, breached his storeroom, and took his weapons and his food. Let them return our weapons to us, but as for the food, we have no need of it.'

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I will look into the matter.' When the Banu Ubayriq heard of that, they came to a man from among them called Usayr ibn 'Urwah, spoke to him about it, and a group of people from the household gathered around him. They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man and his uncle attacked a household from among us, people of Islam and righteousness, accusing them of theft without evidence or certainty.' Qatadah said: 'So I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and spoke to him, and he said: "You attacked a household—among whom are mentioned Islam and righteousness—accusing them of theft without evidence or certainty?"' He said: 'So I returned, and I wished I had lost some of my property (p-1534) and had not spoken to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it. I came to my uncle Rifa'ah, and he said: "O nephew! What have you done?" I told him what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said to me, and he said: "Allah is the One sought for help."'

Not long after, the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, meaning: the Banu Ubayriq.

﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 106], i.e., for what you said to Qatadah. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa: 106]. ﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾ [An-Nisa: 107], i.e., the Banu Ubayriq. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is treacherous and sinful﴾ [An-Nisa: 107]. ﴿They conceal themselves from the people﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], up to His saying: ﴿then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa: 110], i.e., if they seek forgiveness of Allah, He will forgive them. ﴿And whoever earns sin, he earns it only against himself, and ever is Allah Knowing and Wise﴾ [An-Nisa: 111]. ﴿And whoever earns a sin or transgression and then attributes it to an innocent person has borne a slander and a manifest sin﴾ [An-Nisa: 112]. This was their saying to Labid: ﴿Were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, a party of them would have intended to mislead you﴾ [An-Nisa: 113], meaning Usayr and his companions. ﴿But they do not mislead except themselves, and they cannot harm you at all. And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom﴾ [An-Nisa: 113], up to His saying: ﴿then We will give him a great reward﴾ [An-Nisa: 114].

When the Qur'an was revealed, the weapons were brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he returned them to Rifa'ah.

Qatadah said: "When I brought the weapons to my uncle—and he was an old man who had become decrepit in the Jahiliyyah—and I used to think his Islam was tainted, when I brought him the weapons he said: 'O nephew! It is in the way of Allah.' I knew then that his Islam was sound."

(p-1535) When the Qur'an was revealed, Bushayr joined the polytheists, and he stayed with Sulafah, the daughter of Sa'd ibn Shuhayd. Allah revealed concerning him: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers﴾ [An-Nisa: 115], up to His saying: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly strayed far astray﴾ [An-Nisa: 116].

When he stayed with Sulafah, Hassan ibn Thabit satirized him with verses of poetry. So she took his saddle, placed it on her head, went out with it, and threw it in al-Abtah, then said: "You brought me the poetry of Hassan! You never brought me anything good."

Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a strange hadith; we know of no one who transmitted it with a full chain except Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Harrani."

Yunus ibn Bukayr and others narrated this hadith from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah as a mursal report, without mentioning "from his father, from his grandfather."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Hashim ibn al-Qasim al-Harrani, from Muhammad ibn Salamah, part of it. (p-1536) Ibn al-Mundhir narrated it in his "Tafsir" with his chain from Muhammad ibn Salamah, mentioning it in full.

Abu al-Shaykh al-Isfahani narrated it in his "Tafsir" with his chain from Muhammad ibn Salamah, then said at its end: Muhammad ibn Salamah said: "Yahya ibn Ma'in, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Ishaq ibn Isra'il heard this hadith from me."

Al-Hakim narrated it in his "Mustadrak" with his chain, from Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, in a similar meaning, more complete than it, and in it is the poetry. Then he said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of Muslim, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." Thus Ibn Kathir quoted it.

Al-Suyuti said in "al-Lubab": Ibn Sa'd recorded in "al-Tabaqat," with his chain, from Mahmud ibn Labid, who said: "Bushayr ibn al-Harith attacked the upper room of Rifa'ah ibn Zayd, the uncle of Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man, breached it from its back, and took his food and two coats of mail with their equipment. Qatadah came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him of that. He summoned Bushayr and questioned him, and he denied it, and he attributed it to Labid ibn Sahl, a man from the household who had lineage and nobility. So the Qur'an was revealed refuting Bushayr and clearing Labid: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾, the verses. When the Qur'an was revealed concerning Bushayr and he was exposed, he fled to Mecca as an apostate, and he stayed with Sulafah, daughter of Sa'd. He began to slander the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Muslims, and it was revealed concerning him: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger﴾ [An-Nisa: 115], [An-Nisa: from verse 115], the verse. Hassan ibn Thabit satirized him until he returned. That was in the month of Rabi' in the fourth year after the Hijrah." End of quotation.

As for the clarification of the words of the verses and their fruits, we say: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾ means: by what He made you know, informed you of, and revealed to you. That knowledge is called "seeing" because certain knowledge free of doubt operates like sight in strength and clarity.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It is narrated from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him): "None of you should say: 'I judged by what Allah has shown me,' for Allah did not grant that except to His Prophet (ﷺ). Rather, let him exert his opinion (*ijtihad*), for the opinion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was correct, because Allah used to show it to him. As for us, it is conjecture and presumption."

I say: al-Bayhaqi in "al-Madkhal" and Ibn 'Abd al-Barr narrated this report with a similar wording.

Ibn al-Furs said: In this verse is the establishment of opinion (*ra'y*) and analogy (*qiyas*). Al-Suyuti refuted him with what Ibn Abi Hatim recorded (p-1537) from Ibn Abbas that he said: "Beware of opinion, for Allah, Exalted is He, said to His Prophet: ﴿that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾ and did not say: 'by what you saw.'"

Then al-Suyuti said: Others said: His saying ﴿by what Allah has shown you﴾ may include both revelation and independent reasoning (*ijtihad*) together. End of quotation.

Ibn Kathir said: Those among the scholars of usul (legal theory) who hold that the Prophet ﷺ had the right to judge by ijtihad (independent reasoning) have argued from this verse, and from what is established in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) on the authority of Umm Salamah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard the clamour of litigants at the door of his chamber, so he came out to them and said: "Indeed I am only a human being, and I judge only according to what I hear. Perhaps one of you is more eloquent in his argument than another, so I rule in his favour. Whomever I rule in favour of with the right of a Muslim, it is merely a piece of the Fire, so let him take it or leave it."

Imam Ahmad also narrated it from her with the wording: "Two men from the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disputing about inheritances between them which had become obscure, and there was no proof between them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'You bring your disputes to me, and I am only a human being. Perhaps some of you is more eloquent in his argument (or he said: for his argument) than another, so I judge between you according to what I hear. Whoever I give him something of his brother's right, let him not take it, for I am only cutting for him a piece of the Fire, which he will bring on his neck as a collar on the Day of Resurrection.' The two men wept, and each of them said: 'My right is for my brother.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'As for when you have said that, go and divide it, then seek out the right between you, then draw lots, then let each of you absolve his companion.'"

Abu Dawud narrated it and added: "Indeed I judge between you by my opinion, regarding matters on which nothing has been revealed to me." End quote.

(p-1538) Al-Suyuti said: In the verse there is a refutation of those who permit the judge to be non-knowledgeable, because Allah the Exalted delegated judgment to ijtihad, and one who has no knowledge, how can he perform ijtihad?! End quote.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾, meaning: do not argue on their behalf or defend them, and they are Tu'mah and whoever supports him from his people in what has preceded. ﴿Disputant﴾, meaning: one who disputes. In it is that it is not permissible for anyone to dispute on behalf of anyone unless he knows that he is in the right.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 106], meaning: for what you said to Qatadah, as has preceded explained.

Al-Razi said: Those who hold that sins may proceed from the prophets have clung to this verse, and they said: If no sin had occurred from the Messenger ﷺ, he would not have been commanded to seek forgiveness. Then he answered that with several points.

Qadi Iyad said in "al-Shifa": The actions of the prophets, peace be upon them, in matters they were neither forbidden from nor commanded to do, and then were reproached for because of them, or did them by way of interpretation, are only sins in relation to the exaltedness of their station and the perfection of their obedience, not like the sins and disobediences of others, and he extended discussion on this point and pleased with it.

Then he said: Also, in repentance and seeking forgiveness there is another subtle meaning which some scholars indicated, which is seeking the love of Allah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are oft-repenting and loves those who purify themselves﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 222] [Al-Baqarah: part of verse 222]. End quote.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾ [An-Nisa: 107], meaning: they betray them through disobedience. The disobedience of the disobedient is made a betrayal by them of themselves, just as it is made an injustice to themselves, because its harm returns to them.

Al-Razi said: Know that in the verse there is a severe warning, because when the Prophet ﷺ's inclination slightly tilted toward the side of Tu'mah, while it was in Allah's knowledge that Tu'mah was a wicked man, Allah the Exalted reproached His Messenger for that degree of assisting the wrongdoer. So how is the state of one who knows of the oppressor that he is an oppressor, then assists him in that oppression, indeed drives him to it and encourages him to it with the utmost encouragement?! End quote.

It was said "for the treacherous" (p-1539) (and "yakhtanun") although the treacherous is one person, because what is meant by it is him and whoever supported him from his people, and they knew that he was a thief; or it was mentioned in the plural form so that it would include him and everyone who betrays his betrayal. Just as it was mentioned in the form of intensification in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is habitually treacherous and sinful﴾ [An-Nisa: 107], because He, the Exalted, knew of him that he was excessive in betrayal and in committing sins, and what supports this is that he fled to Makkah and apostatized, as we have mentioned earlier.

It is said: If you stumble upon an evil deed from a man, know that it has siblings. It is related from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he ordered the cutting off of the hand of a thief, and his mother came weeping and said: "This is the first theft he has committed, so pardon him." He said: "You have lied; indeed Allah does not take His servant to account for the first time."

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They hide from people﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], meaning: they conceal themselves out of shame before them and fear of their harm. ﴿And they cannot hide from Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], so they are not shy before Him. ﴿And He is with them﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], meaning: He is aware of them and watches over them; nothing of their secret is hidden from Him.

Al-Zamakhshari said: This verse is sufficient as a rebuke of people for what they are in of little shame and fear of their Lord, while they know, if they are believers, that they are in His presence, with no concealment, no heedlessness, and no absence; there remains only clear exposure and disgrace.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When they plot by night what He does not approve of in speech﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], meaning: they devise and fabricate false oaths, the slandering of the innocent, and false testimony.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Here you are—you argued on their behalf in this worldly life﴾ [An-Nisa: 109] and the rest of the verse. Mujadalah is the most intense contention. The meaning: suppose you disputed on behalf of the thief and his people in this world, who will dispute on their behalf in the Hereafter when Allah seizes them with His punishment?!

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or who will be a guardian over them?﴾ [An-Nisa: 109], meaning: a protector and defender from the might and vengeance of Allah the Exalted.

The restriction of the prohibition on disputing to "those who betray themselves" indicates the permissibility of disputing. End quote.

You know that we were attacked during this night; our storeroom was breached, and our food and weapons were taken away.'

(p-1533) He said: I searched the house and asked, and it was said to us: 'We saw the Banu Ubayriq kindle a fire this night, and we do not think, as far as we can see, that it was except on some of your food.'

He said: The Banu Ubayriq had said, while we were asking in the house: 'By Allah, we do not think your companion is anyone but Labid ibn Sahl, a man from among us who is righteous and Muslim.' When Labid heard of that, he drew his sword, then came to the Banu Ubayriq and said: 'By Allah, this sword will certainly reach you, or you will make the theft clear!' They said: 'Keep away from us, O man! By Allah, you are not its perpetrator.' We asked in the house until we did not doubt that they were its perpetrators. My uncle said: 'O nephew! If only you would go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mention this to him.'

Qatadah said: So I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and I said: 'O Messenger of Allah! A household among us, people of rudeness, attacked my uncle Rifa'ah, breached his storeroom, and took his weapons and his food. Let them return our weapons to us, but as for the food, we have no need of it.'

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I will look into the matter.' When the Banu Ubayriq heard of that, they came to a man from among them called Usayr ibn 'Urwah, spoke to him about it, and a group of people from the household gathered around him. They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah! Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man and his uncle attacked a household from among us, people of Islam and righteousness, accusing them of theft without evidence or certainty.' Qatadah said: 'So I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and spoke to him, and he said: "You attacked a household—among whom are mentioned Islam and righteousness—accusing them of theft without evidence or certainty?"' He said: 'So I returned, and I wished I had lost some of my property (p-1534) and had not spoken to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it. I came to my uncle Rifa'ah, and he said: "O nephew! What have you done?" I told him what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said to me, and he said: "Allah is the One sought for help."'

Not long after, the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, meaning: the Banu Ubayriq.

﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 106], i.e., for what you said to Qatadah. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa: 106]. ﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾ [An-Nisa: 107], i.e., the Banu Ubayriq. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is treacherous and sinful﴾ [An-Nisa: 107]. ﴿They conceal themselves from the people﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], up to His saying: ﴿then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa: 110], i.e., if they seek forgiveness of Allah, He will forgive them. ﴿And whoever earns sin, he earns it only against himself, and ever is Allah Knowing and Wise﴾ [An-Nisa: 111]. ﴿And whoever earns a sin or transgression and then attributes it to an innocent person has borne a slander and a manifest sin﴾ [An-Nisa: 112]. This was their saying to Labid: ﴿Were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, a party of them would have intended to mislead you﴾ [An-Nisa: 113], meaning Usayr and his companions. ﴿But they do not mislead except themselves, and they cannot harm you at all. And Allah has sent down to you the Book and wisdom﴾ [An-Nisa: 113], up to His saying: ﴿then We will give him a great reward﴾ [An-Nisa: 114].

When the Qur'an was revealed, the weapons were brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he returned them to Rifa'ah.

Qatadah said: "When I brought the weapons to my uncle—and he was an old man who had become decrepit in the Jahiliyyah—and I used to think his Islam was tainted, when I brought him the weapons he said: 'O nephew! It is in the way of Allah.' I knew then that his Islam was sound."

(p-1535) When the Qur'an was revealed, Bushayr joined the polytheists, and he stayed with Sulafah, the daughter of Sa'd ibn Shuhayd. Allah revealed concerning him: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers﴾ [An-Nisa: 115], up to His saying: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly strayed far astray﴾ [An-Nisa: 116].

When he stayed with Sulafah, Hassan ibn Thabit satirized him with verses of poetry. So she took his saddle, placed it on her head, went out with it, and threw it in al-Abtah, then said: "You brought me the poetry of Hassan! You never brought me anything good."

Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a strange hadith; we know of no one who transmitted it with a full chain except Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Harrani."

Yunus ibn Bukayr and others narrated this hadith from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah as a mursal report, without mentioning "from his father, from his grandfather."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Hashim ibn al-Qasim al-Harrani, from Muhammad ibn Salamah, part of it. (p-1536) Ibn al-Mundhir narrated it in his "Tafsir" with his chain from Muhammad ibn Salamah, mentioning it in full.

Abu al-Shaykh al-Isfahani narrated it in his "Tafsir" with his chain from Muhammad ibn Salamah, then said at its end: Muhammad ibn Salamah said: "Yahya ibn Ma'in, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Ishaq ibn Isra'il heard this hadith from me."

Al-Hakim narrated it in his "Mustadrak" with his chain, from Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, in a similar meaning, more complete than it, and in it is the poetry. Then he said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of Muslim, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." Thus Ibn Kathir quoted it.

Al-Suyuti said in "al-Lubab": Ibn Sa'd recorded in "al-Tabaqat," with his chain, from Mahmud ibn Labid, who said: "Bushayr ibn al-Harith attacked the upper room of Rifa'ah ibn Zayd, the uncle of Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man, breached it from its back, and took his food and two coats of mail with their equipment. Qatadah came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him of that. He summoned Bushayr and questioned him, and he denied it, and he attributed it to Labid ibn Sahl, a man from the household who had lineage and nobility. So the Qur'an was revealed refuting Bushayr and clearing Labid: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾, the verses. When the Qur'an was revealed concerning Bushayr and he was exposed, he fled to Mecca as an apostate, and he stayed with Sulafah, daughter of Sa'd. He began to slander the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Muslims, and it was revealed concerning him: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger﴾ [An-Nisa: 115], [An-Nisa: from verse 115], the verse. Hassan ibn Thabit satirized him until he returned. That was in the month of Rabi' in the fourth year after the Hijrah." End of quotation.

As for the clarification of the words of the verses and their fruits, we say: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾ means: by what He made you know, informed you of, and revealed to you. That knowledge is called "seeing" because certain knowledge free of doubt operates like sight in strength and clarity.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It is narrated from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him): "None of you should say: 'I judged by what Allah has shown me,' for Allah did not grant that except to His Prophet (ﷺ). Rather, let him exert his opinion (*ijtihad*), for the opinion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was correct, because Allah used to show it to him. As for us, it is conjecture and presumption."

I say: al-Bayhaqi in "al-Madkhal" and Ibn 'Abd al-Barr narrated this report with a similar wording.

Ibn al-Furs said: In this verse is the establishment of opinion (*ra'y*) and analogy (*qiyas*). Al-Suyuti refuted him with what Ibn Abi Hatim recorded (p-1537) from Ibn Abbas that he said: "Beware of opinion, for Allah, Exalted is He, said to His Prophet: ﴿that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾ and did not say: 'by what you saw.'"

Then al-Suyuti said: Others said: His saying ﴿by what Allah has shown you﴾ may include both revelation and independent reasoning (*ijtihad*) together. End of quotation.

Ibn Kathir said: Those among the scholars of usul (legal theory) who hold that the Prophet ﷺ had the right to judge by ijtihad (independent reasoning) have argued from this verse, and from what is established in the Two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) on the authority of Umm Salamah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard the clamour of litigants at the door of his chamber, so he came out to them and said: "Indeed I am only a human being, and I judge only according to what I hear. Perhaps one of you is more eloquent in his argument than another, so I rule in his favour. Whomever I rule in favour of with the right of a Muslim, it is merely a piece of the Fire, so let him take it or leave it."

Imam Ahmad also narrated it from her with the wording: "Two men from the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disputing about inheritances between them which had become obscure, and there was no proof between them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'You bring your disputes to me, and I am only a human being. Perhaps some of you is more eloquent in his argument (or he said: for his argument) than another, so I judge between you according to what I hear. Whoever I give him something of his brother's right, let him not take it, for I am only cutting for him a piece of the Fire, which he will bring on his neck as a collar on the Day of Resurrection.' The two men wept, and each of them said: 'My right is for my brother.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'As for when you have said that, go and divide it, then seek out the right between you, then draw lots, then let each of you absolve his companion.'"

Abu Dawud narrated it and added: "Indeed I judge between you by my opinion, regarding matters on which nothing has been revealed to me." End quote.

(p-1538) Al-Suyuti said: In the verse there is a refutation of those who permit the judge to be non-knowledgeable, because Allah the Exalted delegated judgment to ijtihad, and one who has no knowledge, how can he perform ijtihad?! End quote.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾, meaning: do not argue on their behalf or defend them, and they are Tu'mah and whoever supports him from his people in what has preceded. ﴿Disputant﴾, meaning: one who disputes. In it is that it is not permissible for anyone to dispute on behalf of anyone unless he knows that he is in the right.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 106], meaning: for what you said to Qatadah, as has preceded explained.

Al-Razi said: Those who hold that sins may proceed from the prophets have clung to this verse, and they said: If no sin had occurred from the Messenger ﷺ, he would not have been commanded to seek forgiveness. Then he answered that with several points.

Qadi Iyad said in "al-Shifa": The actions of the prophets, peace be upon them, in matters they were neither forbidden from nor commanded to do, and then were reproached for because of them, or did them by way of interpretation, are only sins in relation to the exaltedness of their station and the perfection of their obedience, not like the sins and disobediences of others, and he extended discussion on this point and pleased with it.

Then he said: Also, in repentance and seeking forgiveness there is another subtle meaning which some scholars indicated, which is seeking the love of Allah. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are oft-repenting and loves those who purify themselves﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 222] [Al-Baqarah: part of verse 222]. End quote.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾ [An-Nisa: 107], meaning: they betray them through disobedience. The disobedience of the disobedient is made a betrayal by them of themselves, just as it is made an injustice to themselves, because its harm returns to them.

Al-Razi said: Know that in the verse there is a severe warning, because when the Prophet ﷺ's inclination slightly tilted toward the side of Tu'mah, while it was in Allah's knowledge that Tu'mah was a wicked man, Allah the Exalted reproached His Messenger for that degree of assisting the wrongdoer. So how is the state of one who knows of the oppressor that he is an oppressor, then assists him in that oppression, indeed drives him to it and encourages him to it with the utmost encouragement?! End quote.

It was said "for the treacherous" (p-1539) (and "yakhtanun") although the treacherous is one person, because what is meant by it is him and whoever supported him from his people, and they knew that he was a thief; or it was mentioned in the plural form so that it would include him and everyone who betrays his betrayal. Just as it was mentioned in the form of intensification in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is habitually treacherous and sinful﴾ [An-Nisa: 107], because He, the Exalted, knew of him that he was excessive in betrayal and in committing sins, and what supports this is that he fled to Makkah and apostatized, as we have mentioned earlier.

It is said: If you stumble upon an evil deed from a man, know that it has siblings. It is related from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he ordered the cutting off of the hand of a thief, and his mother came weeping and said: "This is the first theft he has committed, so pardon him." He said: "You have lied; indeed Allah does not take His servant to account for the first time."

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They hide from people﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], meaning: they conceal themselves out of shame before them and fear of their harm. ﴿And they cannot hide from Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], so they are not shy before Him. ﴿And He is with them﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], meaning: He is aware of them and watches over them; nothing of their secret is hidden from Him.

Al-Zamakhshari said: This verse is sufficient as a rebuke of people for what they are in of little shame and fear of their Lord, while they know, if they are believers, that they are in His presence, with no concealment, no heedlessness, and no absence; there remains only clear exposure and disgrace.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When they plot by night what He does not approve of in speech﴾ [An-Nisa: 108], meaning: they devise and fabricate false oaths, the slandering of the innocent, and false testimony.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Here you are—you argued on their behalf in this worldly life﴾ [An-Nisa: 109] and the rest of the verse. Mujadalah is the most intense contention. The meaning: suppose you disputed on behalf of the thief and his people in this world, who will dispute on their behalf in the Hereafter when Allah seizes them with His punishment?!

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or who will be a guardian over them?﴾ [An-Nisa: 109], meaning: a protector and defender from the might and vengeance of Allah the Exalted.

Some of the commentators of the Zaydiyyah said: The fruit of these verses is the obligation to judge without favouritism or inclination, and the prohibition of partisanship and of disputing on behalf of every treacherous and disobedient person. The restriction of the prohibition on disputing to "those who betray themselves" indicates the permissibility of disputing. End quote.

Know that when He, the Exalted, mentioned the threat in this matter, He followed it with a call to repentance, with His saying, Glorified is He:

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

﴿And whoever does wrong or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness of Allah, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [110]

﴿And whoever does wrong﴾, i.e., an ugly deed that is transgressive, whose harm reaches others, as in the story (of Tu'mah), ﴿or wrongs himself﴾, restricting it to disobedience, ﴿then seeks forgiveness of Allah﴾ through sincere repentance (tawbah), ﴿will find Allah Forgiving﴾ of his sins, whatever they may be, ﴿Merciful﴾, i.e., bestowing favor upon him.

Abu al-Su'ud said: In this there is further encouragement for Tu'mah and his people to repent and seek forgiveness, because the penitent witnessing the effects of forgiveness and mercy is an additional blessing.

The discussion of the words of His, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ [111]

﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself﴾, i.e., let him guard against exposing it to punishment. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

﴿And whoever earns a sin or an offense and then throws it upon an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin.﴾ [112]

﴿And whoever earns a sin or an offense﴾ Khati'ah (خطيئة) is a sin, or that which is done deliberately from it, and ithm (إثم) is also a sin, or doing what is not lawful for one. Thus it is in the "Qamus" (al-Qamus al-Muhit, the dictionary).

Al-Raghib (al-Raghib al-Isfahani) said: ithm is more general than 'udwan (transgression). Others said: it is an act that delays one from reward.

﴿Then throws it upon﴾ means casts it onto ﴿an innocent person﴾ meaning: free of what he has been accused of, just as the Banu Ubayriq accused that righteous man, who is Labid ibn Sahl, as has been mentioned earlier, with their vile deed, and he was innocent. ﴿Then has certainly borne a slander﴾ which is buhtan (بهتان), meaning lying about another by saying something for which he is left dumbfounded ﴿and a manifest sin﴾ meaning clear and grave. For he is a sinner by earning the sin, and a slanderer by casting blame on the innocent; so he combines both matters.

(p-1541) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Had it not been for Allah's grace upon you and His mercy, a group of them would have resolved to mislead you. But they mislead none except themselves, and they cannot harm you at all.
