Ibn Kathir said: This is a strange (gharīb) hadith from this route, and parts of it have supporting evidence in the authentic collections and others. End.

I say: al-Tirmidhi also narrated it in his Jami' in the chapter on his virtues (ﷺ), then said: "This is a strange hadith."

It is evident that his saying (ﷺ): "Beware, I am the beloved of God" does not indicate that the rank of love is higher, because it was not stated to compare the two. Rather, this sentence together with what follows was brought to make known his great station, his immense virtue, the distinctive qualities which had not been combined before in any creature, and the right of God, which is the highest of rights, that he is owed: ﴿So that those who were given the Scripture may be certain, and those who believed may increase in faith﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 31].

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ishaq ibn Yasar, who said: "When God took Ibrahim as a close friend (khalil), He cast into his heart such fear that the pounding of his heart could be heard from afar, just as the fluttering of a bird in the air is heard." Likewise, it has come in the description of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that a sound was heard from his chest like the bubbling of a cauldron (mirjal) when its boiling intensifies, out of weeping.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever, of all things, Encompassing.﴾ [126]

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ is an independent sentence, brought to affirm the obligation of obedience to Allah, Exalted is He, upon the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, by explaining that all the existents within them belong to Him, Exalted is He, both in creation and in ownership; nothing of them goes outside His dominion, so that He will recompense each one according to the requirement of his deeds, good or evil.

It has been said: it is to explain that His taking Ibrahim (peace be upon him) as a close friend (khalil), Exalted and Majestic is He, was not because He, glorified be He, had need of that in any of His affairs, as is the custom of human beings, for the basis of their friendship is the dependence of some of them upon others for their interests; rather, it was merely for his honour and distinction (peace be upon him).

It has been said: it is to explain that the friendship (khullah) does not remove him from the rank of servanthood (ubudiyyah).

(p-1585) It has been said: it is to explain that His choosing him (peace be upon him) for friendship was purely by His will, Exalted is He; that is, to Him belongs all that is in them together, and He chooses from them what He wills for whomever He wills. Abu al-Su'ud related this.

﴿And Allah is ever, of all things, Encompassing﴾ means: knowing with comprehensive knowledge, such that no hidden matter of His servants is concealed from Him: ﴿Not an atom's weight escapes Him in the heavens or on the earth, nor is there anything smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear record﴾ [Saba': 3] [Yunus: 61].

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 4, verse 127:

The discussion of His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, "Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them and whom you desire to marry, and [concerning] the oppressed among the children, and that you maintain justice for orphans. And whatever good you do – indeed, Allah is ever Knowing of it."﴾ [127]

﴿They ask you for a ruling concerning women﴾ i.e., they ask you for a fatwa (ifta') concerning women, and ifta' is the clarification of what is unclear (mubham).

﴿Say, "Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and what is recited to you in the Book"﴾ They mentioned several possibilities for (ma). The preferred among them is that it is in the nominative position by coordination with the subject, which is the Name of Majesty (lafz al-jalala), meaning: "and what is recited in the Book also gives you a ruling concerning them." Or it is coordinated with its pronoun in "yuftikum" (gives you a ruling), and this is permissible because of the intervening object and the prepositional phrase. That which is recited in the Book is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly with the orphans, then marry from among women what seems good to you﴾ [An-Nisa: 3].

Al-Razi said: The gist of the matter is that they had asked about many matters concerning women. Of these, whatever did not have a clearly stated ruling, He mentioned that Allah gives them a ruling concerning it. And whatever had its ruling clearly stated in the preceding verses, He mentioned that those recited verses give them a ruling concerning it, and He made the Book's indication of this ruling a ruling from the Book. Do you not see that it is commonly said: "The Book of Allah has clarified this ruling for us"? Just as this is permissible, it is also permissible to say: "The Book of Allah has given a ruling on such-and-such."

Abu al-Su'ud said: The choice of the present tense form (al-mudari') indicates the continuity and permanence of the recitation. And "in the Book" is either related to "yutla" (is recited), or to an omitted element that occurs as a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun within it, meaning: recited while being in it.

﴿concerning the orphan women﴾ is related to "yutla," i.e., what is recited to you concerning their affair. This idafa (construct) is in the sense of "min" (of), since it is the idafa of a thing to its genus. It is said that it is the idafa of an attribute to the thing described, i.e., the women who are orphans.

﴿to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them﴾ i.e., what is due to them of inheritance and other things. ﴿and whom you desire to marry﴾ Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated, from A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said concerning this verse: It is the man who has an orphan girl in his care; he is her guardian and her heir. She shares with him in his property, even in a date palm cluster, so he desires to marry her, and dislikes to give her in marriage to a man who would share his property with what she shares with him, so he restricts her (ya'dulaha). So this verse was revealed.

Also from her, may Allah be pleased with her, she said: The saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿and whom you desire to marry﴾ is the desire of one of you to turn away from his orphan who is in his guardianship when she is little in property and beauty. So they were forbidden to marry those whose wealth and beauty they desired among the orphan women, except with justice, because of their aversion to them.

This report from A'isha indicates that the verse was revealed concerning the poor (mu'dimah) orphan, and that the implied preposition with "an" here is "'an" (from). Sa'id ibn Jubayr interpreted it according to both meanings, i.e., estimating both "'an" and "fi" (in), and he said: it was revealed concerning both the poor and the wealthy.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: What is reported from A'isha is clearer that the first verse, i.e., the one at the beginning of the surah, was revealed concerning the wealthy, and this verse was revealed concerning the poor.

Ibn Kathir said: The point is that when a man has an orphan girl in his care, it is lawful for him to marry her. Sometimes he desires to marry her, so Allah commanded him to give her a dowry like that of her equals among women; if he does not do so, let him turn to other women, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has granted latitude – and this meaning is in the first verse at the beginning of the surah. Other times he has no desire for her because of her plainness in his eyes – or in reality – so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade him to prevent her from marrying (ya'dulaha 'an al-azwaj), fearing that they would share in his property which is between him and her, as Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning the verse, which is His saying: ﴿concerning the orphan women﴾, the verse: In the Jahiliyya, a man would have an orphan girl in his care, and he would throw his garment over her; when he did this, no one could ever marry her. If she was beautiful and he loved her, he would marry her and consume her wealth; if she was plain, he would prevent men from her forever until she died, and when she died he would inherit her. So Allah forbade that and prohibited it.

Note: What we have mentioned from Ibn Jubayr about reading the verse as having both meanings, i.e., that the implied preposition with "an" is both "'an" and "fi," and that each of them is intended from it alternately because it is suitable for both according to the two considerations mentioned earlier.

Al-Khafaji said: Such a thing is not considered ambiguity (labs) but generality (ijmal), as some verifiers have mentioned. End.

I say: This is based on the view that ambiguity (labs) is when the expression indicates something other than what is intended, and generality (ijmal) is when the indication is not clear; in other words, presenting speech in a way that admits multiple matters. Some have versified the difference between them, saying:

The difference between ambiguity and generality is among the things with which attention is concerned in statements.
So if the expression conveys other than the intended meaning, judge its usage to be rejected.
For that is ambiguity. As for the general (mujmal), perhaps one who understands may grasp it.
And that is that you do not understand the opposing view, nor any other, but rather remain undecided.
Its ruling is acceptance in its occurrences, so memorize it as a verse, the greatest of benefits.

﴿and [concerning] the oppressed among the children﴾ is a coordination with "orphan women," and what is recited concerning them is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children﴾ [An-Nisa: 11] etc., for in the Jahiliyya they did not give them inheritance, just as they did not give inheritance to the men who were in charge (al-qawwamun).

Ibn Abbas said concerning the verse: In the Jahiliyya they did not give inheritance to young children or to daughters, and that is His saying: ﴿what is prescribed for them﴾. So Allah forbade that and explained to every holder of a share his share, saying: ﴿For the male is an equal of the share of two females﴾ [An-Nisa: 11], whether young or old. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said likewise.

﴿and that you maintain justice for orphans﴾ in the genitive (bi-l-jarr), coordinated with what precedes it, and what is recited concerning them is His saying: ﴿And do not substitute the bad [of your own] for the good [of theirs], and do not consume their property into your own﴾ [An-Nisa: 2], and the like of that, which is nearly countless.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The meaning is: just as if she is possessed of beauty and wealth, you marry her and keep her for yourself, so likewise if she is not possessed of wealth and beauty, marry her and keep her for yourself. The address is to the rulers or to the guardians and executors.

* *

Note:

Several rulings have been derived from the verse:

The first: the permissibility of marrying a young girl, because the orphan (yatim) is the child who has not reached puberty. In a hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) he said: "There is no orphanhood after puberty (ihtilam)," narrated by Abu Dawud.

From al-Asamm: He meant the one who has reached puberty before marriage, and they were called orphans because of the recency of their orphanhood. The first is more apparent, because it is the literal meaning. They said: The term orphan is sometimes applied to a woman who has reached maturity, by the evidence of his saying (ﷺ): "The orphan girl is consulted concerning herself; if she remains silent, that is her consent, and if she refuses, there is no permission over her," narrated by the authors of the Sunan, and consultation only occurs with a mature woman. And the poet's saying has come:

Indeed the graves marry the widowed women, the solitary women, the orphans.

So he called the mature women orphans, because of their being alone without husbands, and every thing that is unique with no equal is called an orphan, as they say "a unique pearl" (durra yatima). On this matter there are views among the scholars:

The first: the permissibility of marrying a young girl by all guardians; this is the position of the Hadawiyya, Malik, Abu Hanifa and his two companions.

The second: according to al-Nasir and al-Shafi'i: this is not permitted except for the father and the paternal grandfather.

The third: this is not permitted except for the father alone; this is the view of al-Awza'i, and is narrated from al-Qasim.

The evidence of the first two is what is implied by His saying: ﴿and whom you desire to marry﴾, and it was revealed concerning an orphan girl whom her guardian marries without giving her a fair dowry, so they were forbidden from that and commanded to be just in the dowry by His saying in Surat an-Nisa: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly with the orphans, then marry from among women what seems good to you﴾ [An-Nisa: 3]. The true sense of orphanhood is with youth, and other usage is metaphorical; and the lowest of guardians who may marry her is the paternal cousin; if it is valid for him, it is valid [for all others].

The argument of the second view is the Prophet's saying (ﷺ): "The orphan girl is consulted," the hadith mentioned earlier, and permission only occurs after puberty.

Imam Ahmad and al-Daraqutni narrated that Qudama ibn Maz'un married the daughter of his brother – and he was her guardian – to a man she refused, so this was brought to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "She is an orphan, and she is not to be married except with her permission." Thus some of the Zaydi exegetes mentioned it.

The takhrij (sourcing) of the hadiths is my addition, and what he reported, that permission only occurs after puberty, requires evidence, since the report does not indicate it by its explicit wording or implicit meaning.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in "al-Fath": In the hadith: "The widow is not to be married until she is consulted, and the virgin is not to be married until her permission is sought," the apparent meaning of the hadith is the requirement of the consent of the woman being married, whether virgin or previously married, young or old. End.

At-Tirmidhi said in his "Jami'": Some of them said: it is not permitted to marry an orphan girl until she reaches puberty.

Ahmad and Ishaq said: If an orphan girl reaches seven years and is married and consents, the marriage is valid, and she has no option when she matures. They relied on the hadith of A'isha: "that the Prophet (ﷺ) consummated the marriage with her when she was nine years old." A'isha also said: When a girl reaches nine years, she is a woman. End.

The Second Ruling: It is permissible for one person to take charge of both sides of the contract in marriage; the basis is His saying: ﴿and whom you desire to marry﴾.

Ibn Sa'd narrated through the path of Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Sa'id ibn Khalid, that Umm Hakim bint Qarizh said to Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: Several men have proposed to me, so marry me to whichever of them you see fit. He said: Will you make that up to me? She said: Yes. He said: I have married you. Ibn Abi Dhi'b said: So his marriage was valid.

Abd al-Razzaq, Waki', and al-Bayhaqi narrated that al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba wished to marry a woman while he was her guardian, so he commanded someone more distant than himself, and he married her.

Abd al-Razzaq also narrated from Ibn Jurayj who said: I said to Ata': A woman was proposed to by her paternal cousin, who has no other male guardian but him. He said: Let her call witnesses that so-and-so has proposed to her, and I call you as witnesses that I have married him; and let her commission a man from her clan.

Al-Bukhari included these three reports in his Sahih as a suspended narration (ta'liq) under the chapter "When the guardian is himself the one proposing." That is, whether he marries himself or needs another guardian.

Ibn al-Munir said: He mentioned in the chapter heading what indicates both permissibility and prohibition, so as to leave the matter to the judgment of the mujtahid.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: But what appears from his method is that he holds it permissible, for the reports in which the guardian is commanded to have someone else marry her do not explicitly forbid his marrying her himself.

He then said: The salaf have differed on this. Al-Awza'i, Rabi'a, al-Thawri, Malik, Abu Hanifa and most of his companions said: the guardian may marry himself, and Abu Thawr agreed with them.

From Malik: If a previously married woman says to her guardian: "Marry me to whomever you see," and he marries her to himself or to whom he chooses, that binds her, even if she does not know the identity of the husband.

Al-Shafi'i said: the sultan or another guardian like him, or one more distant than him, shall marry them; Zufar and Dawud agreed with him, and their argument is that guardianship is a condition of the contract, so the one marrying cannot be the one giving in marriage, just as one cannot sell to oneself. End.

The Third Ruling: It is permissible for guardians to dispose of property, because the upholding of justice is not complete except by that.

﴿And whatever good you do﴾ especially concerning the rights of the weak, by preserving their property, managing their affairs, and being just to them, ﴿indeed, Allah is ever Knowing of it﴾, so He will reward you for it.

(p-1593) On the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿If a wife fears ill-treatment (nushuz) or aversion (i'rad) from her husband, there is no blame upon them both if they make a settlement between themselves, and settlement is best. And souls are present with stinginess. But if you do good and fear Allah, then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.﴾ [128]

﴿If a wife fears﴾ i.e., from her husband, ﴿ill-treatment (nushuz)﴾ i.e., his shunning of her and his elevating himself above her companionship, by abandoning her bed and falling short in her maintenance; ﴿or aversion (i'rad)﴾ i.e., divorce, or that he reduces his conversation and sitting with her, out of dislike for her or because his eye has aspired to one more beautiful than her.

﴿there is no blame (ithm)﴾ i.e., no sin ﴿upon them both (alayhima)﴾ at that time ﴿if they make a settlement between themselves (an yuslihu baynahuma sulha)﴾ by remitting some of the dower or the maintenance, or by her giving up some of her rights or her turn; seeking the continuation of the companionship, if she agrees to that; otherwise, it is incumbent upon the husband to give her her right or to separate from her.

In "al-Iklil" it is said: The verse is a foundation for a wife's gift of her right to the turn and other things, and whoever permits her to sell that has taken it as evidence.

﴿and settlement is best﴾ i.e., better than separation, ill-treatment and aversion.

Ibn Kathir said: Rather, divorce is hateful to Him, glorified and exalted is He. For this reason there came in the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah, from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The most hated of lawful things to Allah is divorce."

One of the commentators of the Zaydiyyah said: In this verse there is an exhortation to patience upon the very companionship itself, by His saying: ﴿and settlement is best﴾ i.e., better than separation and bad companionship, or better than dispute, or better than all good things, just as dispute is the worst of evils. And among the nobility of his ﷺ character was that he honored the companions of Khadijah after her death. And from him ﷺ: "Indeed, among the greatest of righteousness is that a man maintains the people of his father's affection." In this there is patience, and in patience there are countless (p-1595) virtues and excellences, and settlement contains kinds of encouragement.

It is related from him ﷺ: "Whoever reconciles between two people has earned the reward of a martyr," and from Anas: "Whoever reconciles between two people, Allah gives him for every word the reward of freeing a slave." End.

In "al-Iklil": His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿and settlement is best﴾ is general to every settlement, a foundation for it.

And in the hadith: "Settlement is permissible among Muslims, except a settlement that makes lawful what is forbidden or forbids what is lawful." Whoever permits settlement regarding denial and the unknown has used the generality of the verse as evidence.

﴿And souls are present with stinginess (shuhh)﴾ is an explanation of what man has been created upon, i.e., it has been made present to him, imprinted upon him, never separating from him. So a woman scarcely allows ill-treatment or aversion to be absent from her rights from the man, nor does the man, in keeping her while fulfilling her rights as they should be, when he dislikes her or loves another. The first sentence is an encouragement to reconciliation, and the second is to prepare an excuse for contention and to urge settlement, for the stinginess of a man's soul and his not inclining away from his natural state without persuasion is what moves the woman to give up some of her rights to him in order to win him over; likewise the stinginess of her soul with her rights is what moves the man to be content with something small from her side and not to burden her with giving much, so that settlement is achieved thereby.

﴿But if you do good (ihsan)﴾ in companionship ﴿and fear Allah (tattaqu)﴾ ill-treatment, aversion and diminishing of rights ﴿then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do﴾ of bearing hardships in that ﴿Acquainted﴾, so He will reward you and recompense you.

Abu al-Suud said: In the address to the husbands by way of iltifat (shift of address), and in the expression of guarding their rights by ihsan, and the word "taqwa" which indicates that ill-treatment and aversion are among what is to be guarded against, and the ordering of the generous promise upon it, there is of the gentleness of winning over and encouragement toward good treatment what is not hidden.

What we have presented in the interpretation of the verse is the essence of what has been transmitted from the predecessors, companions and Successors, regarding its meaning.

Ibn Kathir said: I know of no disagreement on that.

In al-Bukhari, from Aisha regarding this verse, (p-1596) she said: "A man has a older wife with whom he does not have much, and he wants to divorce her, so she says: I release you from my affair (ja'altuka min sha'ni fi hill)." So this verse was revealed.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Khalid ibn Arara who said: A man came to Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, and asked him about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿If a wife...﴾ the verse. Ali said: A man has a wife, and his eye turns away from her because of her ugliness or her age, or her bad character, or her [lack of] ..., so he dislikes parting from him; if she sets aside some of her dower for him, it is lawful for him, and if she gives him some of her days, there is no blame.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi and Ibn Jarir also narrated it similarly.

Ibn Jarir also narrated from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was asked about this verse and said: This is a woman who is with a man who has passed her age, so he marries a young woman seeking her child; whatever they agree upon of something is permissible.

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated from Urwah who said: It was revealed concerning Sawda and her likes: ﴿If a wife...﴾ the verse. That was because Sawda was a woman who had grown old, and she feared that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would part from her, and she was stingy about her place with him, and she knew of the love of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for Aisha and her standing with him, so she gave her day from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Aisha, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted that.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi and al-Tirmidhi narrated something similar from Ibn Abbas.

Al-Hakim narrated from Urwah, "from Aisha that she said to him: O nephew! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not favor any of us over another in the division regarding his stay with us, and there was hardly a day but he would go round to us all, approaching each wife without intercourse, until he reached the one whose day it was, and he would spend the night with her. Sawda bint Zam'ah, when she grew old and feared that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would part from her, said: O Messenger of Allah! My day is for Aisha; so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted that from her. She said: Concerning that, Allah revealed, and concerning its likes, I think she said: ﴿If a wife fears ill-treatment...﴾ the verse."

Abu Dawud related it similarly, and in the two Sahihs from Aisha she said: "When Sawda bint Zam'ah grew old, she gave her day to Aisha, and the Prophet ﷺ would divide for her according to Sawda's day."

It is not hidden that his ﷺ acceptance of that from Sawda was only so that his ummah would follow him in the legitimacy and permissibility of that, so it is most excellent in his case, peace and blessings be upon him.

As for the saying of some commentators regarding this story: that the Prophet ﷺ had resolved to divorce Sawda, this is false and a misunderstanding of the story, since his ﷺ resolve upon that has not been transmitted, neither in the Sahihs, nor in the Sunan, nor in the Masanid. The most that is related in the Sunan is that Sawda feared separation because of her old age and imagined it, and it is clear that women in matters of jealousy have varied delusions; so she came forward to the Prophet ﷺ offering her night to Aisha, and he accepted it from her.

As for what Ibn Kathir narrated from some lexicons, that he ﷺ sent to her with her divorce, then she implored him and he took her back, this has an addition beyond its sending and is strange, as he said, and it contains a denial that is not hidden.

A subtle point:

Al-Zamakhshari related here that Imran ibn Hittan the Kharijite was among the ugliest of the children of Adam, and his wife was among the most beautiful of them. She looked at his face one day, then she continued saying "Praise be to Allah." He said: What is the matter with you? She said: I praised Allah that you and I are among the people of Paradise. He said: How? She said: Because you were given someone like me and you were thankful, and I was given someone like you and I was patient, and Allah has promised Paradise to His servants who are thankful and patient. End.

(p-1598) I say: The aforementioned Imran is one whom al-Bukhari narrated from in his Sahih. When he died, his wife was asked about his biography. She said: Shall I be brief or elaborate? It was said: Be brief. She said: I did not prepare food for him by day, nor spread a bed for him by night, meaning that he was one who fasted much and prayed much at night. May Allah have mercy on him.

The discussion of the Lord's words:

﴿And you will never be able to be just between wives, even if you should strive to do so. So do not incline completely [toward one], leaving her as if suspended. And if you amend and fear Allah, then indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [129]

﴿And you will never be able to be just between wives﴾ That is: you cannot make them equal in all respects, such that no inclination at all occurs toward one of them in any matter. For even if the outward division is carried out night by night, there must still be a difference in affection, desire, and intimacy, as Ibn 'Abbas and others have said.

﴿Even if you should strive to do so﴾ That is: to establish justice, and exert yourselves greatly in it, since inclination arises in the heart without choice.

From 'A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to divide [his time] among his wives justly, and then he would say: 'O Allah, this is my division in what I control, so do not blame me for what You control and I do not control,'" meaning the heart. Related by Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan.

﴿So do not incline completely [toward one]﴾ That is: if you incline toward one of them, do not go to excess in that inclination. Al-Mahayimi said: "(p-1599) So do not incline, that is, away from a woman, completely, so that you abandon what is within your capacity of equity."

﴿And leave her﴾ That is, the one away from whom you have inclined ﴿as if suspended﴾ between heaven and earth, neither in one of the two directions: neither a married woman nor a divorced one.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has two wives and inclines toward one of them will come on the Day of Resurrection with one of his sides fallen," (shiqqayhi saqit, according to one report).

Thus I saw it in (Ibn Kathir) as "shiqqayhi," with a dotted shin then a dal (shidqayhi). The narration of the authors of the Sunan as transmitted is: "wa-shiqquhu" (with a dotted letter then a qaf) saqit, and in one narration:ma'il (leaning).

﴿And if you amend﴾ That is: your souls, through equal treatment, division, and justice in what you control, ﴿and fear Allah﴾ against injustice and oppression, ﴿then indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾, so He will forgive you what has passed of your inclination.

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

﴿And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance. And ever is Allah All-Encompassing and Wise.﴾ [130]

﴿And if they separate﴾: i.e., the husband and the wife by divorce, when reconciliation between them has not been achieved, and they have chosen separation (p-1600). ﴿Allah will enrich each﴾: i.e., each of the two, meaning He will make each of them independent of the other. ﴿from His abundance﴾: i.e., His sufficiency, His bounty, and His power. In this there is a deterrent for them both from separating out of spite toward their companion, and a consolation for them both after the divorce.

﴿And ever is Allah Bountiful﴾: i.e., abundant in grace ﴿Wise﴾ in all His actions, decrees, and legislation.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 4, verse 131:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And We have certainly instructed those who were given the Scripture before you and [including] you, to fear Allah. But if you disbelieve - then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And ever is Allah Free of need and Praiseworthy.﴾ [131]

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ is a resumptive sentence (jumlah musta'nafah) that draws attention to the perfection of His vastness and the greatness of His power. That is: how could He not be vast, when to Him belongs what is in them of creatures, provisions and other things? So He may give from them whatever He wills to whomever He wills of His servants. On this reading, it is connected to what precedes it. Or it was placed as a preface to what follows of acting upon His instruction, informing that He is the Owner of what is in the heavens and the earth and the One who judges concerning them. For this reason He said: ﴿And We have certainly instructed those who were given the Scripture before you﴾, that is, from the earlier nations - and "the Scripture" is a generic noun that encompasses the heavenly books - ﴿and [including] you﴾ is conjoined to "those" (alladhina).

﴿That fear Allah﴾, that is: We instructed each of you and them to be mindful of Allah, and mindfulness is worshipping Him alone, with no partner. The meaning is that His instruction is ancient; Allah has continued to enjoin it upon His servants, and you are not singled out for it, for they are made happy in His presence through mindfulness.

﴿But if you disbelieve﴾, that is: in Allah, ﴿then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, that is: He is the Owner of all dominion. Your disbelief does not harm Him, because of His absolute self-sufficiency. The instruction is only for your success, out of mercy toward you, as in the other verse: ﴿If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely, then indeed Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾ [Ibrahim: 8]. And Allah, exalted is He, said: (p-1601) ﴿So they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was independent﴾ [al-Taghabun: 6].

﴿And ever is Allah Free of need﴾ from His servants ﴿and Praiseworthy﴾, that is: praised in His essence, whether they praise Him or do not praise Him.

**The discussion on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:**

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾ [132]

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ He mentions this a third time, either to establish that He, may He be exalted, is self-sufficient and worthy of praise. All created beings indicate His self-sufficiency through their need, and they indicate that He is worthy of praise through the existence and the various attributes and perfections He has bestowed upon them. Or it serves as a preparation for what follows, the conditional "man" (مَنِ, "whoever"), which shows that He, may He be exalted, is able to do all that is possible. That is, everything in the heavens and the earth, of creatures, belongs to Him, both in creation and in ownership. So He is able to annihilate and to bring into being. If you disobey Him, O people, then He is able to destroy you entirely, and to bring into being another people who occupy themselves with His worship and glorification. He mentioned these words in this context three times to establish three matters within its context, as we have explained.

Al-Razi said: When a single proof indicates many things signified, it is good to mention that proof so that it may be used as evidence for one of those things, then mention it again so that it may be used as evidence for the second, then a third time so that it may be used as evidence for the third signified matter. This repetition is better and more appropriate than mentioning the proof only once, because when the proof is repeated, what necessitates knowledge of the signified thing comes to mind, so the knowledge gained of that signified thing becomes stronger and clearer. Thus it becomes evident that this repetition is at the height of excellence and perfection.

Also, when you repeat it three times, and in each instance you derive from it the affirmation of another attribute of the majesty of Allah, the mind is then alerted to the fact that the creation of the heavens and the earth points to noble secrets and sublime aims. At that point a person strives to reflect upon them and to infer from their conditions and attributes the attributes of the Creator, may He be glorified and exalted.

Since the overall purpose of this noble Book is to turn minds and understandings away from occupation with other than Allah and toward immersion in knowledge of Allah, and since this repetition contributes to the attainment of this goal and reinforces it, it is therefore of the highest excellence and perfection. End.

﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾ That is: a Lord who preserves, who has taken upon Himself the task of managing all that He has created.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

﴿If He wills, He can remove you, O people, and bring others [in your place]; and ever is Allah capable of that.﴾ [133]

﴿If He wills, He can remove you﴾, i.e., destroy you and root you out entirely. ﴿O people, and bring others﴾, i.e., bring into existence at once, in your place, another people from mankind, or other creatures in place of humankind. The meaning is that your being left in your present state of disobedience is only due to the perfection of His independence from your obedience, and to the fact that His will, which is founded on consummate wisdom, is not attached to your annihilation, not because He, glory be to Him and exalted above that by a great exaltation, is incapable of it.

﴿And ever is Allah capable of that﴾, i.e., of destroying you entirely and creating others, ﴿Capable﴾, possessing consummate power. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if you turn away, He will substitute a people other than you; then they will not be like you﴾ [Muhammad: 38] [Muhammad: 38]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿If He wills, He can remove you and bring a new creation﴾ [Ibrahim: 19] ﴿And that is not difficult for Allah﴾ [Ibrahim: 20] [Ibrahim: 19]. In this is an affirmation of His independence and His power, and a warning to whoever disbelieves in Him. One of the early scholars (al-Salaf) said: How insignificant are the servants before Allah when they neglect His command!

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world — with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing.﴾ [4:134]

﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world﴾, like the fighter who fights for the sake of booty. ﴿With Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter﴾, meaning: why would he seek the lesser of the two? Let him seek both, or the nobler of them, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Among the people is one who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world," and he will have no share in the Hereafter﴾ [al-Baqarah: 200]. ﴿And among them is one who says, "Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good, and in the Hereafter that which is good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 201]. ﴿Those will have a share of what they have earned, and Allah is swift in account﴾ [al-Baqarah: 202]. [al-Baqarah: 200–202]. And Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We will increase for him his harvest﴾ [al-Shura: 20] [al-Shura: 20], and the verse; and Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Whoever desires the immediate [world], We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We wish﴾ [al-Isra: 18] [al-Isra: 18], and the verse.

Some of them said: The verse refers to the polytheists of the Arabs, for they used to acknowledge Allah the Exalted as their Creator, but did not acknowledge the Resurrection on the Day of Judgment, and they would draw near to Allah the Exalted so that He would give them some of the good of this world and turn its evil away from them.

﴿And Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing﴾, so nothing hidden is concealed from Him, and He recompenses each according to his intention.

[p-1604]

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more deserving of both. So do not follow [your own] desires, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.﴾ [4:135]

﴿O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice﴾ means: it is required by your faith that you strive hard and exert yourselves in upholding justice and steadfastness, for by it the affairs of both worlds are put in order, which necessitates the reward of both. Among the most demanding forms of this is standing firm in testimony as it should be given. So be ﴿witnesses for Allah﴾, that is, establishers of testimony for the truth, giving it sincerely for the sake of His face, exalted is He. ﴿Even if﴾ the testimony is ﴿against yourselves﴾, then bear witness against them by acknowledging the truth against them and do not conceal it. ﴿Or﴾ [against] ﴿parents﴾, that is, the ascendants, ﴿and relatives﴾, that is, the children, siblings and others. Do not show partiality toward them in it, but bear witness to the truth even if its harm returns upon them, for the truth governs over everyone.

﴿Whether one is rich﴾, that is, the one against whom you testify, ﴿is rich﴾, whose approval is usually sought and whose anger is feared, ﴿or poor﴾, who is generally pitied, or whose situation, through the testimony against him, is feared to lead to his being given what suffices him. ﴿Allah is more deserving of both﴾, that is, than the one testified against, and He knows best what is good for both of them. Had testimony against them not been a benefit to them, He would not have legislated it, for He is more solicitous toward His servants than any solicitous one.

﴿So do not follow [your own] desires lest you not be just﴾, that is, do not pursue the intention of deviating from the command of Allah, which is what sets right your affairs and the affairs of those testified against, if you and they would but consider it.

Ibn Kathir said: That is, let not desire, partisanship and your dislike of people lead you to abandon justice in your affairs. Rather, adhere to justice in every circumstance, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 8].

From this is the saying of (p-1605) ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawaha, when the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him to estimate (khars, i.e., assess the yield of) the produce and crops of the people of Khaybar. They wanted to bribe him so that he would be lenient with them. He said: "By Allah! I have come to you from the most beloved of creation to me, and you are more hateful to me than your counterparts, the monkeys and pigs. Yet my love for him and my hatred for you do not lead me to be unjust to you." They said: "By this the heavens and the earth stand."

﴿And if you distort﴾, that is, you twist your tongues away from testifying as it should be done, ﴿or refuse﴾, that is, refuse it by concealing it, ﴿then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted﴾, so He will recompense you for that. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 283].

* *

Note:

Some exegetes of the Zaydiyyah (a Shi'i school) said: This verse has fruits which are rulings:

The first: the obligation of justice (ʿadl) upon judges and rulers, and that they must not deviate from equity because of something to which souls and heart-desires incline, whether wealth, poverty or kinship. Rather, the lowly and the noble, the near and the distant, must be equal in their sight.

It is related that ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) enforced a legal punishment (hadd) upon a son of his. He was reproached regarding the right of kinship, and he said: "On the Day of Resurrection, you will testify before Allah that your father used to enforce the prescribed punishments upon you."

The second ruling: it is obligatory for the one who owes a right to acknowledge it and not conceal it, based on His saying: ﴿even if against yourselves﴾. The meaning of testimony against oneself is acknowledgment, and this is evident.

It has also been said that the meaning is: even if the testimony is a calamity and harm upon yourselves and your fathers, such as when the testimony is against an unjust ruler.

On this matter there is disagreement among the jurists (fuqaha') when one fears harm short of death: is testimony then obligatory or not? It has been said that it is obligatory, because one does not protect his own property by destroying the property of another.

From the Shafi'iyyah (followers of the Shafi'i school) and the theologians (mutakallimun)—and this is the sound position of the school—it is related that it is not obligatory, because testimony is a command to what is right, and its condition is that it must not lead to what is wrong. Rather, the obligation to give testimony falls away only when there arises a strong presumption of harm to oneself, not by mere apprehension.

Al-Mu'ayyad billah said in "al-Ifadah": The witness must testify even if he fears for his own self and property, because what he fears is merely presumed and perhaps will not occur. This is interpreted as meaning a mere possibility, not that he has come to believe that harm will occur. In this case, testimony remains permissible for him despite his fear for his own self.

He said in "Sharh al-Ibanah": It is permissible if his being killed would be a strengthening of the religion, as in forbidding what is wrong. As for concealing it without an excuse, there is no doubt of his sinfulness. It is also related from Ibn ʿAbbas: that is among the major sins.

The third ruling relates to His saying: ﴿witnesses for Allah﴾, that is, you testify for the sake of Allah's face as He has commanded you. This indicates that taking payment for giving testimony is not permissible, because one has not established it for Allah. The jurists have, however, excepted cases in which they permitted taking payment for giving testimony, among them: when one is summoned to a location, since travel is not obligatory for him; and among them: when another person would testify and the right would be realized through him, in which case his testimony is not binding. End.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 4, verse 136:

(p-1607) The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book which He has sent down to His Messenger and the Book which He sent down before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day has certainly strayed far astray.﴾ [136]

﴿O you who have believed, believe﴾ means: remain firm upon your faith ﴿in Allah and His Messenger and the Book which He sent down to His Messenger﴾ Muhammad ﷺ, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and the Book which He sent down before﴾ upon the messengers, with "Books" in the sense of the scriptures. ﴿And whoever disbelieves in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day has certainly strayed far astray﴾ meaning: he has departed from guidance and has gone far, entirely far, from the right path. As for disbelief in Allah, it is evident. As for disbelief in the angels, it is because they are those brought near to Him. As for disbelief in the books, it is because they are the guides to Him. As for disbelief in the messengers, it is because they are the callers. As for disbelief in the Last Day, it is because in it lies the benefit of establishing it and the harm of abandoning it; so whoever denies it necessarily denies the true benefit and the true harm, and that is the far-reaching misguidance. Then disbelief in the angels is disbelief in the manifestations of His inner reality, disbelief in the books is disbelief in the manifestations of the attribute of His speech, disbelief in the messengers is disbelief in the most complete of His manifestations, and disbelief in the Last Day is disbelief in the permanence of His lordship and His justice.

Then disbelief in the angels calls to belief in the devils, and disbelief in the books of Allah leads to belief in the books of the disbelievers, and disbelief in the messengers leads to blind imitation of the forefathers, and disbelief in the Last Day leads to boldness in committing vices. All of this is far-reaching misguidance, as conveyed by al-Mahayimi.

When He, exalted is He, commanded belief and encouraged it, He explained the corruption of the method of one who disbelieves after believing, so He said:

The discussion of the verse of Allah the Exalted:

﴿Indeed, those who believed and then disbelieved, then believed and then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief - Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a way.﴾ [137]

In the interpretation of this verse there are several opinions:

The first: The intended are those who repeatedly apostatized, and from whom an increase in disbelief and persistence upon it has been known. It is improbable of them that they would produce what would earn them forgiveness and merit divine kindness, namely a sound, firm faith that Allah is pleased with. This is because the hearts of those whose habit this is have become accustomed to disbelief and trained in apostasy, and faith has become the least and lowest thing to them, since it appears to them again and again. The meaning is not that if they were to sincerely believe after repeated apostasy and their repentance were sincere, it would not be accepted from them and they would not be forgiven; for that is accepted, since it is an exertion of effort and exhaustion of capacity. Rather, it is a declaration that it is improbable and strange, and it is a matter that hardly comes to be. Likewise, we see the sinner who repents and then returns, then repents and returns again: it is hardly hoped of him that he remains steadfast, and the likely outcome is that he dies in sin. So it is here as well.

The second: Some said: they are the Jews, who believed in the Torah and in Moses, then disbelieved when they worshipped the calf, then believed after its return to them, then disbelieved in Jesus and the Gospel, then increased in disbelief toward Muhammad ﷺ. It has been objected to this view that those who increased in disbelief toward Muhammad ﷺ were not believers in Moses and then disbelievers in the calf, then believers upon its return, then disbelievers in Jesus; rather, they are either believers in Moses and others, or disbelievers due to their disbelief in Jesus and the Gospel.

The answer: This objection arises only if specific people are meant, those present at the time of the mission. But if a kind and a type is meant, by counting what proceeded from some of them as though it proceeded from all of them, then there is no objection. The intended meaning then is the improbability of their faith, given what has been established from them and from their predecessors.

The third: Others said: the intended are the hypocrites. The first faith is their outward profession of Islam, their disbelief after that is their hypocrisy, and the fact that their inner state is contrary to their outer state. The second faith is that whenever they met a group of Muslims they said, "We are believers." The second disbelief is that they: ﴿when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed we are with you; we are only mocking."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 14].

Their increase in disbelief is their diligence and striving in devising kinds of deception and scheming against the Muslims, while the outward display of faith is sometimes also called faith. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe﴾ [al-Baqarah: 221].

Al-Qaffal, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The purpose is not to state this number, but rather to express their wavering, as He said: ﴿wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those﴾ [al-Nisa: 143]. He said: What indicates this is the saying of Allah the Exalted after this verse: ﴿Give the hypocrites the tidings﴾ [al-Nisa: 138].

The fourth: Some people said: the intended is a group from the People of the Book who sought to cast doubt upon the Muslims, so they would sometimes display faith and sometimes disbelief, as Allah the Exalted informed about them: ﴿Believe in what has been revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end, perhaps they will return﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 72].

And His saying: ﴿then increased in disbelief﴾ means that they reached in this matter the limit of mockery and ridicule toward Islam.

al-Zamakhshari, al-Razi and others transmitted these opinions, and all of them are included in the wording of the verse.

* *

Note:

Concerning the verse there are issues:

The first: In "al-Iklil" it is said: those who say that the repentance of an apostate is accepted three times but not on the fourth time have taken evidence from it.

Some of the Zaydis said in (his exegesis): it indicates that the repentance of an apostate is accepted, because He the Exalted affirmed a faith after a disbelief that was preceded by a faith.

And I say: its indication of this is in the case where the apostasy is not repeated; as for when it is repeated, then no, as is not hidden.

Then he said: And from Ishaq: if he apostatizes for the third time, his repentance is not accepted; this is the narration of al-Sha'bi from Ali, peace be upon him. End of quote.

The Hanabila held that whoever's apostasy is repeated, his repentance is not accepted, as we have already mentioned in Aal 'Imran in His saying: ﴿How will Allah guide a people﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 86] and the verse, and His saying after it: ﴿Indeed those who disbelieved after their belief, then increased in disbelief﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 90]. We mentioned there that this verse is like that verse, and that their apparent meaning supports what Ishaq and Ahmad held. As for the opinions presented here, they are from the interpretation of most scholars who hold that the repentance of an apostate is accepted even if repeated. And in sum: the matter is subtle, and Allah knows best.

The second: It indicates that disbelief admits increase and decrease, so it must be that faith is likewise by text, since they are opposites that are mutually exclusive; when one of them admits variation, the other admits it too. And His saying the Exalted:

The Explanation of His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿Give the hypocrites the good news that there is for them a painful punishment﴾ [138]

﴿Give the hypocrites the good news﴾ is in the manner of mockery (al-tahakkum), ﴿that there is for them a painful punishment﴾, for they believed outwardly and disbelieved inwardly. And what indicates that their faith was accompanied by disbelief is their favouring the side of the disbelievers in affection, since they are:

(p-1611)

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek honour with them? Indeed, all honour belongs to God.﴾ [139]

﴿Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers﴾ means: they take them as helpers, going beyond the friendship of the believers. ﴿Do they seek honour with them?﴾ means: do they seek through their alliance strength and dominance? This is a denunciation of their opinion and a refutation of it, and a demonstration of the failure of their hope. For this reason He gave the reason in His saying: ﴿Indeed, all honour belongs to God﴾, meaning: dominance and strength belong to Him alone. So there is no support for them from the disbelievers, and all victory and success come from God, exalted is He. This is like His saying in another verse: ﴿Honour belongs to God, to His Messenger and to the believers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8].

Ibn Kathir said: The purpose of this is to urge the seeking of honour from the presence of God, turning to His worship, and joining the company of His believing servants, who have support in this world and on the Day when the witnesses will stand.

It is fitting here to mention the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, from Abu Rayhana, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever claims descent from nine disbelieving fathers, seeking through them honour and nobility, he is the tenth of them in the Fire." Ahmad alone narrated it.

This Abu Rayhana is an Azdi, and his name is (Shim'un) with a dotted letter, according to what al-Bukhari said; others said it is with an undotted letter. And God knows best.

* *

Note:

al-Hakim said: The verse indicates the obligation of befriending the believers and the prohibition of befriending the disbelievers. He said: What is prohibited is their friendship in religion only. Al-Mu'ayyad billah, may God sanctify his spirit, mentioned the meaning of this, namely: that you love him for what he is upon. This is evident, and it returns to approval of disbelief and of what one loves on its account.

(p-1612) As for mere association, it is not friendship. The scholars, may God have mercy on them, permitted marriage to a sinful woman, and likewise kindness. God praised those who fed prisoners. Many of them also permitted bequeathing to the People of the Dhimma (protected non-Muslim subjects). Likewise, being grieved by what grieves him in a matter, such as the grief of the Muslims at the victory of Persia over the Romans. Thus [it is stated] in the tafsir of some of the Zaydiyya (a Shi'i school).

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

﴿And He has already sent down to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being rejected and ridiculed, do not sit with them until they enter into a conversation other than that; indeed, you would then be like them. Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers together in Hell, all of them﴾ [140]

﴿And He has already sent down to you in the Book﴾ The exegetes said: The polytheists in Makkah used to sit in their gatherings discussing the Qur'an and mocking it, so Allah the Exalted forbade the Muslims from sitting with them by His saying: ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses, turn away from them until they engage in a conversation other than that﴾ [al-An'am: 68]. This verse is from Surat al-An'am, and it is Meccan. So the Muslims refrained from sitting with them. When they migrated to al-Madinah, they used to sit with the Jews and the hypocrites, and the Jews used to mock the Qur'an, so this verse was revealed: ﴿And He has already sent down to you in the Book﴾, meaning in Surat al-An'am.

﴿that when you hear the verses of Allah being rejected﴾, meaning denied, ﴿and ridiculed, do not sit with them until they enter into a conversation other than that﴾. In it is an indication that what was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ, although addressed to him specifically, is revealed for the entire Ummah, and that the basis of turning away from them is knowledge of their engaging in the verses, and for this reason it is expressed sometimes by seeing and sometimes by hearing; and that the intended turning away is the manifestation of opposition by rising from their gatherings, not merely turning away in the heart or with the face.

﴿indeed, you would then be like them﴾, that is: if you sit with them, it indicates your contentment with disbelief (p-1613) in the verses and their ridicule, so you will be like them in disbelief and in incurring punishment. Thus your gathering with them here is the cause of your gathering in Hell, as He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers together in Hell, all of them﴾, because when they shared with them in disbelief and came together in mocking the verses in this world, Allah gathers them together in the punishment of Hell on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

Note:

Some of the exegetes of the Zaydiyyah said: Know that there is no disagreement on the prohibition of sitting and associating when that gives the impression that the one sitting is content, and there is no disagreement that it is prohibited if one fears being led into temptation, and there is no disagreement that it is permissible to sit in order to rebuke them and repel them.

Al-Hakim said: For this reason scholars attend with the people of misguidance to debate with them, and for them in that is great reward. As for when it is free of what we have mentioned, and does not give the impression of contentment, does not lead to temptation, and does not involve rebuking them, scholars have differed about this. Among them are those who made it obligatory to be like them, based on the apparent meaning of the verse.

Al-Hakim said: It is narrated that some people were seized for drinking alcohol during the time of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, and he ordered that they be given the prescribed punishment. It was said: Among them is a fasting person. So he recited His saying: ﴿So do not sit with them﴾ up to His saying: ﴿indeed, you would then be like them﴾. This is also the apparent meaning of the hadith: "It is not permissible for an eye that sees Allah being disobeyed to blink until it changes and moves on."

Abu Ali and Abu Hashim said: If one disapproves in his heart, he is not obligated to do more than that, and it is permissible for him to sit, meaning when he is unable to forbid with the hand or the tongue, and such forbidding would have no effect.

I say: What they both said contradicts the apparent meaning of the verse, so it carries no weight.

Al-Qadi and al-Hakim said: As for one who has a right in that place, he may remain and not leave, like one who attends funerals where wailing takes place, or banquets, and hears what is reprehensible; it is permissible for him to sit, and rebuking them to the extent possible is obligatory upon him.

(p-1614) It is narrated from al-Hasan: If we were to leave the truth for falsehood, the Sharia would be nullified. He once went out to a funeral where women had come out, and he did not return; but Ibn Sirin returned. End.

I say: Whoever has a right in the place must leave as others do, since leaving does not cause the loss of his right, and the generality of the verse includes him; there is no specification except by a specifier. The matter being analogized upon is other than what we are dealing with, with the disagreement it contains, as he related, and there is no analogy in the presence of a text. Al-Hakim related opinions all of which return to specifying the verse, and there is no basis for them except opinion and speculation, so we have turned away from them.

Abu Ali said: The prohibition of sitting in the gathering is because of the ambiguity it causes; so if one shows disapproval, it is permissible to sit in another place, even if near, and as for when they engage in a conversation other than that, sitting is permissible by the implication of the verse. Then the verse is muhkam (definitive) according to the majority.

It is narrated from al-Kalbi that it was abrogated (mansukh) by His saying: ﴿And there is nothing upon those who fear Allah concerning their account, of anything﴾ [al-An'am: 69]. This is rejected, for part of piety is avoiding the gatherings of those who disbelieve in the verses of Allah and mock them.

Al-Hakim said: The verse indicates that one who is content with the mocking of the Messenger and the religion is a disbeliever, since He, the Exalted, said: ﴿indeed, you would then be like them﴾, and it indicates that contentment with disbelief is disbelief.

Al-Samarqandi said: In this verse is evidence that whoever sits in a gathering of disobedience and does not disapprove of them is equal to them in sin, and he should disapprove of them when they speak of disobedience or act upon it; if he is unable to disapprove of them, he should rise from them so that he is not among the people of this verse.

Ibn Jarir related from al-Dahhak that he said: Every innovator in the religion and every person of bid'ah enters into this verse until the Day of Resurrection.

In "Fath al-Bayan" it says: In this verse, considering the generality of its wording, which is the consideration rather than the specificity of the occasion of revelation, is evidence for avoiding every situation in which its people engage in what implies belittling and mockery (p-1615) of the legislated evidences, as occurs frequently among the captives of taqlid who have replaced the opinions of men for the Book and the Sunnah, and nothing remains in their hands except (the imam of our school said: such-and-such) and (so-and-so among his followers said such-and-such); or when they hear someone deriving a ruling on that matter from a Qur'anic verse or a Prophetic hadith, they mock him, do not give any weight to what he said, and do not care about it at all, thinking that he has brought some monstrous matter and a grave affair, and opposed the school of their imam, whom they have placed in the position of a teacher of the laws, even though the imams to whom these followers of taqlid ascribe themselves are free of their conduct, for they have explicitly stated in their writings the prohibition of taking them as authorities. End.

In "al-Iklil": Ibn al-Firs said: Some scholars have used this verse as evidence for the obligation of avoiding the people of sins and desires. In this verse is a basis for what authors do of referring to what was mentioned in another place and drawing attention to it. End.

And His exalted saying:

Commentary on the words of the Exalted: 

﴿Those who wait [in suspense] over you. If you achieve a victory from Allah, they say, "Were we not with you?" And if the disbelievers have a share [of victory], they say, "Did we not gain mastery over you and protect you from the believers?" But Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection. And never will Allah give the disbelievers over the believers a way.﴾ [4:141]

﴿Those who wait [in suspense] over you﴾ is either a substitute (badal) for ﴿those who take [the disbelievers as allies]﴾ [4:139], or a qualifier (sifah) of "the hypocrites," meaning: they wait over you to see what new victory or defeat will befall you.

﴿If you achieve a victory from Allah﴾, that is, support, aid, triumph and spoils, ﴿they say [to you]: "Were we not with you?"﴾, that is, supporting you, so we have a part in your victory, and therefore we should have a share in your spoils. ﴿And if the disbelievers have a share﴾, that is, a turn of fortune against the believers at some times, as happened on the Day of Uhud, for the messengers are tested and then the final outcome is theirs. ﴿They say﴾, that is, the disbelievers, [addressing the hypocrites] in friendliness towards them and flattery of them, so that they may gain favour with them and be safe from their scheming, [and] because of the weakness of their faith: ﴿Did we not gain mastery over you﴾, that is, did we not overcome you and gain the power to kill and capture you, and then spare you? ﴿And protect you from the believers﴾ by discouraging them from you and by slackening in supporting them, until you prevailed over them; otherwise you would have been prey to calamities. The calling of the Muslims' victory "a victory" (fath) and of the disbelievers' portion "a share" (naṣīb) is to magnify the standing of the Muslims and belittle the lot of the disbelievers.

Al-Nasafi (in al-Intisaf) said: This is one of the fine subtleties of the Qur'an, for what happened to the Muslims was the uprooting of the disbelievers' stronghold, the seizing of their lands, homes and wealth, and a land never trodden [by them]. As for what happened to the disbelievers, it was [mere] dominance and power, whose significance does not reach the level of being called a victory. Thus the distinction between them also accords with reality, and Allah knows best.

Some of the Zaydiyyah said: The verse indicates the obligation to love the support of the believers, to dislike that the hand [of power] be over them, and the prohibition of forsaking them. It also indicates that the hypocrite has no share, because the verse alludes to their seeking [a share] when they were denied, saying: "Were we not with you?" Then he said: It is permissible to win over the hypocrites with spoils, as the Messenger ﷺ did on the day of Hunayn, until he gave one of them a hundred camels, while a Muslim received a sheep or a camel.

﴿But Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection﴾, that is, a judgment befitting the standing of each of you in reward and punishment. That is, the hypocrites should not be deceived by having their blood spared in this world for uttering the testimony, for this is due to a wisdom of His, Exalted is He; on the Day of Resurrection their outward appearance will not benefit them.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And never will Allah give the disbelievers over the believers a way﴾ is a refutation of the hypocrites in what they hoped for, expected and awaited of the decline of the believers' dominance, and in their course of flattering the disbelievers out of fear for themselves from them, should the disbelievers prevail over the believers and utterly destroy them, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿So you see those in whose hearts is disease hastening toward them﴾ [5:52] up to His saying: ﴿regretful﴾ [5:52]. That is, Allah will not empower the disbelievers over the believers so as to utterly root them out, even if they attain a victory for a time, as Ibn Kathir stated.

This interpretation takes into account the preceding and following context of the verse, and that the context concerns the hypocrites, and it is good. Close to it is what is in the tafsir of Ibn ʿAbbas, which takes "the disbelievers" to mean the Jews of Medina. Whoever keeps to its general sense says: the meaning of "a way" (sabil) is proof (ḥujjah), and it is called "a way" because it leads to dominance; or the meaning is: as long as the believers act by the truth, do not accept falsehood, and do not abandon forbidding evil, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Whatever affliction befalls you is for what your own hands have earned﴾ [42:30]. He said: Thus it is not meant that the disbelievers may never be granted a turn of fortune.

* *

Note:

This verse may be cited as evidence that a disbeliever may not marry a believing woman, that he has no guardianship (wilayah) over a believing woman in marriage or travel, and that a disbeliever may not intercede for a believer. This is the view of al-Hadi in "al-Ahkam," al-Nafs al-Zakiyyah, and al-Radi bi-Llah, and the like of it is reported from al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi and Ahmad.

Al-Mu'ayyad bi-Llah, the Hanafis and the Shafi'is said, in "al-Muntakhab": he has the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah), by the generality of the evidences for pre-emption, and by analogy with returning a defective item bought from a Muslim.

It may be cited as evidence that when an apostate (murtadd) leaves Islam, his Muslim wife is separated from him. The disagreement is whether this happens by the apostasy itself, as the Hanafis say, or upon the completion of the waiting period ('iddah), as al-Mu'ayyad bi-Llah and the Shafi'is say? Likewise, the sale of a Muslim slave to a dhimmi: the Hanafis permit it, while al-Mu'ayyad and the Shafi'is prohibit it; but according to the first view he is to be compelled to sell him, so that he does not employ him. It is said: there is consensus on the prohibition of selling a Muslim slave-woman to a disbeliever.

There is no disagreement that the verse is specified (takhsis) by matters including: a debt owed by a Muslim to a disbeliever is valid, and a believer spends on his disbelieving parents, and the like. When a general ruling is specified, the usulis have differed: does its indication remain literal (haqiqah) for what remains, or figurative (majaz)? End of quotation.

Some exegetes added: a disbeliever does not inherit from a Muslim, and a Muslim is not executed for killing a dhimmi.

(p-١٦١٨) The discussion on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

﴿Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them. And when they stand up for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to the people and not remembering Allah except a little.﴾ [142]

﴿Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them﴾ means: they do what the deceiver does, by displaying faith and concealing disbelief. Allah does to them what the dominant party does in deception: He leaves them with their lives and property protected in this world, and prepares for them the lowest level of the Fire in the Hereafter.

﴿And when they stand up for prayer﴾ means: when they come to it. ﴿They stand lazily﴾ means: reluctantly, like one compelled to perform the act.

Ibn Kathir said: This is the description of the hypocrites regarding the most noble, most excellent and best of deeds, which is prayer. When they stand up for it, they stand with laziness towards it, because they have no intention in it, no faith in it, and no fear (of Allah) through it, and they do not understand its meaning.

As Ibn Mardawayh narrated from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: It is disliked for a man to stand up for prayer while he is lazy; rather, he should stand up for it with a cheerful face, great eagerness and great joy, for he is conversing with Allah, and Allah is facing him, forgiving him and answering him when he calls upon Him. Then he recited this verse: ﴿And when they stand up for prayer, they stand lazily﴾. End quote.

Al-Hakim said: The verse indicates that one of the signs of the hypocrite is laziness in prayer. Laziness (kasal) is holding back from something because of its difficulty. This verse is about the outward appearance of them, as He said: ﴿And they do not come to prayer except while they are lazy﴾ [al-Tawbah: 54].

Then He mentioned the description of their corrupt inner states: ﴿showing off to the people﴾, meaning: they intend by their prayer to show off and seek fame, so that they may be thought to be believers, not out of sincerity or obedience to the command of Allah. For this reason they often neglect the prayers in which they are not seen, generally, such as the ʿIshāʾ prayer at the time of darkness (ʿatamah) and the Fajr prayer at the time of the dim light of dawn (ghalas). As is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs (Bukhari and Muslim), the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The heaviest prayers upon the hypocrites are ʿIshāʾ and Fajr. If they knew what is in them, they would come to them even crawling. I had certainly intended to order the prayer to be established, then order a man to lead the people in prayer, then set off with men carrying bundles of firewood to a people who do not attend the prayer, and burn their houses over them with fire." And in another narration: "By Him in Whose hand is my soul, if one of them knew that he would find a fat bone or two good meaty morsels, he would attend the ʿIshāʾ prayer. Were it not for the women and children in the houses, I would have burned their houses over them."

Al-Hafiz and Abu Yaʿla narrated from ʿAbd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever performs the prayer well where people see him, and performs it badly where he is alone — that is a contempt by which he has belittled his Lord, mighty and majestic."

As for His words: ﴿and not remembering Allah except a little﴾, there are several interpretations concerning it:

The first: its meaning is "and they do not pray except a little," because they only pray for show as long as there is someone watching them; when they are alone with themselves, they do not pray. The interpretation of "remembrance" (dhikr) as "prayer" has been narrated in other verses from the early generations (al-salaf).

The second: "and they do not remember Allah in their prayer except a little," because they are not humble and do not know what they are saying; rather, in their prayer they are heedless and inattentive.

Imam Malik narrated from al-ʿAlaʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "That is the prayer of the hypocrite, that is the prayer of the hypocrite, that is the prayer of the hypocrite: he sits watching the sun until, when it is between the two horns of the Shaytan, he rises and pecks four times, not remembering Allah in it except a little." Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also narrated it likewise.

The third: its meaning is: "and they do not remember Allah with glorification (tahlil) and exaltation (tasbih) except a remembrance that is rare and infrequent," according to the meaning of remembrance that is understood from it and applies to it. Among the signs of hypocrisy is spending times entirely in worldly talk, and little remembrance of Him, exalted is He, through praise, glorification or exaltation, just as one of the attributes of the believers is remembering Allah, exalted is He, frequently.

The Chapter on the Interpretation of His Words, may He be exalted:

﴿Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those; and whomever Allah leaves astray, you will not find for him a way.﴾ [143]

﴿Wavering between that﴾: it is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from the subject of (yurā'ūna) ("they show off"), or it is in the accusative on the basis of censure (dhamm). (Dhālika) ("that") is a demonstrative referring to faith and disbelief, which are understood from the context, or to (the believers and the disbelievers), in which case what follows it is an explanation of it. That is: they are vacillating between the two, bewildered, whom Satan and desire have tossed back and forth. The real meaning of (mudhabdhab) is one who is repelled from both sides, that is, is driven off and pushed away, so that he is not settled on one side. However, the (dhabdhaba) form contains a repetition that the (dhabb) form does not have, as if the meaning is: whenever he inclines toward one side, he is repelled from it.

﴿Belonging neither to these nor to those﴾: that is, neither joined with the believers nor with the disbelievers. They are neither sincere believers nor openly polytheists. Mujahid said: ﴿Neither to these﴾ means the companions of Muhammad ﷺ, and ﴿nor to those﴾ means the Jews.

﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray﴾ from His religion and His proof, ﴿you will not find for him a way﴾: that is, a path to what is right and to guidance.

Al-Shaykhan narrated, from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "The likeness of the hypocrite is that of a goat wandering between two flocks: it goes toward this one at one time, and toward that one at another time." (al-ā'irah means the bewildered, wavering one, not knowing which of the two flocks to follow.)

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 4, Verse 144:**

The interpretation of His, the Exalted, statement:

﴿O you who have believed, do not take disbelievers as allies (awliya') instead of believers. Do you wish to give Allah a clear case against yourselves?﴾ [144]

﴿O you who have believed, do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers. Do you wish to give Allah a clear case against yourselves?﴾ This is a prohibition against taking the disbelievers as allies (muwalat), meaning keeping their company, befriending them, advising them, confiding affection to them, and disclosing the inner affairs of the believers to them, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Let not the believers take disbelievers as allies instead of believers. Whoever does that has nothing with Allah, except when you fear a danger from them. And Allah warns you of Himself﴾ [Al 'Imran: 28]. That is, He warns you of His punishment if you violate His prohibition. For this reason He said here: ﴿Do you wish to give Allah a clear case against yourselves?﴾, that is, a proof against you for your punishment because of your allegiance to them. The verse indicates the prohibition of believers' allegiance to disbelievers.

Al-Hakim said: It is allegiance in religion and support in it, not opposition or kindness.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It is reported from Sa'sa'a ibn Suhan that he said to a nephew of his: "Be sincere to the believer, and be courteous to the disbeliever and the wicked, for the wicked will be content with you if you have good character, and it is necessary for you to be sincere to the believer."

Abu al-Su'ud said: Directing the denial toward the wish rather than toward its object, by saying "Do you make...", etc., serves to intensify the denial of that and to magnify its gravity by showing that it is something a sensible person would not even wish for, let alone carry out himself, as in His, the Mighty and Majestic, statement: ﴿Or do you wish to question your Messenger?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 108].

(p-1622) A subtle point:

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Every sultan (authority) in the Qur'an is a proof." Similarly said others among the leading Successors (tabi'un).
