When they saw that this was consistent with the principle they established concerning the attributes, and saw that reconciling the prophetic transmitted texts with rational analogy can only be done by making the Qur'an a meaning subsisting in the very Essence of God, exalted is He, like the other attributes, as the earlier ones had made it one of the created made things, and not eternal like the other attributes, and saw that it is nothing but either created or eternal, then the affirmation of a third category subsisting in God entails the indwelling of originated events in His essence, which is a proof of the originatedness of the subject, and it would be invalidated by the proof of the world's createdness. Then they saw that it is not permissible for it to be many meanings; rather, it is either one meaning according to one group, or four meanings according to another group. On this they committed themselves to the position that the true reality of speech is the meaning subsisting in the soul, and that the letters and sounds are not the true reality of speech, but indicate it, so they are called by its name either metaphorically, according to one group, or literally by way of homonymy (*ishtirak*), according to another group, or metaphorically when applied to the speech of God and literally when applied to other than Him, according to another group.

The earlier ones and some who follow their path also disagreed with them and said: "There is no true reality of speech except the letters and sounds. Beyond that there is no meaning except knowledge and its type, or will and its type." So the dispute arose between the two groups. These people claimed that the command, the prohibition and the report are relational attributes of speech, not types or divisions of it, and that the speech of God is one meaning, which if expressed in Arabic is the Qur'an, in Hebrew is the Torah, and in Syriac is the Gospel.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 4, verse 164 (part 5 of 6):

Most people said to them: "This is known to be false by necessity (bi-l-darurah), as the earlier scholars said: He created speech in the air, and so He became one who speaks through it. And the speaker is whoever originates speech, even if it is in a substance other than His own essence." Most people said to them: "This is known to be false by necessity."

The majority of all the sects said: The word "speech" (kalam) is a name for both the wording (lafz) and the meaning (ma'na) together, just as the word "human being" (insan), meaning the one who speaks, is a name for both the spirit (ruh) and the body (jism) together. When the word is applied to only one of them, this is by means of a qarinah (contextual indicator). The meanings of speech are varied and are not limited to knowledge and will, just as its wordings are varied. Although the meanings are closer to unity and collectivity, the wordings are closer to plurality and division. These people held that the letters of the Qur'an are created, though in their view the meaning, which is the speech of God, is not created.

They distinguished between the Book of God and the speech of God. They said: "The Book of God is the letters, and it is created. The speech of God is its meaning, and it is uncreated." These people and the earlier ones agree on the creation of the Qur'an, which the earlier ones said is created. These people differed over where these letters were created. Were they created in the air, or in the self (nafs) of Jibril, or is it that Jibril originated them, or Muhammad?!

As for the bulk of the Community (ummah), the people of hadith, of fiqh and of tasawwuf, they hold to what the messengers brought, and to what was transmitted from them of books and of "remnants of knowledge" (al-atharah min al-'ilm). They are the ones who follow the Message in pure following, without mixing it with what contradicts it from the doctrine of the Sabians. That doctrine is that the whole Qur'an is the speech of God. They do not make part of it the speech of God and part of it not the speech of God.

The Qur'an is the Qur'an that Muslims know to be the Qur'an, its letters and its meanings. The command (al-amr) and the prohibition (al-nahy) are the wording and the meaning together. For this reason, the jurists who wrote on the foundations of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh) from all the sects, the Hanafis, the Malikis, the Shafi'is and the Hanbalis, when they did not depart from the schools of the imams and the jurists, when they spoke about command and prohibition, mentioned this and opposed those who said that the command is the bare meaning alone.

The people of the prophetic transmission (ahl al-athar al-nabawiyyah), the people of the Sunnah and hadith, and the general body of Muslims who are the majority of the People of the Qiblah, know that His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾ [al-Baqarah: 1] ﴿That is the Book, there is no doubt in it, a guidance for the God-fearing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 2] [al-Baqarah: 1-2], and similar verses, is the speech of God and not the speech of another. The speech of God is what He spoke, not what He created in another and what He did not Himself speak.

(Taqi al-Din was also asked): "What do the noble scholars, the masters, the imams of religion, may God be pleased with them all, say about one who says: 'Speech is other than the speaker, and utterance is other than the utterer, and the Qur'an, the recited and the reciter, each of them has a meaning'? Explain this to us with a sufficient explanation so that it reaches the mind of the clever and the dull. May God reward you with His bounty."

(He answered, may God have mercy on him): All praise is due to God. As for one who says that speech is other than the speaker, and utterance is other than the utterer, and he means that it is separate from Him and detached from Him, this is error and misguidance. This is the view of those who say the Qur'an is created, for they claim that God has no attribute subsisting in Him at all, neither the Qur'an nor anything else. They deceive people by their saying: "Knowledge is other than the knower, power is other than the one who has power, and speech is other than the speaker."

Then they say: "Whatever is other than God is created." This is deception on their part. The word "other" (al-ghayr) is used for what can be separated from and detached from another. On this understanding it is not permissible to say: "The knowledge of God is other than Him, or His speech is other than Him," nor to say that one of ten is other than them, and similar examples.

The word "other" may also be used for what is not the same as the other thing. On this understanding the attribute is other than the thing it qualifies. But in this sense, what is other than the essence (dhat) of God, the essence qualified by His attributes, is not created, because His attributes are not the essence itself, but subsist in the essence. God, glorified and exalted is He, is the sacred essence qualified by the attributes of His perfection. The name is not the name of an essence that has no attributes. Rather it is impossible for an essence without attributes to exist. The correct formulation in such matters is to say: speech is an attribute of the speaker, and utterance is an attribute of the utterer. The speech of God is not separate from Him. Rather He made it heard to Jibril and sent it down with it upon Muhammad ﷺ, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And those to whom We have given the Book know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth﴾ [al-An'am: 114]. It is not permissible to say that the speech of God has departed from His essence and passed to another. Rather it is said, as the early scholars (al-salaf) said: It is the speech of God, uncreated; from Him it originated, and to Him it returns.

Their saying "from Him it originated" is a rebuttal of one who says: "It is created in some bodies, and from that created thing it began." They make clear that God is the one who speaks it, and from Him it originated, not from some of the created things.

"And to Him it returns" means that no verse of it remains in the breasts (of men) and no letter in the copies (of the Qur'an).

As for the Qur'an, it is the speech of God. Whoever says that the Qur'an, which is the speech of God, is other than God, his error and deception are like the error of one who says that speech is other than the speaker.

Likewise, whoever says that God has a recited (maqru') that is other than the Qur'an by which He spoke, his error is manifest.

Likewise, whoever says: The Qur'an which Muslims recite is other than the recited thing which Muslims recite, he has erred. But if he means by "Qur'an" the verbal noun of "qara'a yaqra'u qira'atan wa-qur'anan" and says: "I meant the recitation other than the recited thing," then the word "recitation" (qira'ah) is ambiguous. "Recitation" may mean the Qur'an, and it may mean the verbal noun. Whoever takes "recitation" to mean the verbal noun, and says: "The reciter is other than the recited," is like one who makes the act of speaking that he performed other than the speech which he utters. If he means by "other" that it is not identical with it, then he has spoken truly. The speech that a person speaks includes an action like movement, and includes what accompanies the action of letters (p-1746) and meanings. For this reason, "saying" (qawl) is sometimes set against "action" (fi'l), and sometimes is a part of it.

The first case is as one says: "Faith is saying and action." And from it is His Prophet's saying ﷺ: "God has overlooked for my community what their souls whisper or speak of (aw haddathat) so long as they do not act upon it or speak of it."

And from it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and righteous action raises it﴾ [Fatir: 10]. And from it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You are not engaged in any affair, nor recite any part of the Qur'an, nor do any deed﴾ [Yunus: 61] [Yunus: 61]. And similar examples, in which saying and action are distinguished.

As for the inclusion of saying within action, it is as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ [al-Hijr: 92] ﴿about what they used to do﴾ [al-Hijr: 93] [al-Hijr: 92-93]. They explained it as: "There is no god but God."

When he was asked: "Which deed is best?" he said: "Faith in God." (p-1747) Along with his saying: "Faith has seventy-some branches, and modesty is a branch of faith. The best and highest of them is the saying 'There is no god but God,' and the lowest is removing harm from the road." There are many similar examples.

It has been disputed concerning one who swears that he will not do a deed, if he speaks a saying such as recitation, whether he breaks his oath. There are two opinions in the school of Ahmad and others, based on this. These expressions which contain ambiguity and confusion, if their meanings are not specified, dispute and confusion will arise about them. And God, glorified and exalted is He, knows best.

The words of Taqi al-Din, may God have mercy on him, end here.

'Abd Allah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said in his book "al-Radd 'ala al-Jahmiyyah" (The Refutation of the Jahmiyyah): I asked my father about a people who say, when God spoke to Musa: "He did not speak with a voice." My father said: "Rather, He spoke, exalted is His praise, with a voice. These are the hadiths we transmit as they came."

My father said: The hadith of Ibn Mas'ud: "When God, exalted is He, speaks, there is heard a sound (sawt) (p-1748) like the dragging of a chain over rock." He said: The Jahmiyyah deny this, and these are unbelievers who want to deceive people. Then he said: Al-Muharibi narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, from 'Ubayd Allah, who said: "When God, blessed and exalted is He, speaks by revelation, the people of heaven hear His voice and fall down in prostration."

Al-Safarini said in his "Sharh al-'Aqidah": More than forty hadiths have been transmitted affirming the letter and the voice. Imam Ahmad recorded most of them and relied upon them.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar also recorded them in his "Sharh al-Bukhari," and al-Bukhari and other imams of hadith relied upon them, to establish that the Real, glorified is He, speaks with a letter and a voice. They affirmed this principle, held it as a belief, and depended upon it, declaring God free of what does not befit His majesty, of the doubts of createdness and the marks of deficiency, just as they said about all the other attributes. They relied upon what was authentically established for them from the Lawgiver, the infallible in his sayings, who does not speak from desire, ﷺ.

Imam al-Wasiti, son of the Shaykh of the Two Sanctuaries, the Shafi'i, said in his "'Aqidah": I was for a time bewildered about three questions: the question of the attributes, the question of "above" (al-fawqiyyah), and the question of the letter and the voice in the Glorious Qur'an. I was bewildered by the differing opinions found in the books of the scholars of the age concerning all of that: whether it is interpretation (ta'wil) and distortion (tahrif) of the attributes, or leaving them as they are and abstaining from them (imrar wa-al-wuquf), or affirming them without interpretation, without denial, without likening and without comparing. I found the texts in the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger speaking clearly and explaining the realities of these attributes, and likewise regarding the affirmation of exaltedness and being above, and likewise regarding the letter and the voice. Then I found the later theologians (mutakallimun) in their books, some of whom interpreted "istiwa'" (settling) as domination and conquest, and interpreted (p-1749) "nuzul" (descent) as the descent of command, and interpreted the two hands as the two blessings and the two powers, and interpreted the foot as "a foot of truthfulness with their Lord," and similar things.

Then I found them, despite that, making the speech of God a meaning subsisting in the essence, without letter or voice, and making these letters an expression of that subsisting meaning.

Among those who held these opinions, or some of them, are people who have a high place in my breast, like some of the Ash'ari Shafi'i jurists. For I am on the school of al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, and I know the obligations of my religion and its rulings, and I find such noble men holding to these opinions. They are my teachers, and I have complete trust in them because of their knowledge and their virtue. Yet even so, I find in my heart discomfort (hazazat) from these interpretations, which my heart does not find reassuring. I find darkness and gloom from them, I find tightness of chest and lack of expansion accompanying them. So I was like one bewildered and disturbed in his bewilderment, restless in his heart as it turns and changes. I used to fear affirming without qualification the exaltedness, the settling and the descent, for fear of limitation and likening.

Yet when I examine the texts that came in the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger, I find them texts that point to the realities of these meanings. I find the Messenger ﷺ has stated them explicitly, informing about his Lord and describing Him with them. Then I find nothing following those texts that interprets them as these jurist-theologians interpreted them.

Then he said: Those who interpreted what they interpreted, did so because they understood about the attributes of the Lord only what suits created beings. For that reason they distorted the words from their places, and nullified what the Real described Himself with. Had they known that these attributes are all affirmed for Him as befits His majesty and greatness, not as we understand the attributes of created beings, they would have been spared from likening and from interpretation that leads to nullification.

Then he said: The question of the letter and the voice is pursued in this same way. God, exalted is He, has spoken the Glorious Qur'an with all its letters. He said, exalted is He: ﴿Sad, by the Qur'an, full of admonition﴾ [Sad: 1]? Rather: ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim-Sad﴾ [al-A'raf: 1] [al-A'raf: 1], and He said: ﴿Qaf, by the Glorious Qur'an﴾ [Qaf: 1] [Qaf: 1]. Likewise (p-1750) it came in the hadith: "He will call out on the Day of Resurrection with a voice that he who is far away hears just as he who is near hears."

In the hadith: "I do not say that Alif-Lam-Mim (Alif-Lam-Mim) is one letter, but Alif is a letter, Lam is a letter, and Mim is a letter."

These people understood nothing of the speech of God except what they understood of the speech of created beings. They said: "If we affirm that speech consists of letters, this leads to affirming organs and the uvula (lahawat), and likewise if we affirm sound, this leads to the throat and the larynx (hanjara)." So they stumbled in this matter just as they stumbled regarding the attributes mentioned earlier.

The correct position is that God Most High spoke with letters in a manner befitting His majesty and greatness, for He is Able (qadir), and the Able does not need organs or uvulae. Likewise, He has a sound befitting Him that is heard, and that holy sound does not depend on the throat or the larynx. So the speech of God is as befits Him, and His sound is as befits Him. We do not negate letters and sound from His speech, glorified is He, on the grounds that they require organs and uvulae in our case, for in the presence of the Truth they do not require that. This is a matter that opens the breast, and by it a person is relieved of forced interpretation and artificial effort by saying: "This is an expression for that."

If it is said: "Is this which the reader recites the very recitation of God and the very speech of God Himself?" We say: No. Rather, the reader conveys the speech of God, and speech is attributed only to the one who originated it, not to the one who conveys it as a transmitter.

The reader's utterance outside the Qur'an is created, but in the Qur'an the conveying utterance is not distinguished from the speech being conveyed. For this reason the early scholars (al-salaf) forbade saying "My utterance of the Qur'an is created," because it cannot be distinguished, just as they forbade saying "My utterance of the Qur'an is uncreated," for the servant's utterance outside recitation is created, and in recitation it is left unspecified, so that discussion of this does not lead to the claim that the Qur'an is created. What the early scholars commanded silence about, silence about it is obligatory. And God is the Granter of success and the Helper.
